spoke_nodes.label: Gene
spoke_nodes.identifier_scheme: NCBI Gene ID / Entrez Gene ID, stored as a BARE INTEGER (Neo4j numeric type), not a CURIE. Concrete examples: TP53 -> 7157, BRCA1 -> 672, EGFR -> 1956, IL6 -> 3569, MTHFR -> 4524, A1BG -> 1. Ranges span from 1 up to large modern Entrez IDs (e.g. 133039968 for the readthrough locus POC1B-DUSP6, 124904311 for LINC01897). No prefix; to build a CURIE you must prepend 'NCBIGene:'. A separate n.ensembl property holds the Ensembl gene accession (e.g. ENSG00000141510 for TP53).
spoke_nodes.name_property: n.name holds the official HGNC gene SYMBOL (short uppercase symbol), e.g. 'TP53', 'BRCA1', 'EGFR', 'IL6', 'FAM90A3', 'LINC01897', and miRNA gene loci like 'MIR6731', 'MIR5583-2'. It is the approved symbol, NOT the full descriptive name. The full name lives in n.description (e.g. 'tumor protein p53', 'epidermal growth factor receptor').
spoke_nodes.synonyms: n.synonyms is a LIST of alias gene symbols and is populated for most protein-coding genes (e.g. TP53 -> ['BCC7','BMFS5','LFS1','P53','TRP53']; EGFR -> ['ERBB','ERBB1','ERRP','HER1','NISBD2','PIG61','mENA']; BRCA1 -> ['BRCAI','BRCC1','BROVCA1','FANCS','IRIS','PNCA4','PPP1R53','PSCP','RNF53']). It can be EMPTY ([]) for some genes (observed empty for MTHFR). Values are alias symbols, not full phrases; case varies (mostly uppercase, occasional mixed like 'mENA').
spoke_nodes.biookf_mapping: Maps to BioOKF type 'Gene' (subtype protein_coding / ncRNA / miRNA). Per SCHEMA.md typing cheatsheet (line 74): 'a gene / locus / ncRNA-miRNA gene (heritable unit)' -> type Gene, xref namespaces HGNC, NCBIGene, ENSEMBL. This is a 1:1, unambiguous mapping — SPOKE Gene is exactly the BioOKF Gene (heritable locus). CAUTION on the boundary (SCHEMA.md line 131): the heritable locus is Gene, but a specific transcript/RNA species (mRNA/miRNA transcript) is a BioOKF Molecule (subtype rna). SPOKE splits this the same way: the MIR* gene loci live in the Gene label (heritable unit -> BioOKF Gene) while their mature miRNA products live in the separate MiRNA label (which maps to BioOKF Molecule; see MiRNA). SPOKE's Protein label (not covered here) is where the encoded protein Molecule lives.
spoke_nodes.matching_notes: PRIMARY strategy: match a BioOKF Gene node by its identifier/symbol against SPOKE Gene n.name (exact, case-sensitive uppercase HGNC symbol). If the BioOKF node carries an NCBIGene xref, match the bare integer against n.identifier directly (strongest, unambiguous key). If it carries an ENSEMBL xref, match n.ensembl (ENSG...). FALLBACK: if the exact symbol misses, search n.synonyms (list of alias symbols) for the query symbol — do this case-insensitively but be aware most aliases are uppercase and a few are mixed-case (e.g. 'mENA'). NORMALIZATION: symbols are alphanumeric with hyphens (LINC01897, POC1B-DUSP6, MIR5583-2); do not strip hyphens (they are meaningful). Do NOT lowercase for the primary symbol match. PITFALLS: (1) Do not confuse a full descriptive name with the symbol — 'tumor protein p53' is in n.description, not n.name; match names/symbols, not descriptions. (2) An alias symbol can be shared across genes (e.g. 'HGF' appears as an IL6 synonym) so synonym matches are ambiguous — prefer identifier or exact name. (3) Do NOT match a BioOKF Molecule(subtype rna, a transcript) or a mature miRNA to this label; those belong to SPOKE MiRNA/Protein. (4) SPOKE Gene is human-only (Entrez human + miRBase human loci); do not match microbial gene names here — those live in PanGene.

spoke_nodes.label: PanGene
spoke_nodes.identifier_scheme: UniProt pan-genome / cross-organism gene NAME token (a gene-name cluster label from UniProt), stored as a short STRING, not a stable CURIE/accession. Concrete examples: 'yqjB2', 'ybeK_3', 'ndiA-2', 'fur3', 'rhs1', 'spaS', 'tfdK', 'bfr3'. These are predominantly bacterial/microbial gene-name symbols (lowercase-initial, often with numeric or _N disambiguation suffixes). A large fraction are also bare numeric or very short tokens ('08','10','11E','1566','0519'). There is NO namespace prefix and NO integer NCBI ID — the identifier IS the gene-name string. Not resolvable as a public accession on its own.
spoke_nodes.name_property: NONE. PanGene nodes have NO n.name property (keys are only identifier + sources). n.name serializes to null. The identifier string itself is the only human-readable label.
spoke_nodes.synonyms: NONE. No synonyms/aliases/xrefs property exists on PanGene (property_keys = ['sources','identifier'] only). n.synonyms is null.

spoke_nodes.biookf_mapping: Maps to BioOKF type 'Gene' (subtype protein_coding, but MICROBIAL / pan-genome scope). Per SCHEMA.md line 74, a gene/locus (heritable unit) -> Gene. HOWEVER this is a weak/edge mapping: PanGene is a UniProt gene-NAME cluster spanning many bacterial genomes rather than a single heritable locus with a stable NCBIGene/ENSEMBL id, so it behaves more like a cross-organism gene-name grouping. If the BioOKF corpus is human-centric, most PanGene nodes will have NO BioOKF counterpart. Its sole edge ENCODES_PGeP connects to SPOKE Protein (BioOKF Molecule, subtype protein), all microbial (organism suffixes _BACTU, _SALET; zero _HUMAN observed). Do not map PanGene to MolecularClass despite its grouping flavor — it is still a gene-name unit, not a curated gene set.
spoke_nodes.matching_notes: LOW-PRIORITY / rarely matchable label for a human-focused BioOKF. Only attempt if the BioOKF node is explicitly a microbial/bacterial gene named by symbol. STRATEGY: match the BioOKF gene symbol against PanGene n.identifier as a STRING (there is no n.name and no synonyms to fall back on). NORMALIZATION: identifiers are case-sensitive microbial gene names (lowercase-initial + suffix, e.g. 'fur3','yqjB2') — preserve case and suffixes exactly; a plain 'fur' will not match 'fur3'. PITFALLS: (1) HIGH false-match risk — bare-number and 2-6 char tokens ('08','10','11E','1566') will collide with almost anything; never match on short/numeric identifiers without organism corroboration. (2) Do NOT confuse with human Gene: PanGene is microbial-only (all encoded proteins carry non-human organism suffixes; no _HUMAN found), has no NCBIGene integer id, no chromosome, no ensembl, no synonyms — if the BioOKF node has an NCBIGene/HGNC/ENSEMBL xref it belongs in Gene, not PanGene. (3) There is no reliable programmatic disambiguation between two microbial genes sharing a name-cluster; treat PanGene matches as ambiguous by default.

spoke_nodes.label: MiRNA
spoke_nodes.identifier_scheme: Mature human microRNA NAME in miRBase nomenclature, stored as a STRING. Format: 'hsa-' (Homo sapiens) + miR/let family + number + arm suffix (-3p/-5p). Concrete examples: 'hsa-miR-6731-3p', 'hsa-miR-5583-5p', 'hsa-miR-3677-5p', 'hsa-miR-8069', 'hsa-let-7a-5p', 'hsa-let-7b-3p'. A SEPARATE property n.accession holds the stable miRBase mature accession (MIMAT format): e.g. hsa-miR-6731-3p -> MIMAT0027364, hsa-let-7a-5p -> MIMAT0000062. So the resolvable stable ID is n.accession (MIMAT...), while n.identifier is the human-readable miRBase name. All observed entries are human (hsa-).
spoke_nodes.name_property: NONE as a distinct field. MiRNA nodes have NO n.name property (keys = identifier, accession, sources). n.name serializes to null. The n.identifier string (the miRBase mature name, e.g. 'hsa-miR-6731-3p') serves as the de facto name.
spoke_nodes.synonyms: NONE. No synonyms/aliases property on MiRNA (property_keys = ['identifier','accession','sources']). n.synonyms is null. The only alternate identifier is n.accession (the MIMAT miRBase accession), which functions as a cross-reference rather than a synonym list.
spoke_nodes.biookf_mapping: Maps to BioOKF type 'Molecule' (subtype rna / miRNA — the mature RNA SPECIES), NOT to BioOKF Gene. Rationale from SCHEMA.md: the typing cheatsheet line 75 lists 'RNA species (mRNA/miRNA/lncRNA)' explicitly under Molecule (subtype rna), xref namespace RNACENTRAL; and the Gene-vs-Molecule boundary test (line 131) states 'heritable locus = Gene; a specific transcript = Molecule (subtype: rna)'. SPOKE encodes this exact split: the heritable miRNA GENE locus (e.g. 'MIR6731', NCBIGene 102465437) lives in the SPOKE Gene label (-> BioOKF Gene), while the mature miRNA product lives here in SPOKE MiRNA (-> BioOKF Molecule, subtype rna/miRNA). The ENCODES_GeM edge (Gene 'MIR6731' -> MiRNA 'hsa-miR-6731-3p') materializes exactly the BioOKF Gene-encodes->Molecule relationship. AMBIGUITY: a naive matcher may see 'miR-...' and try to force it into Gene — resist this; the mature-name+MIMAT+arm-suffix form is the Molecule, the MIR* symbol in the Gene label is the Gene.
spoke_nodes.matching_notes: PRIMARY: if the BioOKF node has a miRBase MIMAT accession or an RNACENTRAL xref, match against n.accession (exact MIMAT string) — strongest key. Otherwise match the BioOKF miRNA name against n.identifier as an exact string. NORMALIZATION (critical, miRBase names are finicky): (1) case — miRBase uses lowercase 'miR' for mature and the species prefix 'hsa-' is lowercase; canonicalize the query to 'hsa-miR-<num>-<arm>' / 'hsa-let-<...>'; (2) the arm suffix '-3p'/'-5p' is significant and distinguishes two mature products of the same hairpin (hsa-miR-6731-3p vs a hypothetical -5p are different nodes) — never strip it; (3) accept 'hsa-miR-6731' style names without arm suffix as-is (some matures have no arm, e.g. hsa-miR-8069); (4) hyphens are structural — do not remove them. PITFALLS: (1) Do NOT match a miRNA to the SPOKE Gene label — the Gene label holds the GENE symbol form 'MIR6731' / 'MIR5583-2' (uppercase MIR, hyphen-number, no 'hsa-' prefix, no -3p/-5p arm); the MiRNA label holds 'hsa-miR-6731-3p'. Route by form: uppercase 'MIR...' -> Gene; 'hsa-miR-...'/'hsa-let-...' -> MiRNA. (2) No synonyms field exists, so alias-based matching is impossible — rely on canonical name or MIMAT accession only. (3) All nodes are human (hsa-); a non-human miRNA name will not match. (4) miRBase name versioning drift (renamed matures across releases) can cause misses; MIMAT accession is more stable, prefer it when available.

spoke_nodes.label: Protein
spoke_nodes.identifier_scheme: UniProtKB accession (bare, no prefix). Format: standard UniProt 6- or 10-char accession, e.g. "P04637" (TP53/p53), "P00533" (EGFR), "P38398" (BRCA1). NOT a CURIE, NOT prefixed with 'UniProt:'. Covers both reviewed SwissProt and unreviewed TrEMBL entries across all organisms (bulk are non-human microbial, e.g. "A0A0U2LZI3").
spoke_nodes.name_property: n.name holds the UniProt ENTRY NAME (mnemonic), format ACCESSION_ORGANISM for TrEMBL (e.g. "A0A0U2LZI3_9RHIZ") or SYMBOL_ORGANISM for reviewed (e.g. "P53_HUMAN", "EGFR_HUMAN", "BRCA1_HUMAN", "INS_HUMAN"). It is NOT a human-friendly protein name and NOT the gene symbol alone. The full descriptive protein name lives in n.description; the HGNC/gene symbol lives in n.gene (a list).
spoke_nodes.synonyms: No dedicated 'synonyms' property. Alias/synonym content is distributed: n.description carries the UniProt recommended name plus alternative names in parentheses (e.g. P04637 description = "Cellular tumor antigen p53 (Antigen NY-CO-13) (Phosphoprotein p53) (Tumor suppressor p53)"; EGFR = "Epidermal growth factor receptor (2.7.10.1) (Proto-oncogene c-ErbB-1) (Receptor tyrosine-protein kinase erbB-1)"). n.gene is a list of gene-symbol synonyms. n.seqids holds cross-ref sequence IDs (GenBank/EMBL accessions). n.refseq holds RefSeq NP_/NM_ IDs. n.chembl_id links to ChEMBL. Populated well for reviewed human proteins; sparse for TrEMBL.

spoke_nodes.biookf_mapping: Primary map: BioOKF Molecule with subtype 'protein' (per SCHEMA.md cheatsheet row: 'a protein, drug, compound... -> Molecule, subtype protein, xref UniProtKB'). This is the classic Molecule-by-subtype ambiguity: BioOKF Molecule -> SPOKE Protein OR SPOKE Compound depending on subtype; a protein routes to Protein. Note the gene/protein split: BioOKF Gene (subtype protein_coding, xref NCBIGene/HGNC/ENSEMBL) maps to SPOKE Gene, NOT here; SPOKE Protein is the translated product only, joined to its gene via ENCODES_GeP. A BioOKF Structure (3D model) derives_from this Molecule, not equal to it.
spoke_nodes.matching_notes: Match strategy for a BioOKF Molecule(subtype:protein) node NAME to SPOKE Protein: (1) If the BioOKF node has a UniProt xref, match directly on n.identifier (bare accession, strip any 'UniProtKB:'/'UniProt:' prefix and any isoform suffix like '-1'). This is the reliable key. (2) If matching by symbol/name, the SPOKE gene symbol lives in n.gene (a LIST) and the full name in n.description, NOT in n.name (which is the ACC_ORGANISM mnemonic) - do NOT match against n.name for human-readable names. (3) Restrict to human via n.org_name = 'Homo sapiens (Human)' and prefer n.reviewed CONTAINS 'SwissProt' to avoid the ~39M mostly-microbial TrEMBL noise. (4) Normalize gene symbols to uppercase; account for greek->latin (alpha/beta), hyphen/space variants (ErbB-1 vs ErbB1), and 'p53'-style trivial names appearing only inside n.description parentheses. Pitfalls: n.name looks like a symbol for reviewed entries (P53_HUMAN) but is the organism-suffixed mnemonic, not a clean symbol; the same recommended name can appear across ortholog accessions in many organisms, so ALWAYS filter by organism; NEVER scan the 39M-node label unbounded - anchor by accession or by (gene, org_name) with a tight LIMIT.

spoke_nodes.label: ProteinDomain
spoke_nodes.identifier_scheme: Pfam family accession, format 'PF' + 5 digits, e.g. "PF00071" (Ras family), "PF02008" (CXXC zinc finger domain), "PF19543" (Glycoside hydrolase 123 N-terminal domain). Bare accession, no 'Pfam:' prefix. (In InterPro/Pfam nomenclature a Pfam entry is a family; SPOKE labels each individual Pfam entry 'ProteinDomain' and reserves 'ProteinFamily' for Pfam CLANS.)
spoke_nodes.name_property: n.name holds the full human-readable Pfam description/long name, e.g. "Ras family", "CXXC zinc finger domain", "Glycoside hydrolase 123, N-terminal domain", "Coatomer beta subunit appendage platform". Domains of unknown function appear as "Protein of unknown function (DUF3630)" / "Domain of unknown function DUF1846, N-terminal".
spoke_nodes.synonyms: No 'synonyms' property. The only alias field is n.entryName = the short Pfam mnemonic ID, e.g. "GH123_N" (for PF19543), "C1_PlyCB", "DUF1846", "FAM171A1-2-B_C". This is the compact Pfam short name, populated for essentially all nodes. No xrefs, no MeSH.
participating_reltypes: PARTOF_PDpP (ProteinDomain->Protein) - domain occurs in these proteins
MEMBEROF_PDmPF (ProteinDomain->ProteinFamily) - Pfam family belongs to a Pfam clan
spoke_nodes.biookf_mapping: Map: BioOKF MolecularClass with subtype 'protein_domain' (per SCHEMA.md cheatsheet: 'a grouping: ... protein family/domain -> MolecularClass, subtype protein_domain/protein_family, xref INTERPRO/PFAM'). It is a GROUPING/reference element, not a single entity: members (proteins) link via member_of / part_of. Do NOT map to Molecule. xref namespace = PFAM.
spoke_nodes.matching_notes: Match a BioOKF MolecularClass(subtype:protein_domain) to SPOKE ProteinDomain: (1) Best key is a Pfam xref -> match n.identifier exactly (uppercase 'PF' + digits, zero-padded to 5). (2) By name, match the BioOKF identifier/name against n.name (full description) case-insensitively; also try n.entryName for the terse Pfam short-code form (e.g. a source saying 'Ras' or 'zf-CXXC'). (3) Normalization: n.name uses full English descriptions with commas and 'domain'/'family' suffixes; strip/relax the trailing ', N-terminal domain' vs 'domain' and DUF parenthetical forms. Pitfalls: Pfam nomenclature calls PF##### a 'family' but SPOKE labels it ProteinDomain, while SPOKE ProteinFamily = Pfam CLAN (CL#####); do not conflate - a source that says 'InterPro/Pfam family PFxxxxx' maps HERE (ProteinDomain), not to ProteinFamily. Many entries are DUFs with no meaningful synonym; match those on identifier only.

spoke_nodes.label: ProteinFamily
spoke_nodes.identifier_scheme: Pfam CLAN accession, format 'CL' + 4 digits, e.g. "CL0545" (APCOP-app_sub), "CL0163" (Calcineurin), "CL0597" (Post-HMGL), "CL0457" (4HB_MCP). Bare accession, no prefix. A Pfam clan is a higher-order grouping of evolutionarily related Pfam entries (which SPOKE labels ProteinDomain).
spoke_nodes.name_property: n.name holds the Pfam clan short ID / mnemonic (NOT a long English description), e.g. "APCOP-app_sub", "Calcineurin", "Post-HMGL", "GlpM-like", "EpsM", "4HB_MCP". These are compact clan tokens, often terse and abbreviation-heavy.
spoke_nodes.synonyms: No 'synonyms' property and no long-name/description field at all - the node has only identifier, name, sources. There are no aliases, xrefs, or MeSH IDs to fall back on.
participating_reltypes: MEMBEROF_PDmPF (ProteinDomain->ProteinFamily) - the ONLY reltype touching this label; Pfam entries (ProteinDomain) are members of this clan. ProteinFamily is always the object/target endpoint, never the source.
spoke_nodes.biookf_mapping: Map: BioOKF MolecularClass with subtype 'protein_family' (SCHEMA.md cheatsheet grouping row, xref PFAM/INTERPRO). It is a grouping node whose members (Pfam domains/entries) link via member_of. Do NOT map to Molecule. Distinct from SPOKE ProteinDomain only by Pfam hierarchy level (clan vs entry) - both share the same BioOKF type MolecularClass, differing only by the coined subtype (protein_family vs protein_domain).
spoke_nodes.matching_notes: Match a BioOKF MolecularClass(subtype:protein_family) to SPOKE ProteinFamily: (1) The cleanest key is a Pfam clan xref -> match n.identifier exactly (uppercase 'CL' + 4 digits). (2) By name, match against n.name, but note n.name is the terse clan mnemonic (e.g. '4HB_MCP', 'APCOP-app_sub'), NOT a full English family name - a BioOKF node named e.g. 'Calcineurin family' will only fuzzy-match the token 'Calcineurin'; do case-insensitive contains/token matching and strip trailing 'family'/'clan'/'superfamily' words. (3) There is no description or synonym field, so name-only matching is the sole option when no CL accession is present - expect low recall for descriptive source names. Pitfalls: small label (659 nodes); a 'protein family' in casual source text most often corresponds to a Pfam ENTRY (SPOKE ProteinDomain, PF#####), NOT a Pfam clan - only true Pfam CLANS live here. When ambiguous, check for a CL vs PF accession to disambiguate ProteinFamily vs ProteinDomain.

spoke_nodes.label: Complex
spoke_nodes.identifier_scheme: Two coexisting schemes by source. (A) Complex Portal complexes (source is null; sources=['Complex Portal']): n.identifier is an opaque internal integer string (e.g. "3752158019", "4234304213"), and the real EBI CURIE lives in n.complex_portal (e.g. "CPX-3296", "CPX-2304", "CPX-5695"). (B) CellChatDB ligand-receptor complexes (source=['CellChatDB']): n.identifier is 'CellChatDB:' + UniProt-accession pair joined by underscore, e.g. "CellChatDB:O60462_Q9UIW2", "CellChatDB:P04626_P21860".
spoke_nodes.name_property: n.name is a human-readable complex name whose form depends on source. Complex Portal: descriptive English name, e.g. "Fucose-binding lectin II complex", "SARS-CoV Spike - human ACE2 receptor complex". CellChatDB: gene-symbol pair joined by underscore, e.g. "NRP2_PLXNA1", "FZD7_LRP5", "ERBB2_ERBB3", "IL22RA1_IL10RB".
spoke_nodes.synonyms: Populated ONLY for Complex Portal nodes: n.synonyms is a list of alternative complex names (e.g. PF00... 'Fucose-binding lectin PA-IIL complex' for CPX-3296; 'LT-IIB complex' for CPX-2304); some entries carry an empty-string synonym. CellChatDB nodes have NO synonyms property (their key set is just source/name/identifier). n.description (Complex Portal only) holds a long free-text functional summary that also embeds member UniProt accessions and CHEBI/gene references.
key_properties: complex_portal (Complex Portal only, the CPX- CURIE)
data_sources: Complex Portal (EBI, manually curated macromolecular complexes; CPX- accessions)
participating_reltypes: PARTOF_PpCP (Protein->Complex) - subunit proteins are part of the complex; the primary way to enumerate members (e.g. Q9UIW2/PLXNA1 and O60462/NRP2 -> NRP2_PLXNA1)
spoke_nodes.biookf_mapping: Map: BioOKF Molecule with subtype 'complex' (SCHEMA.md cheatsheet explicitly lists 'complex' as a Molecule subtype: 'a protein, drug, compound, ... complex ... -> Molecule'). It is a single (assembled) entity, not a grouping, so Molecule not MolecularClass; its member proteins link via part_of/member_of. Ambiguity note: this is the same Molecule-by-subtype fan-out - BioOKF Molecule -> SPOKE Protein (subtype protein) / Compound (small_molecule/drug) / Complex (subtype complex); route a multi-subunit assembly here.
spoke_nodes.matching_notes: Match a BioOKF Molecule(subtype:complex) to SPOKE Complex: (1) If the source cites a Complex Portal CPX- accession, match on n.complex_portal (NOT n.identifier, which is an opaque integer). (2) By name, match against n.name AND n.synonyms (Complex Portal has both; do case-insensitive contains and strip trailing 'complex'). For ligand-receptor pairs, CellChatDB n.name is 'GENEA_GENEB' (uppercase gene symbols, underscore) - normalize a source's 'ERBB2-ERBB3'/'HER2/HER3' to the underscore uppercase form, and note order may need to be tried both ways (A_B vs B_A). (3) To match by members, use PARTOF_PpCP to enumerate subunit proteins by UniProt accession and reconstruct the pair. Pitfalls: two heterogeneous ID/name conventions in one label - never assume a single scheme; n.identifier is NOT the citable ID for Complex Portal (use complex_portal); CellChatDB nodes lack synonyms/description so only name-pair matching works; some Complex Portal synonyms are empty strings; small label (4252) so exact/near-exact name matching is feasible without scan-size concerns.

spoke_nodes.label: Compound
spoke_nodes.identifier_scheme: Predominantly a prefixed InChIKey CURIE: 'inchikey:<27-char InChIKey>', e.g. 'inchikey:BSYNRYMUTXBXSQ-UHFFFAOYSA-N' (Aspirin). Empirically ~99.8% of nodes use this prefix. A small minority (~0.2%, compounds with no computable InChIKey such as organometallic complexes and biologics) instead use 'chembl.compound:<CHEMBL id>', e.g. 'chembl.compound:CHEMBL1201575' (EFALIZUMAB). So the identifier namespace is InChIKey by default, ChEMBL as fallback. Not a bare integer, not PubChem CID (those live in xrefs).
spoke_nodes.name_property: n.name holds a human-readable compound/drug name. For well-known drugs it is the common/preferred name (e.g. 'Aspirin', 'Ibuprofen'); for structures ingested from PDBe/ChEMBL it is often a long IUPAC-style systematic name (e.g. "'(1S)-1-(9-Deazaadenin-9-YL)-...'") and may include leading quotes/odd casing. ~0.2% of sampled nodes have an empty-string name ('') (43/20000).
spoke_nodes.synonyms: n.synonyms (a string list) carries synonyms/aliases and is present on 100% of sampled nodes. BUT it is a mixed bag: it contains true names (brand names 'Advil'/'Motrin'/'Nurofen', INN 'Ibuprofen (JP17/USP/INN)', chemical names) intermixed with bare cross-reference IDs as plain strings (PubChem CID '2244', CAS '50-78-2', 'CHEBI:15365', 'CHEMBL25', 'DB00945', 'D00109', 'AIN'). For ChEMBL-only fallback compounds synonyms is often just ['']  (empty placeholder). The cleaner, typed cross-references live in n.xrefs (CURIE list, ~99.8% populated): 'chembl.compound:', 'drugbank:', 'kegg.compound:', 'kegg.drug:', 'CHEBI:', 'pubchem.compound:', 'pdb.ligand:', 'biocyc:'.

spoke_nodes.biookf_mapping: Maps to BioOKF `Molecule` (SCHEMA.md line 75: 'a protein, drug, compound, metabolite, antibody, ion, complex' -> Molecule, with subtype drug/small_molecule/metabolite/antibody/complex/ion; source vocabularies CHEBI/PUBCHEM/DRUGBANK/RXNORM/CHEMBL). AMBIGUITY: BioOKF `Molecule` is a superset — its protein/RNA subtypes map to SPOKE Protein, not Compound. So the mapping is directional: a BioOKF Molecule with subtype small_molecule/drug/metabolite/ion/compound -> SPOKE Compound; subtype protein/rna -> SPOKE Protein; subtype complex -> could be SPOKE Complex OR Compound (biologics like EFALIZUMAB/TIRZEPATIDE are stored as Compound here). Do NOT map to BioOKF `MolecularClass` — a single chemical entity is a Molecule; only groupings/classes are MolecularClass (that is SPOKE's PharmacologicClass). Per SCHEMA.md line 326, 'Aspirin is a Molecule' regardless of its treats/binds roles.
spoke_nodes.matching_notes: Best keyed by structure when available: if the BioOKF node has an InChIKey, match directly on identifier 'inchikey:<KEY>' (exact, uppercase, keep the two hash blocks and stereo/proto flags). If it carries a ChEMBL/DrugBank/PubChem/CHEBI/KEGG id, match against n.xrefs CURIEs (chembl.compound:, drugbank:, kegg.drug:, kegg.compound:, CHEBI:, pubchem.compound:, pdb.ligand:) — this is the most reliable ID route and avoids name ambiguity. For NAME matching: (1) try exact match on n.name first, then (2) search n.synonyms (which holds brand names, INN, and chemical synonyms). Normalize before comparing: lowercase (n.name/synonyms have inconsistent casing and stray leading quotes/apostrophes), strip surrounding quotes, normalize Greek letters (alpha<->α, beta<->β), unify hyphens/spaces/commas in systematic names, and strip salt/hydrate suffixes (e.g. 'hydrochloride', 'sodium', '; Hydrate') since SPOKE Compound is keyed on the neutral parent InChIKey (salt forms collapse). PITFALLS: (a) n.synonyms is polluted with bare ID strings (CAS numbers, PubChem CIDs, ChEMBL/DrugBank/KEGG accessions) — do not treat a numeric/accession-looking synonym as a name; route those through xrefs instead. (b) ~0.2% of Compounds have empty name '' and synonyms [''] (ChEMBL-only complexes/biologics) — these are only matchable via identifier/xrefs. (c) The same drug can appear across multiple salt/stereo InChIKeys; prefer the parent. (d) Long IUPAC systematic names in n.name make fuzzy name matching noisy — prefer InChIKey/xref matching whenever a structure or DB id exists.

spoke_nodes.label: PharmacologicClass
spoke_nodes.identifier_scheme: NDF-RT (National Drug File – Reference Terminology) concept NUI — an 'N' + 10-digit code, e.g. 'N0000175856', 'N0000020058', 'N0000009079'. Confirmed by n.url template 'http://purl.bioontology.org/ontology/NDFRT/$identifier'. Bare code, no CURIE prefix. NOT ATC, NOT MeSH, NOT an integer.
spoke_nodes.name_property: n.name holds the full human-readable class label from NDF-RT, e.g. 'Glucagon-like Peptide-1 (GLP-1) Agonists', 'Cytochrome P450 3A4 Inhibitors', 'Increased Acetylcholine Activity', 'CD11a-directed Antibody Interactions'. The wording depends on class_type: MoA classes read like mechanisms ('... Inhibitors/Agonists'), PE classes read like physiologic effects ('Increased/Decreased ... Activity').
spoke_nodes.synonyms: NONE. Empirically confirmed there is no synonyms/aliases/xrefs property on this label (any(k IN keys(n) WHERE k='synonyms') = false across samples). Only name, identifier, class_type, source, license, url exist. No alias field is available for matching.
data_sources: FDA via DrugCentral (n.source); underlying ontology is NDF-RT (National Drug File – Reference Terminology), per n.url = http://purl.bioontology.org/ontology/NDFRT/. License: CC BY 4.0
spoke_nodes.biookf_mapping: Maps to BioOKF `MolecularClass` with subtype `pharmacologic` (SCHEMA.md line 76: 'a grouping: drug class, ... chemical class' -> MolecularClass, subtype pharmacologic; source vocabularies ATC/NCIT — here the actual source is NDF-RT/DrugCentral). Members (individual drugs) link to the class via BioOKF `member_of` (SCHEMA.md line 133/185: one entity=Molecule, a grouping=MolecularClass, members link by member_of) — mirroring SPOKE's INCLUDES_PCiC (PharmacologicClass -> Compound). Do NOT map to BioOKF `Molecule`: this is a class/grouping, not a single chemical entity. Minor ambiguity: NDF-RT class_type values distinguish MoA (mechanism), PE (physiologic effect), CS (chemical structure), Chemical/Ingredient — all still roll up to MolecularClass:pharmacologic; the class_type could inform a finer subtype note.
spoke_nodes.matching_notes: Only 635 nodes and NO synonyms field — matching must rely on n.name and n.identifier. (1) If the BioOKF node carries an NDF-RT NUI ('N##########'), match exactly on n.identifier — most reliable. (2) Otherwise match on n.name, normalized: lowercase, collapse whitespace, and be aware NDF-RT names embed the class-forming suffix ('Inhibitors', 'Agonists', 'Antagonists', 'Blockers') and effect phrasing ('Increased/Decreased X Activity'). A BioOKF drug-class name like 'GLP-1 agonists' should be matched against 'Glucagon-like Peptide-1 (GLP-1) Agonists' — expect parenthetical abbreviations and full expansions, and plural forms. PITFALLS: (a) These are FDA/NDF-RT MoA/PE/CS categories, NOT ATC classes and NOT MeSH pharmacological-action terms — an ATC or MeSH class name may not have a 1:1 string match here (small 635-node vocabulary, sparse coverage). (b) No aliases, so an equivalent class under a different naming convention will miss unless you normalize/expand abbreviations yourself. (c) Some entries are physiologic effects ('Increased Uterine Smooth Muscle Contraction or Tone') rather than drug-class names — do not force-match those to a mechanism-style BioOKF class. (d) Because coverage is small, prefer to route drug-class groupings to SPOKE only when an NDF-RT id or a close name match exists; otherwise leave unmatched rather than over-map.

spoke_nodes.label: Disease
spoke_nodes.identifier_scheme: Disease Ontology CURIE (DOID). Format 'DOID:' + numeric string, e.g. 'DOID:9352' (type 2 diabetes mellitus), 'DOID:0081371'. Verified: all 11,735 nodes start with 'DOID' (query counted 11735). Note zero-padded newer IDs (DOID:0080035) coexist with short legacy IDs (DOID:9352). 27 nodes carry obsolete=true.
spoke_nodes.name_property: n.name = lowercase natural-language disease label following Disease Ontology naming, e.g. 'type 2 diabetes mellitus', 'breast cancer', 'hypertension', 'asthma'. Casing is lowercase EXCEPT proper nouns which stay capitalized (e.g. "Alzheimer's disease", "North Carolina macular dystrophy"). No inverted-comma reordering.
spoke_nodes.synonyms: No dedicated synonyms/aliases property (confirmed by scanning keys() over 100 nodes: only identifier, name, mesh_list, omim_list, obsolete, source). The xref arrays n.mesh_list (MeSH IDs, mix of D-descriptors like 'D006009' and C-supplementary like 'C565495') and n.omim_list (bare OMIM numeric IDs, e.g. '618912') serve as cross-reference/ID-join fields, NOT name synonyms. Both are frequently EMPTY arrays [] (most sampled DOID-only nodes had []); populated only for a subset that DO carries a MeSH/OMIM mapping.
data_sources: Disease Ontology (single value of n.source for all nodes)

example_nodes.name: sorbitol dehydrogenase deficiency with peripheral neuropathy

spoke_nodes.biookf_mapping: Maps to BioOKF `Disease` (a diagnosed condition the patient has; MONDO/DOID/OMIM/ICD10/MESH per the cheatsheet, DOID being explicitly listed). This is a clean 1:1 label mapping. subtype hints from the name: neoplasm/cancer/carcinoma -> `neoplasm`; 'syndrome' -> `syndrome`; infection/'-itis' caused by an Organism (CAUSES_OcD) -> `infection`; injury -> `injury`. Ambiguity vs `Phenotype`: SPOKE Disease is the diagnosis facet only, so it never competes with BioOKF Phenotype for the same node — but a source term dual-listed as disease+phenotype (e.g. hyperlipidemia) would land here IF its CURIE is a DOID/MONDO, and separately in Phenotype if HP. Pin the facet by the incoming xref namespace (DOID/OMIM/MeSH-disease => Disease).
spoke_nodes.matching_notes: PREFERRED: match by identifier when the BioOKF node has a DOID/MONDO/OMIM/MeSH xref. Direct DOID -> n.identifier equality. OMIM number -> search n.omim_list (array contains). MeSH disease ID -> search n.mesh_list (array contains). NAME matching (fallback): lowercase both sides before comparing because SPOKE Disease names are already lowercased (except proper nouns) — e.g. BioOKF 'Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus' -> lower -> exact hit on 'type 2 diabetes mellitus'. Normalize greek letters (alpha/beta), hyphen vs space, and possessive apostrophes ("Alzheimer's"). PITFALLS: (1) No name-synonym field exists, so acronyms (T2DM, COPD) and lay names (heart attack vs 'myocardial infarction') will NOT match on name alone — resolve via xref or an external DOID synonym table first. (2) 27 obsolete=true nodes exist; exclude or de-prioritize them. (3) Do NOT match a diagnosis term to the Symptom or SideEffect labels: e.g. 'endocarditis' also appears under Symptom (MeSH D004696) — keep Disease matches to DOID-namespaced BioOKF nodes. (4) Cancer names differ ('breast cancer' here vs 'breast carcinoma'/'malignant neoplasm of breast' elsewhere).

spoke_nodes.label: Symptom
spoke_nodes.identifier_scheme: MeSH descriptor / supplementary-concept ID (NOT an HPO ID, even for HPO-sourced nodes). Format is a MeSH accession: 'D' + digits for descriptors (e.g. 'D005334' Fever, 'D009325' Nausea, 'D000006') = 1674 of 1905; 'C' + digits for MeSH supplementary concepts (e.g. 'C538141'). Verified: 1674 start with 'D'. HPO-origin symptoms have been re-coded to MeSH IDs (e.g. 'Cryptorchidism' -> D003456), so the namespace is uniformly MeSH regardless of source.
spoke_nodes.name_property: n.name = MeSH descriptor string in MeSH inverted-comma convention (Title Case, qualifier after comma), e.g. 'Abdomen, Acute', 'Amnesia, Anterograde', 'Akathisia, Drug-Induced', 'Fever', 'Nausea'. HPO-sourced entries keep HPO-style phrasing but still Title Case ('Abnormality of the kidney', 'Nephrotic syndrome'). 12 nodes have a NULL name (e.g. identifier C538141).
spoke_nodes.synonyms: No synonyms/aliases property (keys() over 100 nodes = identifier, name, license, url, source only). No xref arrays either. There is NO way to match on synonyms within the node; only the single name string and the MeSH identifier are available.
data_sources: HPO (n.source='HPO', 1478 nodes — the majority; phenotype terms mapped onto MeSH IDs)
participating_reltypes: PRESENTS_DpS (Disease->Symptom; rel_keys = enrichment, odds, cooccur, fisher, sources; rel_sources=['NCBI PubMed'] — literature co-occurrence derived)
spoke_nodes.biookf_mapping: Maps to BioOKF `Phenotype` (the cheatsheet row 'a symptom, sign, side effect, qualitative trait...' -> type=`Phenotype`), with subtype `symptom` (subjective/patient-reported) or `sign` (objective) per SPEC. NOTE the label-name mismatch: SPOKE calls it 'Symptom' but BioOKF has NO 'Symptom' type — it collapses into `Phenotype`. Ambiguity: SPOKE Symptom overlaps heavily with SPOKE SideEffect and even Disease conceptually; all three collapse toward BioOKF `Phenotype`/`Disease`. Because SPOKE Symptom is MeSH-coded while BioOKF Phenotype prefers HP/MP/MEDDRA xrefs, a Symptom node maps to Phenotype but its xref namespace (MeSH) is the disease/phenotype-shared MeSH space, so use the term's clinical facet (a sign/symptom) rather than the namespace to confirm Phenotype.
spoke_nodes.matching_notes: Match a BioOKF Phenotype(subtype symptom/sign) NAME to this label. PREFERRED: if the BioOKF node has a MeSH xref, join on n.identifier directly (both are MeSH IDs). NAME matching: normalize to handle MeSH inverted commas — SPOKE stores 'Abdomen, Acute' where a BioOKF/HPO term would read 'acute abdomen'; strip and reorder around commas, then case-fold. Title-case-fold both sides ('fever' <-> 'Fever'). Normalize hyphens/spaces ('Akathisia, Drug-Induced'). PITFALLS: (1) Only 1905 nodes and NO synonym field — recall is low; many HPO phenotypes are absent or coded under a broader MeSH descriptor ('Abnormality of the kidney'). (2) 12 nodes have NULL name — skip them. (3) CRITICAL cross-label collision: the SAME concept can exist as Symptom (MeSH ID) AND SideEffect (UMLS CUI) — e.g. Nausea = Symptom D009325 AND SideEffect C0027497. When a BioOKF node carries a MeSH xref, prefer Symptom; when it carries a UMLS/MedDRA xref, prefer SideEffect. (4) Do not match a diagnosis (e.g. 'Nephrotic syndrome', 'Endocarditis' appear here) to the Disease label unless it is DOID-coded.

spoke_nodes.label: SideEffect
spoke_nodes.identifier_scheme: UMLS Concept Unique Identifier (CUI), as used by SIDER/MedDRA. Format 'C' + 7 digits, e.g. 'C0013922' (Embolism), 'C0027497' (Nausea), 'C0151662'. Verified: all 5,923 nodes start with 'C' (query counted 5923). This is the UMLS/MedDRA preferred-term CUI space, DISTINCT from MeSH supplementary 'C...' IDs used elsewhere.
spoke_nodes.name_property: n.name = MedDRA/UMLS preferred term, Title Case on first word only, with lab-abnormality terms in adjective-last MedDRA style, e.g. 'Embolism', 'Erythema', 'Rash pustular', 'Gamma-glutamyltransferase increased', 'Blood bilirubin increased', 'Alanine aminotransferase increased', 'Sweating increased'. No inverted-comma reordering; instead a trailing modifier ('... increased', '... venous').
spoke_nodes.synonyms: No synonyms/aliases/xref property (keys() over 100 nodes = identifier, name, sources only). No MeSH/OMIM lists. Matching is limited to the single name string and the UMLS CUI.
data_sources: SIDER 4.1 (n.sources = ['SIDER 4.1'] for every node — the sole contributing DB; SIDER derives its terms from drug labels coded in UMLS/MedDRA)
participating_reltypes: CAUSES_CcSE (Compound->SideEffect; the ONLY reltype touching this label; rel_keys=['sources']; source Compound carries inchikey identifiers e.g. inchikey:DUSHUSLJJMDGTE-ZJPMUUANSA-N)
spoke_nodes.biookf_mapping: Maps to BioOKF `Phenotype` with subtype `side_effect` (cheatsheet: 'a symptom, sign, side effect, qualitative trait...' -> type=`Phenotype`; subtype example `side_effect`; namespaces include MEDDRA which matches SIDER's UMLS/MedDRA coding). Like Symptom, the SPOKE label name has no direct BioOKF counterpart and collapses into `Phenotype`. Some SideEffect terms are actually lab-measure abnormalities ('Alanine aminotransferase increased', 'Blood bilirubin increased') that, seen bottom-up, straddle BioOKF `BiomedicalMeasure` — but as an ADVERSE OUTCOME of a drug they remain `Phenotype`/subtype side_effect (the observed abnormal state, not the measurable variable). The drug->SideEffect edge maps to BioOKF `causes`/`has_phenotype` (adverse-event sense).
spoke_nodes.matching_notes: Match a BioOKF Phenotype(subtype side_effect) NAME to this label. PREFERRED: if the BioOKF node carries a UMLS CUI or MedDRA xref, join on n.identifier (UMLS CUI). NAME matching: case-fold (Title-first-word vs lowercase). Handle MedDRA adjective-last word order: SPOKE 'Sweating increased' / 'Blood bilirubin increased' vs a natural-language 'increased sweating' — reorder tokens or do token-set matching. Normalize hyphens and enzyme abbreviations ('Gamma-glutamyltransferase' vs 'GGT'). PITFALLS: (1) No synonym field and enzyme/lab terms use full names, so abbreviation forms (ALT/AST/GGT) will not match on name. (2) MAJOR cross-label collision with Symptom: identical concept, different namespace — Nausea is SideEffect C0027497 AND Symptom D009325; route by the BioOKF node's xref (UMLS/MedDRA -> SideEffect, MeSH -> Symptom) or by edge context (came from a drug's adverse profile -> SideEffect). (3) Some entries are lab-abnormality phenotypes that a naive matcher might send to BiomedicalMeasure — keep them here when the context is an adverse drug reaction. (4) Only Compound->SideEffect edges exist, so a SideEffect node is only reachable/meaningful in the drug-safety context.

spoke_nodes.label: Anatomy
spoke_nodes.identifier_scheme: UBERON ontology CURIE, colon form. Bare-integer local IDs are Uberon anatomy terms (e.g. UBERON:0003233 = 'epithelium of shoulder'); IDs in the 2000000+ range are developmental/zebrafish terms (e.g. UBERON:2001901 = 'ceratobranchial 3 element'). 100% of a 1000-node sample carried the UBERON prefix. No non-UBERON identifiers observed.
spoke_nodes.name_property: n.name holds the full human-readable UBERON anatomy label in lowercase (e.g. 'epithelium of shoulder', 'lumbar vertebra', 'lymphomyeloid tissue'), not an abbreviation or code.
spoke_nodes.synonyms: Two synonym fields, both SPARSELY populated. n.synonyms holds Uberon exact/related synonyms (in a 500-node sample only ~12/500 had any). n.aliases holds cross-ontology brain-atlas local IDs like 'HOMBA:12573','DHBA_12573' (~22/500 populated), NOT text aliases. n.mesh_id holds a single MeSH descriptor ID when a MeSH mapping exists (e.g. 'D008159' for lumbar vertebra; ~30/500 populated), empty string '' otherwise. Do NOT rely on synonyms for name matching - most Anatomy nodes only have their canonical name.
data_sources: HOMBA (Human/mammalian brain atlas cross-refs appearing in aliases and as a minor source)

example_nodes.name: caudal part of spinal trigeminal nucleus

spoke_nodes.biookf_mapping: BioOKF `Anatomy`. Direct 1:1 match: the SCHEMA.md cheatsheet maps 'organ, tissue, body region, organelle, body fluid' to `Anatomy` with the UBERON xref namespace, exactly what this label is. BioOKF subtypes to coin per-node: organ/tissue/subcellular/body_fluid/body_region. NOTE one subtlety: BioOKF `Anatomy` subtype `subcellular` (organelle) overlaps with SPOKE's SEPARATE `CellularComponent` (GO) label - a BioOKF Anatomy node describing an organelle may need to match SPOKE CellularComponent instead of/in addition to Anatomy. Body-region cell aggregates are still Anatomy here (SPOKE keeps cells in CellType, not Anatomy).
spoke_nodes.matching_notes: Primary strategy: exact case-insensitive match of the BioOKF node's human-readable identifier/name against n.name (UBERON labels are canonical lowercase). If no hit, try n.synonyms (sparse) then fall back to xref: if the BioOKF node carries an xref 'UBERON:xxxxxxx', match directly on n.identifier - this is the most reliable path since only ~7-12% of Anatomy nodes have text synonyms. If the BioOKF node has a MeSH xref, match against n.mesh_id (single descriptor per node). Normalization: lowercase both sides, collapse whitespace, strip trailing qualifiers in parentheses (UBERON synonyms sometimes append '(...)', e.g. 'temporal pole (temporopolar cortex)'). Pitfalls: (1) n.aliases is NOT free-text synonyms - it holds opaque brain-atlas codes (HOMBA:/DHBA_), never match a name against it. (2) Plurals/US-UK spelling differ from UBERON's singular canonical form. (3) Do not confuse organelle names (mitochondrion, nucleus) here with SPOKE CellularComponent - check both labels for subcellular BioOKF nodes. (4) Body-fluid names (blood, plasma) exist in Anatomy but may collide with MaterialSample naming in BioOKF - type by identity.

spoke_nodes.label: CellType
spoke_nodes.identifier_scheme: Cell Ontology CURIE, CL prefix, colon form, 7-digit local ID (e.g. CL:2000082 = 'melanocyte of foreskin', CL:0000836 = 'promyelocyte', CL:0000050 = 'megakaryocyte-erythroid progenitor cell'). Uniform across the label.
spoke_nodes.name_property: n.name holds the full canonical Cell Ontology cell-type label in lowercase (e.g. 'promyelocyte', 'peripheral blood stem cell', 'outer medulla vasa recta descending limb cell'). Descriptive, not an acronym.
spoke_nodes.synonyms: n.synonyms is a list of CL exact/related synonyms and is MODERATELY populated: in a 500-node sample ~223/500 (~45%) had at least one non-empty synonym. Values include abbreviations and alternate spellings (e.g. for 'megakaryocyte-erythroid progenitor cell': ['megakaryocyte/erythroid progenitor cell','MEP','CFU-MegE','Meg/E progenitor',...]; 'peripheral blood stem cell' -> ['PBSC']). Empty entries appear as [''] (a list containing one empty string) for un-annotated nodes - filter x<>'' before use. n.description holds a prose definition (marker genes, lineage) and is well populated.
spoke_nodes.biookf_mapping: BioOKF `CellType`. Direct match: cheatsheet maps 'a cell type / state / line / organoid' to `CellType` with xref namespaces CL, CLO. IMPORTANT: BioOKF collapses cell_type + cell_state + cell_line + organoid into the single `CellType` type, whereas SPOKE SPLITS these across THREE labels: canonical cell types = SPOKE CellType (CL); cell LINES = SPOKE CellLine (CLO); provisional/transcriptomic-atlas cell types = SPOKE ProvCellType (PCL). So a BioOKF CellType node maps to SPOKE CellType when subtype=cell_type/cell_state, to SPOKE CellLine when subtype=cell_line, and possibly to SPOKE ProvCellType for fine-grained single-cell cluster types. Coin subtype cell_type here.
spoke_nodes.matching_notes: Primary: exact case-insensitive match of BioOKF name against n.name (CL canonical labels). Then search n.synonyms (filter to x<>''), which carries the common abbreviations (MEP, PBSC, Th17, etc.) that BioOKF nodes are often named by - this field is essential because clinical/paper text uses acronyms not CL long-form. If BioOKF node has an xref 'CL:xxxxxxx', match n.identifier directly (most reliable). Normalization: lowercase; normalize the '/' vs '-' vs ' ' variants (CL synonyms mix 'megakaryocyte/erythroid' and 'megakaryocyte-erythroid'); strip trailing 'cell'/'cells' inconsistencies; expand or contract Greek letters and 'positive/negative' vs '+/-' marker notation. Pitfalls: (1) A BioOKF cell_line-subtype node should be routed to SPOKE CellLine, not CellType - check subtype/xref namespace (CLO vs CL) first. (2) ProvCellType has CL-lookalike prose but PCL identifiers - do not force a fine cluster type onto a coarse CL node. (3) Empty synonyms encoded as [''] will false-match an empty query string - always filter.

spoke_nodes.label: CellularComponent
spoke_nodes.identifier_scheme: Gene Ontology CURIE from the cellular_component (CC) sub-ontology, GO prefix, colon form, 7-digit local ID (e.g. GO:0061908 = 'phagophore', GO:0005606 = 'laminin-1 complex', GO:0072557 = 'IPAF inflammasome complex'). 100% GO prefix in sample. Each node also stores a resolvable OBO PURL in n.url (e.g. http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_0061908).
spoke_nodes.name_property: n.name holds the canonical GO cellular_component term label in lowercase (organelles, complexes, membranes, subcellular locations), e.g. 'phagophore', 'extrinsic component of presynaptic endocytic zone membrane', 'laminin-1 complex'.
spoke_nodes.synonyms: NO synonyms field. This label has NO synonyms/aliases property at all (keys are source/name/url/identifier/description/license). n.description simply repeats the term name verbatim in the samples (description == name), so it carries no extra matching signal. There is no acronym/alias support - matching must rely on name or the GO identifier.
data_sources: Gene Ontology (GO cellular_component branch); license CC BY 4.0
spoke_nodes.biookf_mapping: AMBIGUOUS between two BioOKF types. GO cellular_component terms are subcellular locations/organelles AND macromolecular complexes. (1) Organelle/location terms (phagophore, presynaptic membrane, nucleus) map to BioOKF `Anatomy` (subtype: subcellular) per the cheatsheet's 'organelle' entry - and thus also overlap SPOKE's own Anatomy label. (2) Protein/macromolecular COMPLEX terms (laminin-1 complex, IPAF inflammasome complex) map to BioOKF `Molecule` (subtype: complex) since the cheatsheet routes 'complex' to Molecule, OR to `BiologicalFunction`/`Concept` in edge-cases. There is no dedicated BioOKF CellularComponent type; a matcher must inspect the term to decide Anatomy-subcellular vs Molecule-complex. When a BioOKF node carries a GO: xref for a CC term, prefer SPOKE CellularComponent.
spoke_nodes.matching_notes: Primary and essentially only reliable path: if the BioOKF node has an xref 'GO:xxxxxxx' in the CC branch, match n.identifier directly. Text matching: exact case-insensitive match of BioOKF name against n.name only (there are NO synonyms to fall back on, so recall is limited to canonical GO labels). Normalization: lowercase, collapse whitespace, normalize hyphen/space; expand roman-numeral/complex suffixes; 'complex' vs 'complexes'. Pitfalls: (1) Because there are no synonyms and description==name, a BioOKF node named with an informal or abbreviated location (e.g. 'ER' for endoplasmic reticulum, 'PM' for plasma membrane) will NOT match - you must expand abbreviations from the BioOKF side before matching. (2) Route by subtype: BioOKF Anatomy(subcellular) and Molecule(complex) nodes both can land here - disambiguate using the GO CC vs the term's semantics. (3) Do not confuse GO-CC terms with the GO biological_process / molecular_function branches, which live in SPOKE's Pathway/BiologicalProcess-type labels, not here.

spoke_nodes.label: AnatomyCellType
spoke_nodes.identifier_scheme: UNDETERMINABLE - the label has ZERO nodes in this SPOKE build (confirmed by MATCH (n:`AnatomyCellType`) RETURN count(n) => 0, and label_properties.property_keys == []). No identifier scheme can be observed. By naming convention it would be a composite Anatomy x CellType (e.g. a cell-type-in-anatomical-context) node, but nothing exists to confirm.
spoke_nodes.name_property: Unknown - no nodes exist, so n.name cannot be observed.
spoke_nodes.synonyms: Unknown - no nodes, no property keys observed.
data_sources: none observable (label is empty in this build)
participating_reltypes: none - the label appears in ZERO relationship_signatures in the schema skeleton; it is an unused/reserved or not-yet-populated label
spoke_nodes.biookf_mapping: No mapping is actionable because the label is empty. Conceptually a composite Anatomy+CellType node would map to a BioOKF `CellType` node linked to an `Anatomy` node via a `part_of`/`located_in` edge (BioOKF represents 'cell type in tissue context' as an edge, never as a fused node). Since SPOKE has 0 such nodes, EXCLUDE AnatomyCellType from any name-matching pipeline.
spoke_nodes.matching_notes: Do NOT attempt to match BioOKF nodes to this label: it contains 0 nodes and participates in 0 relationships in the current SPOKE build. Any query will return empty. If a future build populates it, expect an anatomy+celltype composite; a BioOKF 'cell type located in tissue' concept should be decomposed into a CellType node + an Anatomy node + a part_of/located_in edge rather than matched to a fused node. Treat as a reserved/placeholder label for now.

spoke_nodes.label: ProvCellType
spoke_nodes.identifier_scheme: Provisional Cell Ontology CURIE, PCL prefix, colon form, 7-digit local ID (e.g. PCL:0051183, PCL:0051359, PCL:0051054). 100% PCL prefix. These are provisional/transcriptomic-cluster cell types (single-cell atlas clusters), not stable CL terms.
spoke_nodes.name_property: n.name holds a cluster-derived descriptive label combining an internal cluster code, a coarse cell type, and species tag, e.g. 'CA13_182 hippocampal CA1-3 neuron (Hsap)', 'Splat_358 neuron (Hsap)', 'Astro_53 astrocyte (Hsap)'. The '(Hsap)' suffix = Homo sapiens. Name is atlas-specific, NOT a clean ontology label.
spoke_nodes.synonyms: n.synonyms is WELL populated (every sampled node had 2 entries): typically [the short cluster code (e.g. 'CA13_182','Splat_358','Astro_53'), and a long marker-gene-expression description (e.g. 'GATA3 (Hsap), ZFHX3 (Hsap), ... expressing neuron of brain (Homo sapiens)')]. So synonyms carry both the raw cluster ID and a marker-gene phenotypic descriptor. n.description gives a prose definition with marker genes + soma location; n.study_description names the source atlas ('Siletti et al. 2023, Science - A transcriptomic atlas of the human brain'); n.citation holds a DOI (e.g. DOI:10.1126/science.add7046).
data_sources: underlying study: Siletti et al. 2023 Science human-brain transcriptomic atlas (via citation DOI:10.1126/science.add7046 and study_description)

synonyms_sample: GATA3 (Hsap), ZFHX3 (Hsap), GRIK1 (Hsap), TFAP2B (Hsap), TAFA1 (Hsap) expressing neuron of brain (Homo sapiens)

example_nodes.name: Astro_53 astrocyte (Hsap)
synonyms_sample: COL5A3 (Hsap), GLI3 (Hsap) expressing astrocyte of brain (Homo sapiens)

spoke_nodes.biookf_mapping: BioOKF `CellType` (subtype: cell_type or cell_state / transcriptomic_cluster). These are fine-grained single-cell atlas cell types; the cheatsheet's `CellType` (xref CL/CLO, extendable to PCL) is the right type. Each ProvCellType ISA a coarse SPOKE CellType (CL), so in BioOKF it is a more specific `CellType` node linked by `is_a` to the coarse CellType. Marker genes (MARKER_OF/ENRICHED_IN) become `Gene`-`expressed_in`/`marker` edges, not attributes of the type.
spoke_nodes.matching_notes: These are hard to match by clean name because n.name embeds an atlas cluster code + species suffix. Strategy: (1) Best path is xref - if a BioOKF node carries 'PCL:xxxxxxx', match n.identifier directly. (2) For coarse concepts, do NOT match a generic BioOKF cell type (e.g. 'astrocyte') to a ProvCellType - it will over-match many clusters; route generic types to SPOKE CellType (CL) instead and use ProvCellType only for atlas-cluster-specific concepts. (3) If matching a cluster, search n.synonyms for the short cluster code (e.g. 'Astro_53') - that is the cleanest handle. Normalization: strip the trailing '(Hsap)'/'(Homo sapiens)' species tag and the leading cluster code before comparing the descriptive remainder; lowercase. Pitfalls: (1) The marker-gene 'expressing ... neuron' synonym is a phenotype descriptor, not a name - exact-matching a plain cell-type name against it will fail. (2) Species-scoped to human brain (Siletti atlas) - a non-brain or non-human BioOKF cell type will have no ProvCellType counterpart. (3) Prefer CellType (CL) over ProvCellType whenever the BioOKF concept is a standard, non-cluster cell type.

spoke_nodes.label: CellLine
spoke_nodes.identifier_scheme: Cell Line Ontology CURIE, CLO prefix with UNDERSCORE form (e.g. CLO_0001164, CLO_0009442, CLO_0001206) - note underscore, not colon, unlike the other ontology labels here. Separately, n.accession_id holds the Cellosaurus accession (CVCL_xxxxx, e.g. 'CVCL_DC02','CVCL_9151') and is 100% populated in a 500-node sample. So there are TWO parallel IDs: identifier=CLO_ (primary) and accession_id=CVCL_ (Cellosaurus).
spoke_nodes.name_property: n.name holds the cell-line short name / designation as used in labs, e.g. 'LS141-1G1-65-15-1', '23B6', 'K562/Vin', 'TS2/16.2.1', 'SC-71'. Often a code, catalog-style name, or hybridoma/subclone designation rather than an English phrase.
spoke_nodes.synonyms: n.synonyms is a list of alternate line names/subclone designations, MODERATELY populated (~312/500 = ~62% in sample), e.g. 'K562/Vin' -> ['K562/VCR','K562 H-1','H-1']; 'TTDH7PV' -> ['TrichoThioDystrophy Heterozygote 7 PaVia']. Additionally n.xrefs is FULLY populated (500/500) and holds a rich list of cross-references: the CLO id, Cellosaurus CVCL, Wikidata Q-ids, catalog numbers (ATCC HB-xxxxx, RCB, TKG, ACC, ABCD), and ChEMBL cell IDs (e.g. CHEMBL4295433). Use BOTH synonyms and xrefs for matching.
data_sources: DepMap (present on ~343/2000 nodes - adds DepMap-profiled lines)
spoke_nodes.biookf_mapping: BioOKF `CellType` (subtype: cell_line). The cheatsheet's `CellType` entry explicitly includes 'line' with xref namespace CLO - exactly this label. So a BioOKF cell_line node maps here (not to SPOKE CellType, which is CL canonical types). A secondary reading: because CellLine DERIVES_FROM a Disease and HAS Variants and is a lab reagent/model, a BioOKF author could also model a physical line stock as `MaterialSample` (subtype: cell_line_stock) - but the identity/type of the line itself is `CellType` (cell_line). The disease-of-origin is a separate BioOKF `Disease` node linked by `derives_from`.
spoke_nodes.matching_notes: Richest matching surface of the six labels. Strategy in priority order: (1) xref/accession: if the BioOKF node has a Cellosaurus 'CVCL_xxxxx' xref, match n.accession_id (100% populated) or search n.xrefs; if it has a 'CLO_xxxxxxx' xref, match n.identifier. This is the most reliable because line names are noisy. (2) exact case-insensitive match of BioOKF name against n.name, then n.synonyms (~62% populated with subclone/alt names). (3) catalog numbers (ATCC/RCB/TKG/DepMap) from the BioOKF side can be matched against n.xrefs. Normalization: cell-line names are punctuation-heavy and case-sensitive in biology but often written loosely - normalize by lowercasing, collapsing spaces, and being careful with separators '/','-','.' (e.g. 'K562/Vin' vs 'K562 Vin' vs 'K562-VCR'); parent-line prefixes ('K562/...') indicate derivatives. Pitfalls: (1) SAME_CLnsCLn links duplicate/synonymous line entries - a single physical line may appear as MULTIPLE CLO nodes, so a name can match several; prefer the accession/xref to pick the canonical one and be aware of many-to-one. (2) Do NOT match generic parent-line names (e.g. 'HeLa','K562') to a specific derivative subclone. (3) Route to SPOKE CellLine (CLO) not SPOKE CellType (CL) whenever the BioOKF subtype is cell_line - the two are different labels with different ID namespaces.

spoke_nodes.label: Variant
spoke_nodes.identifier_scheme: Overwhelmingly dbSNP reference-SNP IDs (rsID). Confirmed by query: 1,038,723 of 1,044,775 nodes (99.4%) have an identifier starting with 'rs' (e.g. 'rs9675376', 'rs113488022', 'rs429358'). The remaining ~0.6% (~6,052) are un-rs-mapped variants stored as positional/HGVS-like strings 'chr:pos_ref_alt' (e.g. '10:123694303_AGTTATAAAC_A', '10:77002679:TC_T', bare '10:94433455') plus a placeholder '-'. Namespace: DBSNP (bare rsID, no CURIE prefix). No genome build stored on the node; build/allele context lives on the edges.
spoke_nodes.name_property: n.name is NULL for every Variant (confirmed keys(n) = ['identifier'] only, and n.name returned null on all sampled nodes). The rsID in n.identifier is the only human-usable label.
spoke_nodes.synonyms: None. No synonyms/aliases/xrefs property exists on the node (only 'identifier' key). Alternate identifiers (positional coordinates, ref/alt alleles, HGVS protein/cDNA changes) are carried on the relationships instead (e.g. HAS_CLnhV.Genome_Change / cDNA_Change / Protein_Change / Annotation_Transcript; ASSOCIATES_VaP.ref_allele/alt_allele; AFFECT_VaC.effect_allele), NOT on the Variant node.
data_sources: ClinVar (via ASSOCIATES_VaP r.source='ClinVar' and MAPS_VmG r.sources=['ClinVar'])
PharmGKB / PharmVar (AFFECT_VaC pharmacogenomics: level_of_evidence, PK, phenotype; BELONGS_VbH r.source='PharmVar')
CCLE/DepMap-style cell-line somatic mutation calls (HAS_CLnhV: isTCGAhotspot, isCOSMIChotspot, ExAC_AF, WES/WGS/RNAseq allele counts)

example_nodes.note: ASSOCIATES_VaP -> DOID:3969 papillary thyroid carcinoma, ClinVar, with ref_allele/alt_allele/ClinicalSignificance on edge
positional/HGVS-style identifier for a variant with no rsID (indel), FGFR2 region

participating_reltypes: ASSOCIATES_VaP (Variant->Disease, count=197185, ClinVar + GWAS Catalog; note reltype token says 'VaP' but src=Variant dst=Disease)
HAS_CLnhV (CellLine->Variant, count=179452, somatic mutation calls with consequence in variant_classification)
spoke_nodes.biookf_mapping: BioOKF `Variant` (Biomedical entity). Direct 1:1 match per SCHEMA.md cheatsheet row 'a deviation from reference: SNV, indel, CNV/SV, allele, genotype, haplotype, fusion, STR' -> type `Variant`; xref namespaces DBSNP, CLINVAR, dbVar, HGVS. Subtype is agent-coined per node: SPOKE gives no node-level subtype, but the somatic consequence on HAS_CLnhV.variant_classification (Missense_Mutation, Frame_Shift_Del/Ins, Splice_Site, Nonsense_Mutation, 5'UTR, Intron, Silent, etc.) is BioOKF variant *consequence* which SCHEMA.md §Variant-consequence explicitly says is an ATTRIBUTE (SO/VEP) on the variant, never its own node -> put on the edge/qualifier, not the subtype universe. Also note GenomicFeature -> Variant/SequenceFeature by subtype: an rsID SNP is unambiguously the Variant (deviation-from-reference) side, not SequenceFeature (which is a reference region).
spoke_nodes.matching_notes: Match a BioOKF Variant node to SPOKE Variant almost exclusively by IDENTIFIER, not name (name is null here). Strategy: (1) If the BioOKF node has a dbSNP xref/identifier, normalize to a bare lowercase-'rs' rsID (strip 'DBSNP:'/'dbSNP:' prefix, keep the number, e.g. 'DBSNP:rs429358' -> 'rs429358') and do an exact identifier lookup — this hits 99.4% of nodes. (2) For variants lacking an rsID, fall back to the positional form; but SPOKE's positional strings are inconsistent ('chr:pos_ref_alt' with both '_' and ':' separators, no 'chr' prefix, mixed indel notations like '10:77002679:TC_T') and are GRCh38 without a stated build on the node, so normalize genome build to GRCh38 and try both separator styles; this is low-yield and error-prone. (3) Do NOT try HGVS/protein-change matching against the node — those live only on edges. Pitfalls: rsIDs are versionless and can be merged/deprecated in dbSNP, so a BioOKF rsID may not resolve; the same genomic variant may exist as both an rs node and a positional node (no dedup); and never match a Variant by a gene symbol found inside a Haplotype-style string — that is the Haplotype label, not Variant.

spoke_nodes.label: Haplotype
spoke_nodes.identifier_scheme: PharmVar/PGx star-allele nomenclature. n.identifier is a gene-symbol + star-allele designation, e.g. 'CYP2A6*19', 'CYP2A6*18.003', 'CYP2C19*...', 'CYP26A1*...', 'CYP2S1*...'. The core allele is 'GENE*N' and sub-alleles add a '.NNN' suffix (e.g. 'CYP2A6*19.001'). Not a CURIE; it is the canonical PharmVar haplotype name. Every node also carries n.reference, a RefSeq genomic accession pinning the gene's reference sequence, e.g. 'NC_000019.10' (chr19, GRCh38), 'NC_000010.11', 'NC_000001.11', with a small number of nodes using the literal 'REFERENCE' for the wild-type/reference haplotype.
spoke_nodes.name_property: n.name is NULL (confirmed keys = ['reference','identifier'], n.name returned null). The star-allele string in n.identifier is the human-readable name.
spoke_nodes.synonyms: None. No synonyms/aliases property. The only extra field is n.reference (a RefSeq accession, not a synonym). Constituent variants are not listed on the node; they are reachable via Variant-[BELONGS_VbH]->Haplotype edges (each carrying reference_allele/alternative_allele/type).
data_sources: PharmVar (confirmed: Variant-[BELONGS_VbH]->Haplotype edges have r.source='PharmVar'; the star-allele nomenclature and the '.NNN' sub-allele scheme are PharmVar's)
Underlying PGx knowledge overlaps PharmGKB, which reuses PharmVar core allele definitions

example_nodes.note: sub-allele; constituent variants via BELONGS_VbH include rs1137115, rs8192725, rs4803381 (PharmVar)

participating_reltypes: BELONGS_HbG (Haplotype->Gene, count=1854 — exactly one per haplotype; e.g. CYP2A6*19 -> Gene CYP2A6 NCBIGene 1548; empty rel props)
BELONGS_VbH (Variant->Haplotype, count=7098 — the rsID/variants that define/tag the haplotype, with r.source='PharmVar', reference_allele, alternative_allele, type)
spoke_nodes.biookf_mapping: BioOKF `Variant` (Biomedical entity), subtype `haplotype` or `allele`. SCHEMA.md cheatsheet explicitly lists 'haplotype' and 'allele' as Variant subtypes ('a deviation from reference: SNV, indel, CNV/SV, allele, genotype, haplotype, fusion, STR' -> `Variant`). So SPOKE Haplotype and SPOKE Variant BOTH collapse into BioOKF `Variant`, distinguished only by agent-coined subtype (haplotype vs snv/indel). Its BELONGS_HbG->Gene edge is BioOKF `part_of`/`located_in` a Gene locus; its constituent Variants relate by member/part composition. Pharmacogenomic star alleles carry no separate BioOKF type.
spoke_nodes.matching_notes: Match a BioOKF haplotype/star-allele node to SPOKE Haplotype by exact identifier string on the star-allele name. Normalization: uppercase the gene-symbol prefix, keep the '*' and the numeric allele, and preserve the '.NNN' sub-allele suffix exactly ('CYP2A6*19' != 'CYP2A6*19.001'; the sub-allele is a distinct node). Strip any 'PharmVar:'/'PharmGKB:' prefix a BioOKF xref might carry down to the bare 'GENE*N' form. Pitfalls: (1) the reference/wild-type allele may appear with reference='REFERENCE' — handle the literal. (2) Do NOT confuse the gene-symbol prefix with a Gene node — the whole 'CYP2A6*19' string is the Haplotype identifier; use BELONGS_HbG to get the Gene. (3) Coverage is narrow: only a handful of pharmacogenes (CYP2A6, CYP2C19, CYP26A1, CYP2S1, and other CYPs) are represented, so most BioOKF star alleles (e.g. HLA, DPYD, TPMT, SLCO1B1, VKORC1) will have no SPOKE Haplotype match — expect misses rather than false matches.

spoke_nodes.label: Chromosome
spoke_nodes.identifier_scheme: UCSC-style chromosome names. n.identifier is 'chr' + name: the 22 autosomes 'chr1'..'chr22', the sex chromosomes 'chrX' and 'chrY', and the mitochondrion 'chrM' — exactly 25 nodes, enumerated in full by query. Human GRCh38/HG38 assembly (the CONTAINS_CcC edges to Cytoband carry r.build='HG38'). No CURIE, no RefSeq accession on the node.
spoke_nodes.name_property: n.name is NULL (keys = ['identifier'] only). The 'chrN' string in n.identifier is the label. (Note the numeric/letter portion after 'chr' is what most external schemes call the chromosome 'name'.)
spoke_nodes.synonyms: None. No synonyms property. There is no stored alternate naming (e.g. no bare '1'/'MT'/RefSeq NC_ accession) — only the 'chrN' identifier.
data_sources: GRCh38 / HG38 human assembly (build stamped on the CONTAINS_CcC edges to Cytoband, r.build='HG38')
participating_reltypes: CONTAINS_CcC (Chromosome->Cytoband, count=862 — every cytoband hangs off its chromosome; r.build='HG38'). This is the ONLY reltype touching Chromosome; there are no Chromosome->Gene or Chromosome->Variant edges in the schema.
spoke_nodes.biookf_mapping: No clean fit among the 28 BioOKF types — a whole chromosome is a reference genomic region, not a deviation-from-reference. It is NOT `Variant`. The nearest BioOKF slot is `SequenceFeature` (a reference genomic element; SCHEMA.md 'Variant vs SequenceFeature: region of reference = SequenceFeature'), subtype agent-coined e.g. `chromosome`, xref via a genome-region namespace. If a consumer treats a chromosome as a pure structural/positional scaffold rather than a functional feature, `Other` (with note: 'reference chromosome / genomic scaffold') is the honest fallback. Ambiguity: SPOKE uses Chromosome/Cytoband purely as a positional backbone (gene-to-band mapping), so many BioOKF pipelines will not mint a node for it at all and instead treat 'chr1' as a coordinate attribute on other nodes' edges.
spoke_nodes.matching_notes: Match by normalizing chromosome tokens to the 'chrN' form: prepend 'chr' if absent ('1' -> 'chr1'), map mitochondrial aliases 'MT'/'M'/'chrMT' -> 'chrM', keep 'X'/'Y' uppercase ('chrx' -> 'chrX'). Reject build mismatches only conceptually (SPOKE is GRCh38; a GRCh37 chromosome is still 'chr1' so the identifier matches regardless — do not over-filter). Pitfalls: only 25 canonical nodes exist — there are NO alt-contigs, no scaffolds, no patch/HLA contigs, and no bare-number or RefSeq-accession variants; any BioOKF chromosome expressed as 'NC_000001.11' or '1' must be normalized to 'chr1' before lookup or it will miss.

spoke_nodes.label: Cytoband
spoke_nodes.identifier_scheme: ISCN cytogenetic band designations. n.identifier = chromosome-number + arm (p/q) + band(.sub-band), e.g. '1p36.33', '1p36.32', '7q11.21', '1q22'. 862 bands total (standard human ideogram at GRCh38 resolution). Each node also stores genomic coordinates: n.startpos and n.endpos as 0-based integer base positions on that chromosome (e.g. 1p36.33 = 0..2,300,000; 7q11.21 = 62,100,000..67,500,000), i.e. GRCh38 coordinates (the parent Chromosome's CONTAINS_CcC edge is r.build='HG38'). Not a CURIE.
spoke_nodes.name_property: n.name is NULL (keys = ['startpos','endpos','identifier']). The ISCN band string in n.identifier is the label. The chromosome part is embedded in the identifier (the '1' in '1p36.33'), NOT prefixed with 'chr'.
spoke_nodes.synonyms: None. No synonyms property. The extra fields are numeric coordinates (startpos/endpos), not aliases. The parent chromosome is obtained via Chromosome-[CONTAINS_CcC]->Cytoband, and the genes located in the band via Gene-[CONTAINS_CcG]->Cytoband.
data_sources: ISCN / UCSC cytoBand ideogram (standard human cytogenetic band naming and coordinates)
GRCh38 / HG38 assembly (parent Chromosome CONTAINS_CcC edge r.build='HG38'; startpos/endpos are GRCh38 coordinates)
Ensembl HG38 (gene-to-band mapping: Gene-[CONTAINS_CcG]->Cytoband edges carry r.source='Ensembl HG38')

example_nodes.note: contains genes RNF223, OR4F29, OR4F16 via Gene-[CONTAINS_CcG]->Cytoband

participating_reltypes: CONTAINS_CcC (Chromosome->Cytoband, count=862 — each band's parent chromosome, r.build='HG38')
CONTAINS_CcG (Gene->Cytoband, count=19696 — cytogenetic location of genes; r.source='Ensembl HG38'; note reltype name 'CcG' but direction is Gene(src)->Cytoband(dst))
spoke_nodes.biookf_mapping: No dedicated BioOKF type — a cytoband is a reference genomic region (a coordinate interval), not a deviation-from-reference, so NOT `Variant`. Closest is `SequenceFeature` (subtype agent-coined e.g. `cytoband` or `chromosome_band`; SCHEMA.md: 'region of reference = SequenceFeature'), representing the karyotypic locus interval [startpos,endpos] on its chromosome. Alternatively `Concept` (subtype `classification`/`ontology_term`) if a consumer treats the band purely as a cytogenetic label rather than a physical feature. Ambiguity: because a cytoband is really positional metadata, many BioOKF ingests will express it as a `located_in`/`part_of` qualifier (a gene's cytogenetic location edge to its chromosome) rather than minting a standalone node.
spoke_nodes.matching_notes: Match by exact ISCN band string after normalization: lowercase the arm letter (p/q), strip any leading 'chr' if a BioOKF node writes 'chr1p36.33' -> '1p36.33' (SPOKE has NO 'chr' prefix on cytobands, only the bare number), and preserve the '.subband' precisely ('1p36' vs '1p36.33' are different-resolution nodes — SPOKE stores the fine sub-band, so a coarse '1p36' will miss). To match by coordinates instead of name, use startpos/endpos as a GRCh38 interval and test containment; convert build if the BioOKF node is GRCh37. Pitfalls: (1) do not confuse the chromosome prefix inside the band with a Chromosome node ('1p36.33' band vs 'chr1' chromosome — link via CONTAINS_CcC). (2) Coordinates are 0-based half-open UCSC-style; do not treat startpos as 1-based. (3) Only canonical p/q bands for chr1-22,X,Y exist (862 total); acrocentric-arm or non-standard bands may be absent.

spoke_nodes.label: Pathway
spoke_nodes.identifier_scheme: Heterogeneous, source-dependent — NOT a single namespace. Four flavors observed: (a) WikiPathways accession, bare WPxxxx string, e.g. "WP5064"; (b) Reactome, CURIE-like "reactome:R-HSA-<n>", e.g. "reactome:R-HSA-1059683"; (c) MetaCyc pathway frame ID, e.g. "HSERMETANA-PWY" or "PWY-4361"; (d) KEGG, a human-readable label string with a numeric suffix rather than a code, e.g. "Glycan biosynthesis - 2", "Energy metabolism - 1". Distribution (by sources array): metacyc 3139, WikiPathways 880, Reactome 797, kegg 633.
spoke_nodes.name_property: n.name holds the full pathway title (free text), e.g. "Interleukin-6 signaling", "Constitutive androstane receptor pathway", "L-methionine biosynthesis III". PITFALL: MetaCyc-sourced names embed HTML/entity markup, e.g. "S-methyl-5-thio-α-D-ribose 1-phosphate degradation I" — must strip tags and decode entities before matching.
spoke_nodes.synonyms: n.synonyms exists ONLY on Reactome-sourced Pathway nodes (property set name/identifier/synonyms/reactome_id/version/sources). It is a list but is typically just [name] (echoes the name); low added value. WikiPathways/MetaCyc/KEGG Pathway nodes have NO synonyms property (keys are name/identifier/sources/license/url). No cross-source alias field.
spoke_nodes.biookf_mapping: BioOKF `BiologicalPathway` with subtype `pathway` (or `signaling` for Reactome signaling nodes). This is the canonical 'pathway' bucket in the cheatsheet (row: 'a pathway, reaction, signaling cascade... -> BiologicalPathway; namespaces GO, REACT, KEGG, WIKIPATHWAYS, RHEA'). No ambiguity at the type level — Pathway never maps to BiologicalFunction (that is MolecularFunction/GO-MF). Note overlap with Reaction and BiologicalProcess which also map to BiologicalPathway but by different subtypes (reaction / go_bp).
spoke_nodes.matching_notes: Match a BioOKF BiologicalPathway (subtype pathway/signaling) NAME to n.name. Strategy: (1) if the BioOKF xref is a WikiPathways WP id, Reactome R-HSA id, KEGG, or MetaCyc frame, match directly on n.identifier (normalize Reactome to 'reactome:'+id; strip any 'WikiPathways:' prefix to bare WPxxxx). (2) Otherwise match on name: lowercase, collapse whitespace, and for MetaCyc nodes FIRST strip HTML tags (...) and decode HTML entities (α->alpha, β->beta) — otherwise greek-letter and italic markup will block exact matches. (3) KEGG identifiers are themselves descriptive strings with a ' - N' suffix; strip the suffix when comparing to a plain pathway name. Pitfalls: many pathway titles are Roman-numeral-versioned ("... III") — keep the numeral; do not confuse a Pathway with an EC 'reaction' string or a Reaction equation. Reactome synonyms just echo the name, so searching them adds nothing.

spoke_nodes.label: BiologicalProcess
spoke_nodes.identifier_scheme: Gene Ontology CURIE, GO:<7-digit>, e.g. "GO:0048219", "GO:0042117". Uniform — every node is a GO Biological Process term. No mixing with other ontologies.
spoke_nodes.name_property: n.name is the full GO term label (lowercase free text), e.g. "monocyte activation", "inter-Golgi cisterna vesicle-mediated transport", "regulation of translation at presynapse". This is the primary human-readable field.
spoke_nodes.synonyms: The `synonyms` property key does NOT exist on these nodes. A `description` property exists but is a verbatim duplicate of `name` (queried: 0 nodes where description <> name), so it carries NO extra alias content. Effectively NO synonym/alias field is populated — matching must rely on the GO id or the exact name.
data_sources: Gene Ontology (source = "Gene Ontology"); license CC BY 4.0
spoke_nodes.biookf_mapping: BioOKF `BiologicalPathway` with subtype `go_bp` (cheatsheet: 'GO biological process ... -> BiologicalPathway'; and the boundary rule 'a process = BiologicalPathway'). Explicitly NOT BiologicalFunction — that is reserved for GO Molecular Function (the MolecularFunction label). One-to-one, unambiguous type mapping.
spoke_nodes.matching_notes: Match a BioOKF BiologicalPathway (subtype go_bp / physiologic / pathologic / behavior) to this label. Best key: if the BioOKF node has a GO xref, match directly on n.identifier (both use GO:####### form). By name: lowercase and collapse whitespace — GO labels are already lowercase; watch for comma-qualified names ("regulation of translation at presynapse, modulating synaptic transmission") which are distinct terms from the un-qualified parent. Since there are NO synonyms in SPOKE, a BioOKF node whose name is a known GO synonym (not the primary label) will FAIL to match here — resolve the synonym to the canonical GO label via an external GO synonym table first. Do not route GO Molecular Function terms here (they live in MolecularFunction).

spoke_nodes.label: MolecularFunction
spoke_nodes.identifier_scheme: Gene Ontology CURIE, GO:<7-digit>, e.g. "GO:0016784", "GO:0030246" — the GO Molecular Function sub-ontology. Same namespace format as BiologicalProcess; the two are disambiguated only by the SPOKE label, not by id pattern.
spoke_nodes.name_property: n.name is the full GO-MF term label, an '...activity'/'...binding' phrase, e.g. "3-mercaptopyruvate sulfurtransferase activity", "biotin transmembrane transporter activity", "carbohydrate binding".
spoke_nodes.synonyms: No `synonyms` property present. `description` exists but duplicates `name` (same as BiologicalProcess), so no extra aliases. Matching relies on GO id or exact name.
data_sources: Gene Ontology (source = "Gene Ontology"); license CC BY 4.0
spoke_nodes.biookf_mapping: BioOKF `BiologicalFunction` with subtype `catalytic` / `binding` / `transporter` (cheatsheet: 'a molecular function (catalytic / binding / transporter activity) -> BiologicalFunction; namespace GO (MF)'; boundary rule 'an elemental molecular activity (GO-MF) = BiologicalFunction'). This is the ONLY SPOKE label of the six that maps to BiologicalFunction rather than BiologicalPathway. Unambiguous.
spoke_nodes.matching_notes: Match a BioOKF BiologicalFunction (GO-MF) here, NOT to BiologicalProcess. Best key: GO xref -> n.identifier direct match. By name: lowercase, collapse whitespace; GO-MF labels almost always end in 'activity' or are '<X> binding' — use that as a disambiguator against BiologicalProcess. No synonyms in SPOKE, so a BioOKF name that is a GO-MF synonym must be canonicalized to the primary GO label externally before matching. Pitfall: the same underlying enzyme concept can appear as an EC name (e.g. 'alpha,alpha-trehalase') and as a GO-MF ('trehalase activity') — these are DIFFERENT nodes/labels; do not collapse EC into MolecularFunction.

spoke_nodes.label: Reaction
spoke_nodes.identifier_scheme: Source-dependent, three flavors: (a) KEGG reaction id "R#####", e.g. "R13147", "R04184" (15677 nodes); (b) MetaCyc reaction frame id "RXN-#####", e.g. "RXN-15029" (10659 nodes); (c) Reactome reaction/event CURIE "reactome:R-HSA-<n>", e.g. "reactome:R-HSA-1254285" (4851 nodes).
spoke_nodes.name_property: n.name varies by source. KEGG: an enzyme-name-plus-equation string, e.g. "globoside N-acetylhexosaminohydrolase; alpha-D-Galactosyl-(1->4)-... <=> Globoside + H2O", or a simple "A <=> B" ("Prefumagillin <=> Fumagillin"). Reactome: a descriptive event name, e.g. "ERBB4s80:STAT5A complex translocates to the nucleus", "ERBB4s80:STAT5A binds CSN2 gene promoter". MetaCyc: name is frequently NULL (only the RXN-##### identifier is present) — a major matching pitfall. No synonyms field on any Reaction node (keys = sources/identifier/name only).
spoke_nodes.synonyms: No synonyms/aliases property at all (keys are just sources, identifier, name). MetaCyc reactions often have name=null too, so many nodes are matchable ONLY by their source-native id.
