spoke_nodes.biookf_mapping: BioOKF `BiologicalPathway` with subtype `reaction` (cheatsheet: 'a pathway, reaction, signaling cascade... -> BiologicalPathway; namespaces ... KEGG, RHEA'). Shares the BiologicalPathway type with SPOKE Pathway (subtype pathway) and BiologicalProcess (subtype go_bp); distinguish by subtype. NOTE the participants (Compound consumed/produced) map to BioOKF Molecule via `converts_to`/`participates_in` edges, but the Reaction node itself is BiologicalPathway, not Molecule.
spoke_nodes.matching_notes: Prefer id-based matching: KEGG R##### -> n.identifier; MetaCyc RXN-##### -> n.identifier; Reactome R-HSA -> 'reactome:'+id. Name matching is UNRELIABLE for Reaction: (1) ~10k MetaCyc nodes have name=null (cannot name-match at all); (2) KEGG names are compound 'enzyme; equation' strings — split on ';' and on '<=>' to isolate substrates/products or the enzyme name; equations use ASCII arrows (<=>, ->) and salt/stereo prefixes (alpha-, beta-, D-, L-). If a BioOKF node is really a chemical conversion, consider matching its reactants/products to Compound and traversing CONSUMES/PRODUCES rather than string-matching the Reaction name. Pitfall: Reactome 'reaction' names are prose event descriptions (binding/translocation events), not chemical equations — treat them as event labels.

spoke_nodes.label: EC
spoke_nodes.identifier_scheme: Enzyme Commission number, dotted 4-level code class.subclass.subsubclass.serial, e.g. "3.1.7.2", "1.14.14.85", "2.3.1.183". Higher-level (partial) EC codes also exist as nodes, e.g. "5.5.1" (a sub-subclass parent). Components are exposed as separate string properties: class, subclass, subsubclass, serial.
spoke_nodes.name_property: n.name is the accepted/recommended enzyme name, e.g. "alpha,alpha-trehalase", "phosphinothricin acetyltransferase", "guanosine-3',5'-bis(diphosphate) 3'-diphosphatase". PITFALL: for unnamed/incompletely-characterized entries n.name is the bare EC number itself (queried: 489 nodes where name == identifier, e.g. "4.2.1.71").
spoke_nodes.synonyms: Synonyms live in n.aliases (NOT n.synonyms). It is a SINGLE STRING with '; '-delimited alternative names, e.g. "guanosine-3',5'-bis(diphosphate) 3'-pyrophosphatase; PpGpp-3'-pyrophosphohydrolase; PpGpp phosphohydrolase". Populated on 6775 of 8679 nodes (~78%). Aliases may carry annotations like '(gene name)', '(incorrect)', '(ambiguous)' that must be stripped. Must split on '; ' to get individual aliases.
data_sources: ExplorEnz (source = "ExplorEnz", the official IUBMB Enzyme Nomenclature DB)
spoke_nodes.biookf_mapping: Ambiguous — no perfect single BioOKF type. Best fit: `BiologicalFunction` (subtype `catalytic`) since an EC number denotes an enzymatic catalytic activity, closely parallel to GO-MF catalytic activities. Defensible alternative: `MolecularClass` (subtype `enzyme_class` / `protein_family`) because an EC number is a grouping/classification that many proteins are members_of (HAS_PhEC has 5.25M protein edges — it behaves like a class proteins belong to). Partial EC codes ("5.5.1") are pure classification nodes and lean `MolecularClass`/`Concept`. Recommend: leaf EC (catalytic activity of a defined enzyme) -> BiologicalFunction/catalytic; upper-level EC codes -> MolecularClass. It is NOT a Molecule and NOT a Pathway.
spoke_nodes.matching_notes: Primary key: the EC number. If a BioOKF node has an EC xref (e.g. 'EC 3.2.1.28' or 'ec:3.2.1.28'), normalize to the dotted code and match n.identifier exactly. By name: match the BioOKF enzyme name against n.name AND against each '; '-split token of n.aliases (lowercase, collapse whitespace). When splitting aliases, STRIP trailing qualifiers in parentheses ('(gene name)', '(incorrect)', '(ambiguous)') and drop clearly-flagged '(incorrect)' aliases to avoid false positives. Pitfalls: (1) 489 EC nodes have name == the bare number — name-matching those is impossible, use the code; (2) an alias may actually be a GENE NAME (e.g. 'CYP72A224 (gene name)') — do not use it to match a Gene node; (3) the same enzyme concept exists separately as a GO-MF '...activity' node in MolecularFunction — decide target label by whether the BioOKF node is coded by EC number (->EC) or by GO id (->MolecularFunction). Greek/stereo prefixes (alpha,alpha-; D-; L-) appear in names and must be normalized consistently.

spoke_nodes.label: PwGroup
spoke_nodes.identifier_scheme: Reactome CURIE "reactome:R-HSA-<n>", e.g. "reactome:R-HSA-179842", "reactome:R-HSA-9674862". Same id namespace as Reactome Pathway/Reaction nodes — disambiguated only by the SPOKE label. The bare Reactome id is also stored in n.reactome_id.
spoke_nodes.name_property: n.name is a Reactome physical-entity / complex / entity-set name, typically colon-joined subunit list, e.g. "ADAM:Zn2+", "EGFR:AAMP", "EGF-like ligands:EGFR dimer", "EGFR:FAM83B,(FAM83A, FAM83D)". These are macromolecular COMPLEXES / entity sets, NOT pathways or processes despite the label name.
spoke_nodes.synonyms: n.synonyms is populated (a list). Usually just [name], but can carry a longer descriptive alias, e.g. for "ADAM:Zn2+" synonyms = ["ADAM:Zn2+", "ADAM metalloprotease:Zinc cofactor"]. Worth searching for the human-readable expanded form.
spoke_nodes.biookf_mapping: Ambiguous and often mis-suggested by the label name. Semantically a PwGroup is a Reactome physical-entity SET / macromolecular COMPLEX (verified: proteins EGFR + AAMP are PARTOF the group 'EGFR:AAMP'). Best BioOKF fits: (a) `Molecule` with subtype `complex` when the group is a defined molecular complex of proteins/compounds (matches cheatsheet 'complex' subtype under Molecule); or (b) `MolecularClass` (subtype gene_set/entity_set) when it is an entity SET / grouping (e.g. 'EGFR:FAM83B,(FAM83A, FAM83D)' listing alternative members). It is NOT a BiologicalPathway despite 'Pw' in the name — do NOT map it like SPOKE Pathway. Members attach via BioOKF `part_of` / `member_of`.
spoke_nodes.matching_notes: Do NOT treat PwGroup as a pathway. Primary key: Reactome id -> match n.identifier / n.reactome_id (both 'reactome:R-HSA-n' and bare 'R-HSA-n' forms). By name: the name is a ':'-joined subunit expression, not a natural phrase — split on ':' and ',' to recover component tokens (protein symbols / compound names / 'Zn2+') and match those components to Protein/Compound/Gene nodes via the PARTOF edges rather than string-matching the whole complex name. Search n.synonyms for the expanded human-readable form (e.g. 'ADAM metalloprotease:Zinc cofactor'). Pitfalls: (1) many synonyms just echo the terse name (no extra info); (2) same 'reactome:R-HSA-*' id space collides with Reactome Pathway and Reaction — always confirm via the SPOKE label before mapping; (3) a BioOKF node named after a single protein should map to Protein/Molecule, not to a PwGroup complex that merely contains it.

spoke_nodes.label: Organism
spoke_nodes.identifier_scheme: Two co-existing schemes keyed off NCBI Taxonomy. (1) ncbi-taxonomy nodes (60,587): bare NCBITaxon integer as a string, e.g. n.identifier='9606' (Homo sapiens), '562' (Escherichia coli), '1773' (Mycobacterium tuberculosis), '1280' (Staphylococcus aureus). (2) BV-BRC genome nodes (357,630): a composite '<NCBItaxon>.<genome_id>' decimal-looking string, e.g. '39491.58', '470.2143' — the integer part before the dot is the parent NCBITaxon id and the fractional part is the BV-BRC genome accession. No CURIE prefix is ever present (it is NOT 'NCBITaxon:9606', just '9606'). Prefix with 'NCBITaxon:' when emitting an xref.
spoke_nodes.name_property: n.name holds the organism's scientific name. For ncbi-taxonomy nodes it is a clean binomial/label ('Homo sapiens', 'Escherichia coli', 'SARS coronavirus Tor2'). For BV-BRC strain nodes the value is wrapped in literal double-quote characters and includes 'strain <id>', e.g. n.name='"[Eubacterium] rectale strain AF24-17"' — the surrounding double quotes are part of the stored string and must be stripped before matching.
spoke_nodes.synonyms: NONE. There is no synonyms/aliases/xrefs/common_name/synonym/mesh_list property on any Organism node (verified: 0 of 418,217 nodes carry any such key). Organisms have exactly one name string. The only 'alias' signal is incidental: BV-BRC strain names sometimes embed a legacy/basionym in brackets (e.g. '[Eubacterium] rectale' for taxon 39491 whose species node is named 'Agathobacter rectalis'), but this is not a structured synonym field.

participating_reltypes: ISA_OiO (Organism->Organism, taxonomic hierarchy; strain ISA species)
MEASURES_CLmO (ClinicalLab->Organism, incoming; LOINC lab test measures organism)
spoke_nodes.biookf_mapping: Direct, unambiguous 1:1 map to BioOKF type 'Organism' (cheatsheet row: 'a species, strain, pathogen, microbe' -> Organism, namespace NCBITaxon). subtype should be derived from n.level: level='species' -> subtype 'species'; level='strain' (the dominant level, 377,775 nodes) -> subtype 'strain'; any pathogenic microbe with a CAUSES_OcD edge or disease property could be tagged subtype 'pathogen'. Higher taxonomic ranks (genus, family, order, class, phylum, superkingdom, etc.) also present and still map to Organism (SPEC treats any taxon as Organism). Boundary reminder from SCHEMA.md: a group of PEOPLE is Population and an investigation is Study — never Organism; only a taxon/species/strain is Organism. xref should be emitted as NCBITaxon:<integer> (use the integer part before any dot for BV-BRC composite ids).
spoke_nodes.matching_notes: Match a BioOKF Organism node to this label by (a) NCBITaxon id if available: strip any 'NCBITaxon:' prefix and match the bare integer against n.identifier for ncbi-taxonomy nodes, or against the integer prefix (STARTS WITH '<id>.') for BV-BRC strain nodes — the species-level node carries the bare integer, strains carry '<id>.<genome>'. (b) By name: normalize before matching — lowercase, strip surrounding literal double-quotes (BV-BRC), collapse the ' strain <id>' / ' str. <id>' suffix, normalize whitespace/hyphens, and handle 'subsp.'/'subspecies' and 'sp.' abbreviations. Prefer the ncbi-taxonomy node (clean binomial) for species-level matches. PITFALLS: (1) No synonym field exists, so a query name that is a legacy basionym or common name (e.g. 'Eubacterium rectale', 'human', 'colon bacillus') will NOT match the current scientific name ('Agathobacter rectalis', 'Homo sapiens', 'Escherichia coli') — resolve common/legacy names to an NCBITaxon id externally first. (2) The same underlying taxon appears as BOTH a clean species node (ncbi-taxonomy) and many quote-wrapped strain nodes (BV-BRC) sharing the taxon-id prefix; dedupe by taxon integer. (3) SARS-CoV-2 (NCBITaxon 2697049) is ABSENT from Organism (returns nothing), though SARS-CoV-1-era taxa like 'SARS coronavirus Tor2' (227984) are present — do not assume COVID-19 virus coverage here. (4) BV-BRC strain names contain literal embedded double-quote characters that will break naive exact-string equality.

spoke_nodes.identifier_scheme: FOODON CURIE (Food Ontology term ID), always the 'FOODON:' prefix followed by an 8-digit zero-padded number. spoke_nodes.name_property: n.name holds a lowercase descriptive food label, often with a parenthetical preparation/state qualifier, matching the FOODON term label. Examples: 'imitation grape-flavored apple juice', 'lychee (canned)', 'liver (cooked)', 'kiwifruit (peeled, raw)'. Not a symbol or scientific name; it is the human-readable ontology label.
spoke_nodes.synonyms: NO dedicated synonyms/aliases/xrefs property exists. keys(n) union over samples = [name, source, identifier, subset_list] only. subset_list carries FooDB food codes (e.g. ['F4550'], ['F3689']) not lexical synonyms. To find alternate names you must rely on the ISA_FiF food hierarchy or the single canonical name; there is no alias field to search.

spoke_nodes.biookf_mapping: Maps directly and unambiguously to BioOKF type Food (SCHEMA.md cheatsheet: 'a food item, food group, dietary product' -> Food, subtype food_item/food_group/dietary_product, xref namespaces FooDB, FOODON). The FOODON CURIE goes straight into the BioOKF xref. Note the boundary rule (SPEC §5.D): a dietary-pattern EXPOSURE (e.g. 'Mediterranean diet') is Exposure not Food, but SPOKE Food nodes are concrete food items/products, so they are Food. subset_list Fxxxx = FooDB xref.
spoke_nodes.matching_notes: Match a BioOKF Food node NAME to this label by string-matching n.name (the FOODON label). Normalize: lowercase both sides; the SPOKE name frequently carries a parenthetical state/prep qualifier (e.g. '(canned)','(raw)','(cooked)'), so try (a) exact lowercase match, then (b) strip the trailing parenthetical and match the base food term, then (c) match against ISA_FiF parents which are the generic 'X food product' rollups (e.g. 'kiwifruit food product' is the hub for kiwifruit variants). If the BioOKF node carries a FOODON xref, match on identifier directly — this is the most reliable path since every node is a FOODON CURIE. Pitfalls: NO synonyms field, so brand/common-name variants (e.g. 'garbanzo' vs 'chickpea') will miss unless both resolve to the same FOODON term; hyphenation and comma-vs-parenthesis ordering differ ('Tomato, sundried' appears on edge food_name but node name is 'tomato ...'); do not confuse a food item with a DietarySupplement/Blend brand product (those are NHANES commercial products, integer IDs, not FOODON).

spoke_nodes.biookf_mapping: Ambiguous / no clean 1:1. A branded multi-ingredient supplement PRODUCT is not a single biomedical entity. Best BioOKF fit is Food with subtype 'dietary_product' (SCHEMA.md cheatsheet explicitly lists 'dietary product' under Food). spoke_nodes.matching_notes: Matching a BioOKF node NAME to a DietarySupplement is brand-string matching, not ontology matching. Normalize: uppercase or case-fold both sides (SPOKE names are ALL-CAPS); strip trailing dose tokens ('150 MG','1000 MCG','1300 MG') and unit words. There is NO synonyms field and NO CURIE, so you cannot resolve by identifier from an external ontology — the integer id is DSLD-internal and won't appear in a BioOKF xref. Match strategy: (1) if the BioOKF node is an ingredient/active (vitamin D, fish oil, biotin), do NOT match it here — match its Compound instead and traverse CONTAINS_DScC back to supplements; (2) only match at the DietarySupplement level when the BioOKF node is itself a named commercial product. Pitfalls: many names embed the ingredient ('OREGANO OIL 150 MG', 'FISH OIL 1300 MG'), tempting false matches to an ingredient concept — these are products, not the substance; product_type 'Generic'/'Default'/'Regular' and supplement_type 'Standard'/'Prenatal'/'Infant\/pediatric'/'Mature' are categorical filters, not names.

spoke_nodes.label: ClinicalLab
spoke_nodes.identifier_scheme: Predominantly LOINC codes in the numeric 'code-check' format (n.identifier = e.g. '27858-0', '20430-5', '82505-9', '2251-7'). A minority are UMLS/LOINC hierarchy class codes in the 'MTHU' namespace (e.g. 'MTHU000001' = 'Laboratory Class', 'MTHU000005' = 'Antibiotic susceptibilities') used as parent/ISA grouping nodes. So: mostly LOINC lab-test codes, plus a handful of UMLS MTHU LOINC-class codes. Confirmed by query: `MATCH (n:ClinicalLab) WHERE NOT n.identifier =~ '[0-9]+-[0-9]' RETURN n.identifier` returns MTHU* codes.
spoke_nodes.name_property: n.name holds the full LOINC Fully-Specified Name (the 6-part colon-delimited LOINC string): Component:Property:Time:System:Scale:Method, e.g. 'Lutropin^7th specimen post XXX challenge:ACnc:Pt:Ser/Plas:Qn', 'pH:LsCnc:Pt:BldMV:SemiQn', 'Estriol:MCnc:Pt:Ser/Plas:Qn'. For MTHU class nodes it is a plain label ('Laboratory Class').
spoke_nodes.synonyms: No dedicated synonyms/aliases property. The closest human-readable alias is n.component_names (the analyte/component text, e.g. 'Estriol', 'Norfentanyl', 'pH', 'Lutropin^7th specimen post XXX challenge'), which is populated on essentially all lab-test nodes. n.systems / n.system_names carry the specimen/system (pipe-delimited LOINC part codes and their names, e.g. systems='LP7576-4|LP7479-1|LP7567-3', system_names='Ser/Plas'). components carries pipe-delimited LOINC part (LP) codes.
data_sources: LOINC (implied by LOINC code + LOINC part LP-code structure; n.source and n.sources are null on ClinicalLab nodes)

example_nodes.name: Antibiotic susceptibilities
example_nodes.note: UMLS MTHU LOINC-class grouping node used in ISA_CLiCL hierarchy

spoke_nodes.biookf_mapping: Primary map: BioOKF `BiomedicalMeasure` (subtype `lab_test`) — a ClinicalLab node is a LOINC lab test, exactly the SCHEMA.md cheatsheet row 'a measurable variable: lab test, vital, score... -> BiomedicalMeasure ... LOINC, NCIT, OBA, EFO'. Ambiguity: the MTHU 'class' nodes and some assay-oriented entries (e.g. antibiotic susceptibility, culture) are closer to BioOKF `MethodOrProcedure` (subtype `lab_assay`/`diagnostic`; SNOMEDCT/CPT/NCIT/OBI). Also the MEASURES_* edges make ClinicalLab the natural SPOKE anchor for a BioOKF `measures` predicate whose object is a Compound/Protein/Anatomy.
spoke_nodes.matching_notes: To match a BioOKF `BiomedicalMeasure` node named like a lab test to ClinicalLab: (1) If the BioOKF node carries a LOINC identifier, match directly on n.identifier (LOINC code, e.g. '2251-7'). (2) Otherwise match the analyte against n.component_names, NOT n.name — n.name is the full colon-delimited LOINC FSN and will almost never equal a plain analyte string. Normalize: lowercase, strip the LOINC modifier suffix after '^' (e.g. 'Lutropin^7th specimen...' -> 'lutropin'), and be aware many components have Greek letters / hyphens ('3-Hydroxyglutarate'). (3) A single analyte (e.g. 'Estriol') maps to MANY ClinicalLab rows (serum vs urine, quantitative vs qualitative, different methods) — expect one-to-many; disambiguate on system_names (specimen) and the property/scale tokens in n.name. Pitfall: the same analyte also exists as a SPOKE Compound (linked via MEASURES_CLmC, target id 'inchikey:...'); do not confuse the measurement (ClinicalLab) with the substance (Compound). Pitfall: n.source/n.sources are null, so you cannot filter by source.

spoke_nodes.label: SDoH
spoke_nodes.identifier_scheme: Two distinct schemes. (a) SNOMED CT concept CURIEs prefixed 'SNOMED_' (e.g. 'SNOMED_611531000124109' Housing insecurity, 'SNOMED_275972003' Cholesterol screening) — 364/1515 nodes. (b) The majority (1151/1515) are AHRQ/agency measure codes: opaque uppercase underscore-delimited variable names, e.g. 'AHRQ_ACS_AVG_HH_SIZE', 'AHRQ_ACS_GINI_INDEX', 'AHRQ_ACS_MDN_OWNER_COST_MORTGAGE'. Confirmed by scheme-split query (SNOMED=364, other=1151).
spoke_nodes.name_property: n.name is the human-readable label. For SNOMED nodes it is the SNOMED preferred term with its semantic tag in parentheses, e.g. 'Housing insecurity (finding)', 'Personal care disability (finding)', 'Cholesterol screening (procedure)', 'Transportation insecurity (finding)'. For AHRQ measure nodes n.name is identical to the opaque identifier (e.g. name='AHRQ_ACS_GINI_INDEX'), i.e. NOT human-friendly.
spoke_nodes.synonyms: No synonyms/aliases property. Cross-reference is via n.mesh_ids (list of MeSH descriptor IDs, e.g. ['D000091003']); populated on roughly 86/300 sampled nodes (~29%), so partially populated. n.description holds a free-text definition but is populated only on a minority (e.g. Transportation insecurity has one; most are null).
data_sources: SNOMED CT (sources=['SNOMED CT'] on the SNOMED-CURIE nodes)

AHRQ SDOH Database and many US federal/agency survey sources recorded in n.data_source: ACS (American Community Survey), AHRF (Area Health Resources File), SEDA, CRDC, OPP, BRFSS, NCHS, Census, EPA, NOAA, etc. (n.data_source has ~70 distinct values)

example_nodes.name: Transportation insecurity (finding)
example_nodes.description: A condition in which one is unable to regularly move from place to place...

participating_reltypes: ASSOCIATES_SaD (SDoH->Disease; e.g. Housing insecurity -> COVID-19 (DOID:0080600), asthma (DOID:2841))
spoke_nodes.biookf_mapping: BioOKF `SocialFactor` — the SCHEMA.md alias table maps `SDOH`/`SDoH` -> `SocialFactor` explicitly. Subtypes from the cheatsheet: `economic`/`education`/`housing`/`healthcare_access`/`social_support` (e.g. Housing insecurity -> housing; Gini/median-income measures -> economic; cholesterol/cancer screening -> healthcare_access). Ambiguity: SNOMED '(procedure)' screening entries (e.g. 'Cholesterol screening (procedure)') straddle BioOKF `MethodOrProcedure` (screening) vs `SocialFactor` (healthcare access) — SPOKE lumps them under SDoH; classify by intent. Source recommendation on cheatsheet: 'Biolink SDoH, local'.
spoke_nodes.matching_notes: To match a BioOKF `SocialFactor` to SDoH: (1) If the BioOKF node has a SNOMED code, match on n.identifier by stripping the 'SNOMED_' prefix and comparing the numeric concept id. (2) For name matching against SNOMED nodes, strip the trailing semantic tag '(finding)'/'(procedure)'/'(situation)' from n.name before comparing, and lowercase (e.g. 'Housing insecurity (finding)' -> 'housing insecurity'). (3) The ~1151 AHRQ measure nodes have opaque names==identifiers ('AHRQ_ACS_...') that will NOT surface via natural-language name search — do not expect a BioOKF concept like 'income inequality' to string-match 'AHRQ_ACS_GINI_INDEX'; you must map semantically or via a curated crosswalk, or fall back to mesh_ids where present. (4) Use n.mesh_ids to bridge when a BioOKF node carries a MeSH id. Pitfall: many SDoH nodes are US-specific administrative measures with no clean ontology anchor; false matches are easy if you only substring-match on tokens like 'income' or 'poverty'.

spoke_nodes.label: Environment
spoke_nodes.identifier_scheme: OBO ontology CURIEs with underscore separator: mostly ENVO (Environment Ontology) IDs, e.g. 'ENVO_01000405' (respirable suspended particulate matter), 'ENVO_01000415' (fine respirable suspended particulate matter), 'ENVO_00010505' (aerosol); plus a few upper-level BFO (Basic Formal Ontology) IDs used as ancestors, e.g. 'BFO_0000001' (entity), 'BFO_0000002' (continuant), 'BFO_0000040' (material entity). Only 11 nodes total, all retrieved.
spoke_nodes.name_property: n.name is the ENVO/BFO ontology label (lowercase natural-language term): 'respirable suspended particulate matter', 'fine respirable suspended particulate matter', 'aerosol', 'environmental material', 'material entity', 'continuant', 'entity'.
spoke_nodes.synonyms: n.synonyms is a list and IS populated for the leaf pollution terms with the epidemiologically-standard abbreviations: ENVO_01000405 synonyms=['PM10'], ENVO_01000415 synonyms=['PM2.5'], ENVO_01000814 (aerosolised solids)... ; ENVO_00010483 synonyms=['portion of environmental material'], ENVO_01001089 synonyms=['solid aerosol']. Upper-ontology BFO nodes have empty synonyms=[]. n.mesh_ids also present (list): ENVO_01000405 has mesh_ids=['D052638'] (Particulate Matter); most others empty.
data_sources: Environment Ontology (ENVO) — n.sources=['Environment Ontology'] on all 11 nodes (BFO ancestors are imported into ENVO and also carry sources=['Environment Ontology'])
spoke_nodes.biookf_mapping: BioOKF `Exposure`, subtype `environmental` — the cheatsheet row 'a behavioral/environmental/occupational/dietary exposure -> Exposure ... ECTO, ExO' and 'Exposure vs SocialFactor vs Food: environmental exposure = Exposure'. The recommended sources are ECTO/ExO but SPOKE uses ENVO here; still an environmental-exposure concept (air pollution / particulate matter). Note the alias table also lists BioOKF `ExposureOrFactor` -> Exposure/SocialFactor/Food/Population/GeographicLocation as a coarse bucket. Upper BFO nodes (entity, continuant, material entity) are pure ontology scaffolding and map to `Other` (or should be dropped) rather than a real Exposure.
spoke_nodes.matching_notes: Tiny label (11 nodes), all air-pollution/particulate ENVO terms plus BFO scaffolding. To match a BioOKF `Exposure` (environmental): (1) match on ENVO id if the BioOKF node carries one. (2) The most useful matching field is n.synonyms — the pollution shorthand 'PM2.5'/'PM10' lives there, not in n.name; so an environmental-exposure concept named 'PM2.5' matches ENVO_01000415 only via synonyms. Normalize case and the '.'/'.'-vs-'.' in 'PM2.5'. (3) n.name matching should be case-insensitive against lowercase ENVO labels. (4) Bridge via n.mesh_ids (e.g. D052638 = MeSH 'Particulate Matter'). Pitfall: three of the eleven nodes (BFO entity/continuant/material entity and other high-level ENVO ancestors) are ontology upper classes, not exposures — exclude them from Exposure matching.

spoke_nodes.label: Location
spoke_nodes.identifier_scheme: Heterogeneous, keyed by n.type. Country: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code (id='US','NP','NF'; n.iso3 gives alpha-3 'USA','NPL','NFK'). Zipcode: 'STATE-ZIP' (id='NC-27427','MA-01139'; n.name is the bare 5-digit ZIP '27427'). CensusTract: 'GEOID:<11-digit FIPS tract>' (id='GEOID:22115950600'). City: numeric FIPS/GNIS place code (id='4803192' Anderson city). County: 5-digit FIPS county code (id='48481' Wharton County). State: 2-digit FIPS state code (id='24' Maryland, '54' West Virginia). Division / SubDivision: GeoNames dotted admin codes (id='JE.3237073','CH.AG.1901.4001','LC.07'). type distribution: CensusTract 84134, City 58441, Zipcode 42724, SubDivision 5402, Division 3816, County 3196, Country 251, State 52.
spoke_nodes.name_property: n.name holds the place name / label appropriate to the level: Country full name ('United States of America','Nepal'); State name ('Maryland'); County name ('Wharton County'); City name ('Anderson city'); Zipcode holds the bare ZIP digits ('27427'); Division/SubDivision GeoNames admin names ('St Saviour','Aarau'). CensusTract n.name is null (identified only by GEOID). Some Division rows have empty n.name=''.
spoke_nodes.synonyms: No synonyms/aliases/xrefs property. The only alternate-identifier field is n.iso3 (ISO alpha-3), populated on Country nodes only. There is no populated synonym list for sub-national places.
data_sources: UnitedStatesZipcode_database (US Country entry, State, County, City, Zipcode; n.sources=['UnitedStatesZipcode_database'])
spoke_nodes.biookf_mapping: BioOKF `GeographicLocation` — cheatsheet row 'a country, region, place -> GeographicLocation, subtype country/region/place, sources GeoNames/GADM/ISO-3166'. Subtype mapping: Country->country; State/Division/SubDivision->region; County/City/Zipcode/CensusTract->place. The alias/range note in SCHEMA.md ('range += GeographicLocation') confirms GeographicLocation is the endpoint for prevalence/mortality edges, mirroring SPOKE's PREVALENCE_DpL / MORTALITY_DmL / PREVALENCEIN_SpL into Location. `ExposureOrFactor` also lists GeographicLocation as a possible refinement but the clean map is GeographicLocation.
spoke_nodes.matching_notes: Match strategy depends on granularity. Country: match on ISO alpha-2 (n.identifier) or alpha-3 (n.iso3) if the BioOKF node carries an ISO-3166 code; else case-insensitive match on n.name full country name (watch official long forms: 'United States of America' vs 'United States'/'USA'). Sub-national US: match County/State/City by FIPS code in n.identifier when available (most reliable), else by name+type; note County names include the ' County' suffix and City names include ' city' suffix — strip these when comparing. Zipcode: n.name is the bare 5-digit ZIP but n.identifier is 'STATE-ZIP' — match on the ZIP by parsing after the hyphen, and beware leading zeros ('01139'). CensusTract has no name; only match via GEOID. Pitfalls: (a) 198k nodes — never scan unbounded; filter by n.type first. (b) Duplicate/ambiguous names across levels (e.g. many 'Outside city limits' City nodes, empty-string Division names) — always disambiguate with n.type and PARTOF_LpL parentage. (c) two source datasets (GeoNames vs US zipcode DB) can both describe the US, so the same country/place may appear twice.

spoke_nodes.label: Version
spoke_nodes.identifier_scheme: No identifier at all — n.identifier is null on all Version nodes (skeleton samples show identifier=None). These are SPOKE build/release metadata singletons keyed only by n.version (e.g. '0.1') and n.timestamp (nanosecond epoch integer). Not a biomedical entity and not identifier-addressable.
spoke_nodes.name_property:
n.name is null. Version has no name property; the semantically-naming field is n.version (e.g. '0.1'). n.description holds an HTML release-notes blurb ('

Release Notes

This is an early access version of SPOKE...').
spoke_nodes.synonyms: None. No synonyms/aliases/xrefs. Only version, description, timestamp exist.
data_sources: SPOKE internal build metadata (UCSF SPOKE); no source/sources/license property is set

example_nodes.description:
Release Notes

This is an early access version of SPOKE...

participating_reltypes: None — Version does not appear as src or dst in any relationship_signature; it is an isolated metadata label.
spoke_nodes.biookf_mapping: No BioOKF type. Version is graph-provenance/build metadata (a SPOKE release stamp), not a biomedical concept. It is out of scope for the 28 typed BioOKF nodes; if it absolutely had to be recorded it would be `Other` with a note (build/version provenance), but it should be excluded from BioOKF node matching entirely.
spoke_nodes.matching_notes: Do NOT attempt to match any BioOKF concept node to Version. It carries no identifier and no name, only a build version string ('0.1') and a nanosecond timestamp. Treat as SPOKE housekeeping/provenance and skip. If provenance capture is needed, read n.version and n.timestamp as metadata about the SPOKE snapshot, not as an entity to align.

spoke_nodes.label: DatabaseTimestamp
spoke_nodes.identifier_scheme: No identifier — n.identifier is null on all DatabaseTimestamp nodes. These are per-source ETL/ingest provenance records keyed by n.name (the source dataset) plus n.created / n.updated nanosecond-epoch timestamps. Not identifier-addressable and not a biomedical entity.
spoke_nodes.name_property: n.name is the name of the upstream source database / ingestion module whose load time this node records, e.g. 'Uberon anatomy', 'ExplorEnz EC', 'ExplorEnz EC and EC', 'MeSH symptoms', 'FoodOntology foods'. It is a data-pipeline label, not a biomedical concept name.
spoke_nodes.synonyms: None. No synonyms/aliases. Only created, name, updated exist.
data_sources: SPOKE internal ETL/build metadata; each node names the upstream source it timestamps (Uberon, ExplorEnz EC, MeSH, FoodOntology, etc.) but has no source/sources/license property of its own
participating_reltypes: None — DatabaseTimestamp is absent from all relationship_signatures; it is an isolated provenance label.
spoke_nodes.biookf_mapping: No BioOKF type. DatabaseTimestamp is ingestion/provenance metadata (per-source created/updated build stamps), not a biomedical concept. Out of scope for the 28 BioOKF types; at most `Other` with a provenance note, but it should be excluded from BioOKF node matching.
spoke_nodes.matching_notes: Do NOT match BioOKF concept nodes to DatabaseTimestamp. Although n.name mentions source ontologies ('Uberon anatomy', 'MeSH symptoms'), these are pipeline-load records, not entities — a BioOKF Anatomy node must never be matched to the 'Uberon anatomy' DatabaseTimestamp. Use these nodes only as data-freshness/provenance signals (which source was loaded when). Skip for entity alignment.

spoke_nodes.label: TestNode
spoke_nodes.identifier_scheme: No identifier — n.identifier is null. TestNode carries only n.name='test'. These are placeholder/QA scratch nodes left in the graph; not identifier-addressable and carry no real content.
spoke_nodes.name_property: n.name is the literal string 'test' on every node (all 14 sampled/returned show name='test'). No meaningful naming.
spoke_nodes.synonyms: None. The only property is name.
data_sources: None — no source/sources/license; these are internal test/QA placeholder nodes
participating_reltypes: None — TestNode does not appear in any relationship_signature; isolated/placeholder label.
spoke_nodes.biookf_mapping: No BioOKF type. TestNode is garbage/QA placeholder data (14 nodes all named 'test'), not a biomedical concept. Explicitly out of scope; do not map to any of the 28 types (not even `Other`) — it should be filtered out.
spoke_nodes.matching_notes: Ignore entirely. Never match any BioOKF node to TestNode. Treat as noise/QA artifact to be excluded from all matching and from any coverage statistics. Its presence (14 nodes, name='test', no identifier, no edges) is a data-hygiene artifact of the SPOKE build.

spoke_edges.meaning: A disease is statistically/curatorially associated with a gene, i.e. the gene is implicated in the disease (text-mining, curated, and experimental disease-gene evidence). This is a generic gene-disease association, not a causal or mechanistic claim.
edge_sources: DISEASES (Jensen Lab DISEASES resource; sub-channels captured in diseases_sources, e.g. knowledge/text-mining/experiments)
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: associated_with (high confidence). Not 'causes' or 'predisposes_to' because the DISEASES association is generic and non-directional/non-mechanistic. Confidence high for associated_with.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: SPOKE subject = Disease, object = Gene. BioOKF subject should be the Disease (Disease associated_with Gene). Semantically symmetric association (gene<->disease); BioOKF direction Disease->Gene follows the SPOKE edge direction, but the relation is effectively undirected.

spoke_edges.meaning: A gene is associated with a clinical symptom/phenotypic sign: variants/defects in this gene are linked (via HPO gene-to-phenotype annotations mapped to MeSH symptom terms) to presentation of the symptom.
edge_sources: HPO (Human Phenotype Ontology gene-to-phenotype annotations); Symptom nodes are MeSH terms
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: has_phenotype (high) — the gene's dysfunction manifests the symptom; can also secondarily map to associated_with (medium). Prefer has_phenotype since HPO annotations describe phenotypic features of gene defects.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: SPOKE subject = Gene, object = Symptom. BioOKF subject = Gene (Gene has_phenotype Symptom). Directional (gene -> phenotype); not symmetric.

spoke_edges.meaning: A social determinant of health (SDoH; SNOMED findings such as housing insecurity, hearing loss) co-occurs with / is statistically associated with a disease in the biomedical literature. Edge carries co-occurrence enrichment statistics rather than a causal claim.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: associated_with (high). Despite SDoH plausibly being risk factors, the evidence is literature co-occurrence enrichment (odds/fisher), so 'associated_with' is correct; 'predisposes_to' would over-claim (low confidence).
spoke_edges.direction_notes: SPOKE subject = SDoH (the 'S' in SaD, a SNOMED social-determinant finding), object = Disease. BioOKF subject = SDoH (SDoH associated_with Disease). Association is symmetric co-occurrence; SPOKE stores it SDoH->Disease.

spoke_edges.meaning: A genetic variant (dbSNP rsID) is associated with a disease/phenotype via clinical variant curation. Edge records the ClinVar clinical significance (e.g. pathogenic), ref/alt alleles, collection method, and a confidence score. The 'P' abbreviation is Phenotype/Pathophenotype, but the concrete object label in SPOKE is Disease.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: associated_with (high) as the general mapping. When ClinicalSignificance is Pathogenic/Likely pathogenic it leans toward 'predisposes_to'/'causes' (medium confidence), but the reltype as a whole is a variant-disease association so 'associated_with' is the safe primary mapping.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: SPOKE subject = Variant, object = Disease. BioOKF subject = Variant (Variant associated_with Disease). Directional variant->disease; not symmetric.

spoke_edges.meaning: A compound's activity/sensitivity is affected by (associated with) the mutation status of a gene: an ANOVA analysis of cancer cell-line drug screens shows the compound's IC50/sensitivity differs by the gene's mutation feature. Essentially a pharmacogenomic drug-response-vs-gene-mutation association.
edge_sources: CancerRX (GDSC / Genomics of Drug Sensitivity in Cancer)
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: affects_response_to (high) — the gene mutation affects the response to the compound, i.e. a pharmacogenomic response modifier. Secondary: associated_with (medium). Not 'regulates'/'binds' (it is a statistical drug-sensitivity-vs-mutation link, not molecular binding).
spoke_edges.direction_notes: SPOKE subject = Compound, object = Gene, and the edge means 'compound sensitivity is affected by gene mutation'. For BioOKF affects_response_to, the natural subject is the Gene (Gene affects_response_to Compound), so direction is INVERTED relative to SPOKE. Not symmetric.

spoke_edges.meaning: A genetic variant affects an individual's pharmacological response to a compound/drug: the variant's effect allele is associated with altered drug pharmacokinetics (PK) or clinical phenotype/efficacy/toxicity, with a level-of-evidence grade and supporting PMIDs (pharmacogenomics).
edge_sources: PharmGKB-style pharmacogenomic annotations (no r.sources/r.source populated on sampled edges; provenance carried via PMIDs and level_of_evidence)
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: affects_response_to (high) — variant affects response to the drug. Secondary associated_with (low-medium).
spoke_edges.direction_notes: SPOKE subject = Variant, object = Compound. BioOKF subject = Variant (Variant affects_response_to Compound). Direction matches SPOKE. Not symmetric.

spoke_edges.meaning: A gene (via a specific mutation/variant recorded on the edge) confers an adverse drug response / clinical resistance or toxicity to a compound in a given disease context. Curated clinical evidence linking gene mutation to adverse drug response ('m G ar C' = mutated Gene adverse-response Compound).
edge_sources: CIViC (Clinical Interpretation of Variants in Cancer)
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: affects_response_to (high, specifically adverse/toxicity response). Could also inform 'contraindicated_in' at the gene-mutation level (low-medium confidence). Primary: affects_response_to.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: SPOKE subject = Gene (mutated), object = Compound. BioOKF subject = Gene (Gene affects_response_to Compound). Direction matches SPOKE. Not symmetric. Very small (7 edges).

spoke_edges.meaning: Two analytes (clinical lab measurements and/or plasma proteins) are statistically correlated across a wellness cohort. Edge records the correlation type (e.g. Spearman), correlation value(s), sample size N, and Bonferroni-corrected p-value. An analyte-analyte co-variation relationship ('A c A' = Analyte correlates Analyte).
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: associated_with (high) — statistical correlation is a form of association; BioOKF has no dedicated 'correlates_with', so it collapses to associated_with. Possibly 'interacts_with' (low) but that implies mechanism, which correlation does not assert.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Analytes correlate symmetrically; SPOKE stores an arbitrary direction (ClinicalLab or Protein on either side, including cross-type). BioOKF subject can be either endpoint (undirected/symmetric); represent as associated_with with either analyte as subject. Endpoints span all four ClinicalLab/Protein combinations.

spoke_edges.meaning: Two diseases resemble each other, quantified by literature co-occurrence enrichment (they are mentioned together far more than chance). Edge stores odds ratio, enrichment, co-occurrence count, and Fisher-test statistics. A disease-disease similarity relationship.
edge_sources: NCBI PubMed (literature co-occurrence enrichment / Fisher test)
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: associated_with (high) — disease-disease resemblance/co-occurrence maps to associated_with (BioOKF has no 'resembles'/'similar_to'). Not 'is_a' (this is statistical resemblance, not taxonomic subsumption), though pairs like thyroid carcinoma/papillary thyroid carcinoma are coincidentally hierarchical.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Resemblance is symmetric; SPOKE stores an arbitrary direction Disease->Disease. BioOKF subject can be either Disease (undirected). Represent as associated_with, symmetric.

spoke_edges.meaning: Two cell-line records denote the same underlying cell line (synonymous entries / cross-referenced duplicate accessions), e.g. differently-named Cellosaurus records for one line. An identity/sameness link used for cell-line deduplication and cross-referencing.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: same_as / identity — not in the listed BioOKF predicate set. Closest listed predicate is associated_with (low confidence) as a fallback; semantically it is an owl:sameAs-style identity link, so ideally flagged as an equivalence/xref edge rather than a biological relation. 'is_a' is inappropriate (it is co-reference, not subsumption).
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Sameness is inherently symmetric; SPOKE stores an arbitrary direction CellLine->CellLine. BioOKF subject can be either CellLine (undirected/symmetric equivalence).

spoke_edges.meaning: A chemical compound (drug/ligand) binds a protein target, typically with an associated pharmacological mode of action. Verified sample edges carry a drugcentral_relationship such as INHIBITOR, AGONIST, ANTAGONIST, ALLOSTERIC MODULATOR, BLOCKER, ACTIVATOR, BINDING AGENT, so this is the compound-target binding / bioactivity edge.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: binds (high confidence for the physical association). Because most edges carry a pharmacological action verb (inhibitor/agonist/antagonist/activator), a secondary mapping to affects_response_to or regulates is defensible (medium) for action-typed edges; plain 'binds' is the safest primary.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: BioOKF subject = Compound, object = Protein (Compound binds Protein). Not symmetric in SPOKE storage (directed Compound->Protein), though physical binding is conceptually mutual.

spoke_edges.meaning: A compound (often a small molecule, ion, or crystallographic ligand such as glycerin, sulfate ion, zinc cation) binds a specific Pfam protein domain, derived from structural crystal-contact data. This is a domain-level binding annotation rather than whole-protein bioactivity.

example.b_name: Immune inhibitor A peptidase M6, catalytic domain

spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: binds (high confidence). ProteinDomain is a sub-molecular structural feature; the semantics are the same physical-binding relation as BINDS_CbP but at domain granularity.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: BioOKF subject = Compound, object = ProteinDomain (Compound binds ProteinDomain). Directed as stored; binding is conceptually mutual.

spoke_edges.meaning: Cell-cell communication interaction between molecular entities that are Complexes and/or Compounds, sourced from CellChatDB. Verified samples are ligand-complex to receptor-complex signaling pairs (e.g. Activin AB complex interacting with the ACVR1B_ACVR2A receptor complex) annotated with the signaling pathway_name.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: interacts_with (high confidence) as the generic mapping. For the ligand->receptor signaling semantics it can also map to participates_in (the named signaling pathway) at medium confidence; associated_with is an acceptable fallback.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: BioOKF subject = the source entity (ligand side), object = destination entity (receptor side). Mixed endpoint labels (Complex or Compound on either side). Ligand->receptor gives a natural direction, but 'interacts_with' is symmetric so direction is weakly informative.

spoke_edges.meaning: A drug/compound interacts with a food or food category (food-drug interaction), sourced from FIDEO. Captures clinically relevant drug-food interactions such as Rifamycin with alcoholic beverage, or Fluconazole with pineapple food product.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: interacts_with (high confidence). This is a drug-food interaction; associated_with is an acceptable lower-precision fallback.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: BioOKF subject = Compound, object = Food (Compound interacts_with Food). Conceptually symmetric interaction; stored directed Compound->Food.

spoke_edges.meaning: Domain-domain interaction between two Pfam protein domains, inferred from structural crystal contacts (ProtCID). Represents which structural domains physically interact (e.g. Proteasome subunit domain interacting with the AAA (Cdc48) domain).
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: interacts_with (high confidence). Physical/structural interaction between two protein domains.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: BioOKF subject = source ProteinDomain, object = destination ProteinDomain. Symmetric relation (domain-domain interaction has no inherent direction); stored directionally but treat as undirected.

spoke_edges.meaning: Two distinct sub-populations sharing one reltype. (1) Protein->Compound: predicted/known protein-chemical interactions from STITCH, with confidence subscores (textmining, database, experimental, prediction, overall_confidence) — the dominant bulk of the 69.2M edges. (2) Protein->Complex: CellChatDB ligand(Protein)-to-receptor(Complex) cell-signaling edges carrying pathway_name (e.g. SEM3F_HUMAN interacting with the NRP2_PLXNA1 receptor complex).
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: interacts_with (high confidence) as the umbrella predicate for both sub-populations. The STITCH Protein-Compound edges are association/interaction evidence — associated_with is a reasonable fallback (medium). The CellChatDB Protein->Complex signaling edges can additionally map to participates_in for the named pathway (medium).
spoke_edges.direction_notes: BioOKF subject = Protein, object = Compound or Complex. STITCH protein-chemical interaction is effectively symmetric (direction not meaningful); the CellChatDB Protein->Complex subset is ligand->receptor and carries a meaningful biological direction. Endpoint label of the object disambiguates which provenance/semantics apply.

spoke_edges.meaning: Protein-protein interaction from STRING, carrying the full STRING evidence-channel score breakdown (neighborhood, fusion, cooccurrence, coexpression, experiments, databases, textmining) plus a combined score and confidence. General functional/physical PPI network edge.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: interacts_with (high confidence). STRING PPI; associated_with is an acceptable lower-precision fallback for functional-association-only channels.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: BioOKF subject = source Protein, object = destination Protein. Predominantly symmetric (STRING PPI); an is_directed flag exists and is mostly false/null with a minority true, so most edges should be treated as undirected.

spoke_edges.meaning: A curated ligand-receptor (and related ligand-ligand / adhesion-adhesion) interaction between two proteins used for cell-cell communication analysis, sourced from CellPhoneDB. Each edge is annotated with interaction_type (Ligand-Receptor, Ligand-Ligand, Adhesion-Adhesion), a signaling class (e.g. 'Signaling by Chemokines'), curator, resource, and an is_ppi flag.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: interacts_with (high confidence). For Ligand-Receptor edges, participates_in (the named signaling class/pathway) is a reasonable secondary mapping (medium).
spoke_edges.direction_notes: BioOKF subject = source Protein (ligand side for Ligand-Receptor edges), object = destination Protein (receptor side). Ligand->receptor confers a natural direction; ligand-ligand and adhesion-adhesion subtypes are symmetric.

spoke_edges.meaning: Proteolytic-processing relationship: a parent/precursor protein is cleaved into a derived mature chain or peptide product, from UniProt. The destination nodes are UniProt PRO_ processed-product entries (e.g. A0A2T1KRV5 cleaves to PRO_5023297991), representing the products of proteolytic maturation of the precursor.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: derives_from (high confidence: the product chain derives from the precursor) OR converts_to (high confidence: precursor converts_to product). Direction of the SPOKE edge (precursor->product) matches converts_to naturally; if BioOKF derives_from points product->precursor, the mapping requires an edge flip. Primary: converts_to (precursor->product); derives_from is the equivalent flipped predicate.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: SPOKE stores precursor(subject)->product(object). For BioOKF converts_to, keep this direction (precursor converts_to product). For derives_from, the subject is the product and the object is the precursor, i.e. the direction must be reversed relative to SPOKE. Not symmetric.

spoke_edges.meaning: A microRNA targets (post-transcriptionally represses) a gene, from miRDB. Each edge carries a prediction_score reflecting the computational target-prediction confidence (e.g. hsa-miR-6731-3p targeting ZNF630, HDAC9, RAB33B).
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: regulates (high confidence — miRNA targeting is post-transcriptional down-regulation of the gene, and BioOKF collapses up/downregulates into 'regulates'). affects_response_to is not appropriate; associated_with is a weaker fallback.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: BioOKF subject = MiRNA, object = Gene (MiRNA regulates Gene). Directed and not symmetric — the miRNA acts on the gene, not vice versa.

spoke_edges.meaning: A transporter protein transports a compound/substrate across a membrane, from the Transporter Classification Database (TCDB). Edges carry the TCDB transporter classification id (tc_id) and family (tc_family), e.g. the sodium-coupled nucleoside transporter S28A1 transporting Zidovudine.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: interacts_with (medium-high) as the generic mapping, since BioOKF's controlled predicate list has no dedicated 'transports' term. participates_in is a weak alternative; the transport action itself is best captured as a typed interacts_with (transporter->substrate). Confidence for the exact predicate is medium because transport is a specific action being coerced into a broader predicate.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: BioOKF subject = Protein (transporter), object = Compound (substrate). Directed (transporter acts on substrate); not symmetric.

spoke_edges.meaning: A compound (drug) is used to treat a disease. In this SPOKE build the edges are sourced from the Clinical Trials Knowledge Provider (CTKP) and all carry phase=4 (approved / late-phase clinical use), distinguishing them from mid-stage trial edges. The purpose property is predominantly ['treatment'] but a minority also carry prevention/diagnostic/screening/basic_science, so the edge more precisely means 'compound applied to disease in phase-4 clinical practice, chiefly therapeutically'.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: treats (high confidence for purpose=['treatment'], the dominant case). A minority of edges carry purpose=['prevention'] -> prevents, or purpose=['diagnostic']/['screening'] -> used_to_study/measures; these could be split out at lower confidence. Primary mapping: treats, high.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: BioOKF subject = Compound (the drug); object = Disease. Direction matches SPOKE src->dst (Compound treats Disease). Asymmetric/non-symmetric.

spoke_edges.meaning: A compound (drug) is contraindicated in a disease/condition, i.e. the drug should not be given to patients who have this disease because of harm risk. Sourced from DrugCentral; the act_sources property records the underlying bioactivity/label databases (CHEMBL, WOMBAT-PK, IUPHAR, PDSP, DRUG MATRIX, scientific literature) supporting the contraindication.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: contraindicated_in, high confidence. Direct semantic match to the BioOKF contraindicated_in predicate.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: BioOKF subject = Compound (the drug); object = Disease (the condition in which it is contraindicated). Direction matches SPOKE src->dst. Asymmetric.

spoke_edges.meaning: A compound (drug) causes/is associated with a side effect (adverse drug reaction). Sourced from SIDER 4.1, which mines drug package inserts / labels, so semantically these are 'side effect X is reported for drug Y' associations rather than proven mechanistic causation. SideEffect nodes are UMLS-coded (e.g. C0013922 'Embolism').
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: causes, high confidence (drug -> adverse effect). Because SIDER edges are label-derived associations, 'associated_with' is a defensible lower-confidence alternative; but the intended semantics (drug induces the adverse effect) map best to causes. Primary: causes, high; the SideEffect is effectively a phenotype so has_phenotype is a secondary/weaker mapping.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: BioOKF subject = Compound (the drug); object = SideEffect. Direction matches SPOKE src->dst (Compound causes SideEffect). Asymmetric.

spoke_edges.meaning: A microbe/organism is associated with a disease based on differential abundance in the human microbiome. Sourced from HMDAD (Human Microbe-Disease Association Database). Despite the verb 'CAUSES', the evidence property is 'Increase'/'Decrease' (or null), meaning the organism's abundance is increased or decreased in patients with the disease — i.e. a curated microbiome-disease association, not a demonstrated causal/infectious mechanism. Carries pubmed provenance.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: associated_with, high confidence — the edge is a differential-abundance microbe-disease association, not mechanistic causation, so BioOKF's association-collapse rule applies. causes/predisposes_to would over-claim; map at low confidence only. Primary: associated_with, high.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: BioOKF subject = Organism (microbe); object = Disease. Direction matches SPOKE src->dst. The underlying relationship is an association (correlational) so is effectively symmetric in meaning, but stored/emitted Organism->Disease.

spoke_edges.meaning: A compound is being (or has been) evaluated in clinical trials for a disease indication. Sourced from CTKP. Unlike TREATS_CtD (all phase 4), these edges span phases 0 through ~3.5, i.e. investigational / not-yet-approved use. The purpose property is dominantly ['treatment']. Represents 'under clinical investigation for' rather than an established therapy.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: used_to_study, high confidence (compound investigated against a disease in trials). BioOKF has no dedicated 'in_clinical_trials_for' predicate; used_to_study captures the investigational relationship. A weaker secondary mapping to treats is possible but should be low confidence because the compound is not an established therapy for the indication. Primary: used_to_study, high.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: BioOKF subject = Compound; object = Disease (the trial indication). Direction matches SPOKE src->dst. Asymmetric.

spoke_edges.meaning: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST) result: an organism (bacterial strain) responds to a compound (antibiotic) with a measured phenotype. Sourced from BV-BRC. The resistant_phenotype property is one of Resistant / Susceptible / Intermediate, and edges carry lab measurement metadata (MIC measurement_value/sign/unit, laboratory_typing_method/platform, vendor, testing_standard_year). So 'RESPONDS_TO' covers the full susceptibility spectrum, not only susceptibility — it is a drug-response/AST measurement edge.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: affects_response_to, high confidence — the organism's phenotype describes its response/resistance to the drug (a pharmacological response measurement). Because each edge also records a quantitative MIC, measures is a defensible secondary mapping. Primary: affects_response_to, high; measures, medium.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: SPOKE stores Organism->Compound. BioOKF affects_response_to is drug-centric (subject typically the biomarker/organism affecting the drug's effect); here the Organism is the natural BioOKF subject and Compound the object, matching SPOKE src->dst. Asymmetric.

spoke_edges.meaning: A pharmacogenomic biomarker (a gene variant) confers RESISTANCE of a tumor/patient to a drug, in a given disease context. Sourced from CIViC. Although the endpoint label is Gene->Compound, the biomarker is variant-level: the edge carries variant (e.g. AR F877L, RSF1 Amplification, DNMT3A Mutation), disease/disease_id context, clin_sig = 'Resistance', tier, pubmed, and a CIViC url. Meaning: 'this gene alteration predicts resistance/lack of benefit to this drug'.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: affects_response_to, high confidence — a genomic variant modifying drug response (specifically conferring resistance). BioOKF has no separate 'confers_resistance' predicate, so the resistance direction is captured as affects_response_to (the clin_sig='Resistance' value carries the polarity). Primary: affects_response_to, high.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: SPOKE stores Gene->Compound; BioOKF subject = Gene (variant biomarker), object = Compound (drug), matching src->dst. Asymmetric. The disease context (r.disease) is qualifier metadata, not a third endpoint. Distinguished from RESPONSE_TO_mGrC / REDUCES_SEN_mGrsC only by clin_sig value.

spoke_edges.meaning: A pharmacogenomic biomarker (gene variant) confers REDUCED SENSITIVITY of a tumor to a drug (an intermediate between full sensitivity and outright resistance). Sourced from CIViC; identical edge structure to the other two CIViC pharmacogenomic reltypes, distinguished by clin_sig = 'Reduced Sensitivity'. Variant-level (e.g. KIT variants), disease-contextual. Only 2 edges in this build.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: affects_response_to, high confidence — genomic variant that diminishes (but does not abolish) drug response. Polarity ('Reduced Sensitivity') is carried in clin_sig. Primary: affects_response_to, high.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: SPOKE stores Gene->Compound; BioOKF subject = Gene (variant), object = Compound. Matches src->dst. Asymmetric. One of three CIViC pharmacogenomic reltypes split purely by clin_sig; BioOKF collapses all three into affects_response_to.

spoke_edges.meaning: A pharmacogenomic biomarker (gene variant) predicts SENSITIVITY / positive RESPONSE of a tumor to a drug. Sourced from CIViC, clin_sig = 'Sensitivity/Response'. Variant-level and disease-contextual (e.g. EGFR T790M / L858R -> Osimertinib in Lung Non-small Cell Carcinoma; KIT D816V -> Midostaurin in Systemic Mastocytosis; AREG Expression -> Panitumumab in Colorectal Cancer). Means 'this gene alteration predicts the patient will respond to this drug'.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: affects_response_to, high confidence — genomic variant conferring drug sensitivity/response. Polarity ('Sensitivity/Response') is in clin_sig. Primary: affects_response_to, high.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: SPOKE stores Gene->Compound; BioOKF subject = Gene (variant biomarker), object = Compound (drug). Matches src->dst. Asymmetric. Together with RESISTANT_TO_mGrC and REDUCES_SEN_mGrsC forms the CIViC pharmacogenomic family, distinguished only by the clin_sig value; all map to affects_response_to with polarity preserved as an edge property.

spoke_edges.meaning: A gene locus gives rise to (encodes) a mature microRNA. The Gene is the miRNA host/precursor locus and the MiRNA node is the mature miRBase product (e.g. hsa-miR-*). This is the gene-product 'encodes' relationship specialized to miRNA products rather than proteins.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: encodes (high confidence). The VERB is literally ENCODES and semantics are gene->product.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = Gene (source), object = MiRNA (destination). BioOKF direction Gene->MiRNA matches SPOKE src->dst. Not symmetric (a reverse 'derives_from' would be the inverse, but SPOKE stores it directed as encodes).

spoke_edges.meaning: A gene encodes a protein product. Gene node (NCBI gene) points to the UniProt protein(s) it codes for, including isoforms/unreviewed entries. Core central-dogma gene->protein relationship.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: encodes (high confidence).
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = Gene, object = Protein. BioOKF Gene->Protein matches SPOKE src->dst. Directed, not symmetric. Note: two provenance shapes observed on real edges — {sources:[UniProt]} and {license, source:UniProt}.

spoke_edges.meaning: An organism (NCBI taxon: species/strain/virus) encodes a protein in its proteome. Links each UniProt protein to the source organism whose genome encodes it. This is the largest edge family in this set (~40M) because it spans every non-human organism proteome in UniProt.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: encodes (medium-high). The subject is an organism rather than a gene, so this is an organism-level 'encodes' / proteome-membership. Could alternatively map to a produces/derives_from-style relation, but ENCODES verb and gene-product semantics favor 'encodes'. If BioOKF requires a Gene subject for 'encodes', fall back to associated_with (protein associated_with organism).
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = Organism, object = Protein. BioOKF Organism->Protein matches SPOKE src->dst. Directed, not symmetric.

spoke_edges.meaning: A PanGene (a pan-genome orthologous gene grouping / gene-name cluster such as 'yqjB2', 'ybeK_3') encodes a protein. Aggregates orthologous protein products across strains/organisms under a shared pangenome gene identifier. ~9.4M edges.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: encodes (medium-high). A pangenome gene grouping encoding its protein members; same 'encodes' semantics as Gene->Protein but at the ortholog-cluster level.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = PanGene, object = Protein. BioOKF PanGene->Protein matches SPOKE src->dst. Directed, not symmetric.

spoke_edges.meaning: A compound participates in a (Reactome) reaction — i.e. it is a molecular participant (typically a required input such as ATP/ADP) of the reaction. Distinct from CONSUMES/PRODUCES which are directional metabolic roles; this is a generic Reactome participation of small molecules.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: participates_in (high confidence).
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = Compound, object = Reaction. BioOKF Compound->Reaction matches SPOKE src->dst. Directed.

spoke_edges.meaning: A gene participates in a GO Biological Process — i.e. the gene's product is annotated to that biological process (GO BP term). Standard GO functional annotation of genes to processes.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: participates_in (high confidence). GO BP annotation = gene participates in a biological process.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = Gene, object = BiologicalProcess. BioOKF Gene->BiologicalProcess matches SPOKE src->dst. Directed. Edge carries an 'evidence' qualifier (e.g. 'Inferred') and an 'unbiased' flag.

spoke_edges.meaning: A gene participates in / is associated with a GO Cellular Component — the gene product localizes to that subcellular location/component (GO CC term). GO localization annotation.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: located_in (high confidence) — GO CC denotes subcellular localization. Secondary: participates_in (matches the SPOKE PARTICIPATES verb) but 'located_in' better captures CC semantics.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = Gene, object = CellularComponent. BioOKF Gene->CellularComponent matches SPOKE src->dst. Directed.

spoke_edges.meaning: A gene participates in / has a GO Molecular Function — the gene product carries out that molecular activity (GO MF term, e.g. 'sulfurtransferase activity'). GO function annotation.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: participates_in (high confidence, matching PARTICIPATES verb). Could also be read as 'has molecular function' (a has-function relation); if BioOKF lacks that, participates_in / associated_with are the fallbacks.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = Gene, object = MolecularFunction. BioOKF Gene->MolecularFunction matches SPOKE src->dst. Directed.

spoke_edges.meaning: A gene participates in a biological pathway (WikiPathways). The gene product is a member/component of the named pathway.

example.b_name: 7 oxo C and 7 beta HC pathways

spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: participates_in (high confidence). Gene participation in a pathway.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = Gene, object = Pathway. BioOKF Gene->Pathway matches SPOKE src->dst. Directed. Edge has 'vestige' flag and WikiPathways license.

spoke_edges.meaning: A gene participates in a (Reactome) reaction as a physical entity — typically the gene locus itself as the substrate of a transcription/regulatory reaction (e.g. transcription factors binding the gene). Small, specialized family where the DNA gene is a reaction participant.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: participates_in (high confidence).
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = Gene, object = Reaction. BioOKF Gene->Reaction matches SPOKE src->dst. Directed.

spoke_edges.meaning: A PwGroup (a Reactome pathway/complex 'group' — an assembled molecular complex or set, e.g. 'EGFR:AAMP', 'EGFR:EGF-like ligands') participates in a Reactome reaction as a participant entity. PGp abbreviates PwGroup-participates, NOT PanGene.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: participates_in (high confidence). A molecular complex/group participating in a reaction.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = PwGroup (protein complex/set), object = Reaction. BioOKF PwGroup->Reaction matches SPOKE src->dst. Directed.

spoke_edges.meaning: A protein participates in a (Reactome) reaction — as substrate, product, catalyst, or regulator/participant entity. Links UniProt proteins to the Reactome reactions they take part in.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: participates_in (high confidence).
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = Protein, object = Reaction. BioOKF Protein->Reaction matches SPOKE src->dst. Directed.

spoke_edges.meaning: An enzyme (EC number / enzyme class) catalyzes a metabolic reaction. Links Enzyme Commission activity nodes to the KEGG/MetaCyc reactions they catalyze.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: catalyzes (high confidence). Verb is literally CATALYZES.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = EC (enzyme), object = Reaction. BioOKF EC->Reaction matches SPOKE src->dst. Directed. Sources are per-edge single-DB (kegg OR metacyc).

spoke_edges.meaning: A reaction consumes a compound — the compound is an input/substrate (left-hand side / reactant) of the metabolic reaction. Directional metabolic role from KEGG.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: participates_in (medium) as the closest generic BioOKF predicate; the substrate role ('consumes'/'has input') is more specific than any BioOKF term. If a 'consumes'/reactant relation is unavailable, participates_in captures it; converts_to is NOT appropriate here (that is compound-to-compound). Confidence medium because BioOKF lacks a dedicated consumes predicate.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = Reaction, object = Compound. SPOKE stores Reaction->Compound; semantically the compound is consumed BY the reaction. BioOKF direction Reaction->Compound preserves src->dst. Directed, not symmetric. Paired inverse role is PRODUCES_RpC. Note the same Reaction+Compound pair can appear in both CONSUMES and PRODUCES across a reversible reaction's two directions.

spoke_edges.meaning: A reaction produces a compound — the compound is an output/product (right-hand side) of the metabolic reaction. Directional metabolic role from KEGG, inverse role of CONSUMES_RcC.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: participates_in (medium) as closest generic predicate; the product role ('produces'/'has output') is more specific than any BioOKF term. converts_to is NOT appropriate (compound-to-compound). Confidence medium because BioOKF lacks a dedicated produces predicate.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = Reaction, object = Compound. SPOKE Reaction->Compound; compound is produced BY the reaction. BioOKF Reaction->Compound preserves src->dst. Directed, not symmetric. Inverse role of CONSUMES_RcC; a reversible reaction lists a metabolite under both.

spoke_edges.meaning: A protein domain (Pfam PF entry, e.g. PF14806) is a member of a protein family/clan (Pfam clan CL entry, e.g. CL0545). Groups related Pfam domains into their higher-level clan/family.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: member_of (high confidence). Verb is literally MEMBEROF; domain is a member of the family/clan. Closely related to is_a / part_of, but member_of is the exact match.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = ProteinDomain, object = ProteinFamily. BioOKF ProteinDomain->ProteinFamily matches SPOKE src->dst. Directed (member -> group), not symmetric.

spoke_edges.meaning: A gene is significantly down-regulated (lower expression) in a given anatomical structure/tissue relative to other tissues, from differential-expression profiling. The edge carries the statistical evidence (log2 fold-change, p-value, FDR) for the tissue-specific under-expression.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: regulates (high confidence; BioOKF collapses UP/DOWNREGULATES into 'regulates'). Secondary weak reading could be 'expressed_in' but the directional DE semantics fit 'regulates' best.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = Anatomy (this-doc), object = Gene. Directed and asymmetric (tissue affects gene expression); not symmetric.

spoke_edges.meaning: Exposure to a compound/drug down-regulates a gene's expression, inferred from CMAP/LINCS L1000 drug-perturbation transcriptional signatures (negative z-score). Represents drug-induced transcriptional repression of the target gene.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: regulates (high confidence; UP/DOWNREGULATES collapse to 'regulates'). 'affects_response_to' does not apply (that is the response direction). No 'treats' semantics here.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = Compound (this-doc), object = Gene. Directed/asymmetric: compound perturbs gene.

spoke_edges.meaning: Perturbing (overexpressing/applying) a ligand-encoding source gene down-regulates a target gene, from CMAP/LINCS ligand-treatment (trt_lig) transcriptional signatures. Gene-ligand-perturbation Gene relationship.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: regulates (high confidence). Gene-gene regulatory effect from ligand perturbation; collapses to 'regulates'.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = source (ligand/perturbing) Gene (this-doc), object = affected Gene. Directed/asymmetric.

spoke_edges.meaning: Knockdown of a source gene (shRNA/CRISPR, CMAP/LINCS trt_sh/trt_xrt) results in down-regulation of a target gene's expression. Captures a directional gene-gene regulatory dependency revealed by loss-of-function perturbation.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: regulates (high confidence). Knockdown-Gene down-regulates Gene collapses to 'regulates'.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = knocked-down source Gene (this-doc), object = affected Gene. Directed/asymmetric.

spoke_edges.meaning: Overexpression of a source gene (CMAP/LINCS trt_oe) down-regulates a target gene's expression. Directional gene-gene regulatory effect revealed by gain-of-function perturbation.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: regulates (high confidence). Overexpression-Gene down-regulates Gene collapses to 'regulates'.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = overexpressed source Gene (this-doc), object = affected Gene. Directed/asymmetric.

spoke_edges.meaning: A gene is significantly up-regulated (higher expression) in a given anatomical structure/tissue relative to other tissues, from differential-expression profiling, with log2 fold-change, p-value and FDR evidence.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: regulates (high confidence; UP/DOWNREGULATES collapse to 'regulates'). Directional tissue over-expression.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = Anatomy (this-doc), object = Gene. Directed/asymmetric; mirror of DOWNREGULATES_AdG.

spoke_edges.meaning: Exposure to a compound/drug up-regulates a gene's expression, inferred from CMAP/LINCS L1000 drug-perturbation signatures (positive z-score). Drug-induced transcriptional activation of the target gene.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: regulates (high confidence). Mirror of DOWNREGULATES_CdG; collapses to 'regulates'.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = Compound (this-doc), object = Gene. Directed/asymmetric.

spoke_edges.meaning: Perturbing a ligand-encoding source gene up-regulates a target gene, from CMAP/LINCS ligand-treatment (trt_lig) transcriptional signatures. Gene-ligand-perturbation Gene activating relationship.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: regulates (high confidence). Mirror of DOWNREGULATES_GPdG.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = source (ligand) Gene (this-doc), object = affected Gene. Directed/asymmetric.

spoke_edges.meaning: Knockdown of a source gene (CMAP/LINCS trt_sh/trt_xrt) results in up-regulation of a target gene's expression, revealing a directional (often repressive) gene-gene regulatory dependency by loss-of-function.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: regulates (high confidence). Mirror of DOWNREGULATES_KGdG.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = knocked-down source Gene (this-doc), object = affected Gene. Directed/asymmetric.

spoke_edges.meaning: Overexpression of a source gene (CMAP/LINCS trt_oe) up-regulates a target gene's expression. Directional activating gene-gene regulatory effect from gain-of-function perturbation.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: regulates (high confidence). Mirror of DOWNREGULATES_OGdG.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = overexpressed source Gene (this-doc), object = affected Gene. Directed/asymmetric.

spoke_edges.meaning: A transcription-factor protein regulates the transcription of a target gene (curated TF->target-gene regulatory interaction). Direction/sign is not encoded (generic regulation); evidence includes assay method (ChIP, EMSA, DNase footprinting, curator inference) and PMID literature references.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: regulates (high confidence). Classic TF->target regulation. Not 'binds' (though ChIP implies binding) because the asserted semantic is transcriptional regulation.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = TF Protein (this-doc), object = target Gene. Directed/asymmetric (regulator -> regulated).

spoke_edges.meaning: A gene is a prognostically UNFAVORABLE marker for a disease/cancer: high expression of the gene is statistically associated with worse patient outcome (survival), per Human Protein Atlas pathology/prognostic analysis. The p_value quantifies the survival association.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: associated_with (high confidence; association-like biomarker edge) and secondarily 'measures'/biomarker sense. Not 'causes' or 'predisposes_to' (it is a prognostic correlation, not causation).
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = Gene (this-doc), object = Disease. Directed by convention (gene-as-marker of disease); underlying statistical association is symmetric in meaning but stored gene->disease.

spoke_edges.meaning: A gene is a defining marker of a provisional cell type: its expression identifies/characterizes that cell type in single-cell reference data. Edge carries an f-beta confidence score and the Ensembl IDs of the marker set the gene belongs to.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: associated_with (high confidence, marker-of relationship) with a 'measures'/biomarker flavor. Weakly relatable to 'expressed_in' but the asserted semantic is cell-type marker identity, best mapped to associated_with.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = Gene (this-doc), object = ProvCellType. Directed (gene marks cell type); asymmetric.

spoke_edges.meaning: A gene is a prognostically FAVORABLE marker for a disease/cancer: high expression is statistically associated with better patient outcome (survival), per Human Protein Atlas prognostic analysis. p_value quantifies the survival association.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: associated_with (high confidence; biomarker/prognostic association, mirror of MARKER_NEG). Biomarker 'measures' sense secondary. Not causal.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = Gene (this-doc), object = Disease. Directed gene->disease (gene-as-marker); mirror of MARKER_NEG_GmnD (favorable vs unfavorable).

spoke_edges.meaning: A gene's expression is enriched in a specific (ontology-mapped) cell type relative to others, from single-cell atlas data. Edge carries an enrichment score and mean_expression quantifying the cell-type specificity.

example.b_name: long-range projecting sst GABAergic cortical interneuron (Mmus)

spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: expressed_in (high confidence — gene enriched/expressed in a cell type). Secondary 'associated_with' possible, but the enriched-expression semantic maps most directly to expressed_in.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = Gene (this-doc), object = CellType. Directed (gene enriched-in cell type); asymmetric.

spoke_edges.meaning: A gene's expression is enriched in a specific provisional (not-yet-canonical) cell type relative to others, from single-cell atlas data, with enrichment score and mean_expression. Same semantics as ENRICHED_IN_GeiCT but the target is a ProvCellType node.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: expressed_in (high confidence). Mirror of ENRICHED_IN_GeiCT for provisional cell types.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = Gene (this-doc), object = ProvCellType. Directed/asymmetric.

spoke_edges.meaning: An anatomical structure/tissue expresses a gene (the gene is detectably expressed in that tissue), per BGee expression calls. This is a presence-of-expression edge (no fold-change/direction), distinct from the directional UP/DOWNREGULATES_AdG DE edges.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: expressed_in (high confidence). BioOKF 'expressed_in' has gene as subject and anatomy as object, so the direction is reversed relative to this SPOKE edge (see direction_notes).
spoke_edges.direction_notes: SPOKE stores Anatomy(subject)->Gene(object) i.e. 'anatomy expresses gene'. BioOKF's expressed_in is Gene->Anatomy, so mapping requires flipping subject/object. Directed/asymmetric.

spoke_edges.meaning: A gene is expressed in a given cell type. Quantitative single-cell/tissue expression from the Human Protein Atlas, capturing where a gene's transcript is detected across cell types with expression level and cell-type specificity.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: expressed_in (high confidence). The edge is a canonical gene-expressed-in-celltype relationship; maps directly to expressed_in.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: BioOKF subject = Gene (this-doc), object = CellType. Directed (Gene EXPRESSEDIN CellType); not symmetric.

spoke_edges.meaning: A gene is expressed in (the tissue/pathology of) a disease, drawn from Human Protein Atlas pathology/cancer expression data. Captures elevated or characteristic gene expression measured in diseased (typically cancer) tissue, with protein-transcripts-per-million and specificity.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: expressed_in (medium-high confidence) as the literal semantic; secondary associated_with (medium) since HPA pathology expression is often used as a gene-disease association signal. Primary mapping is expressed_in.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: BioOKF subject = Gene, object = Disease. Directed; not symmetric. Note the object is a Disease used as an expression context (diseased tissue), not a molecular target.

spoke_edges.meaning: A protein is expressed/detected in a specific cell line, from the Cell Surface Protein Atlas (via Pharos): surface proteins detected on cultured cell lines by surfaceome proteomics.
