spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: expressed_in (high confidence). Protein-detected-in-cell-line is a direct expressed_in relationship.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: BioOKF subject = Protein, object = CellLine. Directed; not symmetric.

spoke_edges.meaning: A protein is expressed in a cell type, sourced from Cell Taxonomy where the protein serves as a marker of that cell type (protein_is_a_cellMarker flag), often under specified tissue/species/condition context.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: expressed_in (high confidence). The protein is a canonical marker expressed in the cell type; maps to expressed_in. A weak secondary reading as a defining/marker (member/characteristic-of) relationship exists but expressed_in is the intended semantic.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: BioOKF subject = Protein, object = CellType. Directed; not symmetric.

spoke_edges.meaning: A disease localizes to / is anatomically associated with an anatomical structure. Derived from literature co-occurrence (NCBI PubMed) with Fisher-test enrichment, indicating the disease is discussed/manifests in that anatomy (e.g., papillary thyroid carcinoma in lymph node).
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: located_in (medium-high confidence) as the literal semantic (disease localizes to anatomy); secondary associated_with (medium) because the edge is co-occurrence/enrichment-based rather than an asserted ontological localization. Primary mapping is located_in.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: BioOKF subject = Disease, object = Anatomy. Directed; not symmetric. Uses r.source (singular) = 'NCBI PubMed'.

spoke_edges.meaning: A compound (chemical) is found/measured in a geographic location, from environmental monitoring (WHO Ambient Air Quality Database): e.g., measured concentration of Nitrogen Dioxide in a city, with value, unit, media, year, and metric.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: located_in (medium confidence) as 'compound present at location'; secondary measures/associated_with (low-medium) since edges carry measured concentration values. No clean BioOKF predicate exists for environmental-concentration measurement; located_in is the closest.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: BioOKF subject = Compound, object = Location (geographic). Directed; not symmetric. This is a geospatial/environmental edge, not a molecular localization.

spoke_edges.meaning: An environmental factor/exposure (Environment node, e.g., respirable suspended particulate matter) is found/measured in a geographic location, from emissions-inventory data (2020 National Emissions Inventory), with measured value, unit, metric, and year.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: located_in (medium confidence) as 'environmental factor present at location'; secondary measures/associated_with (low-medium) given measured values. Environmental-exposure-at-location; located_in is the closest BioOKF fit.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: BioOKF subject = Environment, object = Location (geographic). Directed; not symmetric. Geospatial/exposure edge.

spoke_edges.meaning: An organism (typically a bacterial/pathogen strain) was isolated in / sampled from a geographic location, from the BV-BRC pathogen genomics database. Records where a given microbial strain was collected.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: located_in (medium confidence) as 'organism isolated at location'; secondary derives_from (low-medium, sample provenance). No dedicated 'isolated_in' predicate in BioOKF; located_in is closest.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: BioOKF subject = Organism, object = Location (geographic). Directed; not symmetric. Geospatial sampling-provenance edge.

spoke_edges.meaning: A protein's abundance/level is decreased (downregulated) in a disease. A small curated set; the example set is derived from a RECOVER long-COVID proteomics study (GitHub Hadlock_lab/RECOVER), with supporting PMIDs. Indicates the protein is measured at reduced levels in the disease state.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: regulates (high confidence) — BioOKF collapses UP/DOWNREGULATES into 'regulates'; this is the disease-context down-direction of a protein-level change. Secondary associated_with (medium) as a protein-disease association. Direction/sign (decrease) is lost in the 'regulates' collapse.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: BioOKF subject = Protein, object = Disease. Directed; not symmetric. Sign = decreased (downregulated in disease); the disease is the context, not the agent of change.

spoke_edges.meaning: A protein's abundance/level is increased (upregulated) in a disease, largely from Cell Taxonomy where the protein is an elevated cell marker under a disease condition. Indicates the protein is measured at higher levels / is a marker enriched in the disease state.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: regulates (high confidence) — the increase/up-direction counterpart of DECREASEDIN, collapsed to 'regulates' in BioOKF. Secondary associated_with (medium) as a protein-disease association / disease biomarker. Sign (increase) is lost in the collapse.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: BioOKF subject = Protein, object = Disease. Directed; not symmetric. Sign = increased (upregulated in disease); disease is the context. This is the directional sibling of DECREASEDIN_PdD.

spoke_edges.meaning: A disease presents with (manifests) a symptom. Derived from literature co-occurrence (NCBI PubMed) with Fisher-test enrichment linking a disease to a clinical symptom/sign (e.g., lymphoma presents Acute Abdomen).
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: has_phenotype (high confidence) — disease-presents-symptom is the canonical has_phenotype relationship. Secondary associated_with (medium) because it is co-occurrence/enrichment-derived rather than curated. Primary mapping is has_phenotype.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: BioOKF subject = Disease, object = Symptom. Directed; not symmetric.

spoke_edges.meaning: A (pathogen) protein impacts a disease outcome — a pathogen-host-interaction edge from the PHI-base (PHI) database. The protein is a pathogen gene product whose mutation/deletion alters disease phenotype (e.g., 'reduced virulence'), with experimental evidence and host tissue context. NOT a human gene-disease association: the protein belongs to the infecting organism and its perturbation changes pathogenicity.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: affects_response_to / causes-related — best fit is 'affects' semantics captured by predisposes_to (medium) or causes (low-medium) for virulence contribution; most defensibly associated_with (medium-high) as a pathogen-protein-to-disease impact. Because BioOKF lacks a pathogen-virulence predicate, associated_with is the safe primary, with a note that the true relation is 'protein perturbation impacts disease/virulence'.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: BioOKF subject = Protein (pathogen protein), object = Disease. Directed; not symmetric. Distinct from INCREASEDIN/DECREASEDIN: this is a functional/causal impact on virulence (from mutant phenotype experiments), not a protein-abundance change; the protein is pathogen-derived, not host.

spoke_edges.meaning: Taxonomic subclass within the anatomy (Uberon) ontology: a more specific anatomical structure is a kind of a broader anatomical structure (e.g. 'lumbar vertebra 5' is-a 'lumbar vertebra').
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: is_a (high confidence)
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = child/more specific Anatomy (a); object = parent/broader Anatomy (b). BioOKF child -is_a-> parent. Asymmetric (hierarchical).

spoke_edges.meaning: LOINC hierarchy: a specific clinical lab test/observation is-a member of a broader LOINC category/class (e.g. a lutropin challenge-test panel is-a 'Challenge tests'; a blood-spot chemistry test is-a 'Chemistry').
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: is_a (high); could also be read as member_of a LOINC class (medium)
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = specific lab test (a); object = broader LOINC class (b). Asymmetric. Uses singular 'source' property, not 'sources'.

spoke_edges.meaning: Cell Line Ontology (CLO) subclass: a specific/named cell line is-a kind of broader cell-line category (e.g. named line 'TTDH7PV' is-a 'immortal human skin-derived cell line').
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: is_a (high confidence)
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = specific CellLine (a); object = broader CellLine class (b). BioOKF child -is_a-> parent. Asymmetric.

spoke_edges.meaning: Cell Ontology (CL) subclass: a more specific cell type is-a kind of broader cell type (e.g. 'neutrophilic promyelocyte' is-a 'promyelocyte').
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: is_a (high confidence)
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = specific CellType (a); object = broader CellType (b). Asymmetric hierarchical.

spoke_edges.meaning: ChEBI chemical ontology subclass: a specific compound/molecular entity is-a member of a broader chemical class (e.g. '3-Methylcyclohexanone' is-a 'cyclohexanones').
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: is_a (high confidence)
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = specific Compound (a); object = broader chemical class Compound (b). Asymmetric. A given compound can have multiple parents (multiple is_a edges).

spoke_edges.meaning: Disease Ontology (DOID) subclass: a more specific disease is-a kind of broader disease (e.g. 'hyperphosphatasia with impaired intellectual development syndrome 6' is-a the umbrella syndrome).

example.a_name: hyperphosphatasia with impaired intellectual development syndrome 6
example.b_name: hyperphosphatasia with impaired intellectual development syndrome

spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: is_a (high confidence)
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = specific Disease (a); object = broader parent Disease (b). Asymmetric. Uses singular 'source' property.

spoke_edges.meaning: Enzyme Commission number hierarchy: a fully specified enzyme class (e.g. 4-level EC 5.5.1.8 '(+)-bornyl diphosphate synthase') is-a its parent sub-subclass (EC 5.5.1). Encodes the EC numbering tree.

example.b_name: Intramolecular lyases (only sub-subclass identified to date)

spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: is_a (high confidence)
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = more specific EC class (a); object = broader EC class (b). Asymmetric hierarchical.

spoke_edges.meaning: Environment Ontology (ENVO) subclass: a specific environmental material/exposure is-a a broader environmental entity (e.g. 'fine respirable suspended particulate matter' is-a 'respirable suspended particulate matter').
edge_sources: ENVO (implied by ENVO_* node identifiers; no source property on the edge)
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: is_a (high confidence)
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = more specific Environment (a); object = broader Environment (b). Asymmetric. Edge carries NO properties (no sources/source); provenance only inferable from ENVO node identifiers.

spoke_edges.meaning: FoodOn ontology subclass: a specific food or food product is-a a broader food category (e.g. 'fuzzy kiwifruit' / 'kiwifruit' is-a 'kiwifruit food product').
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: is_a (high confidence)
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = specific Food (a); object = broader Food category (b). Asymmetric. Uses singular 'source' property.

spoke_edges.meaning: NCBI Taxonomy hierarchy: a taxon is-a child of its parent taxon (e.g. strain 'Brenneria salicis ATCC 15712 = DSM 30166' is-a species 'Brenneria salicis'; species is-a genus). Encodes the taxonomic tree.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: is_a (high confidence); taxonomic parent could also be read as member_of a taxon (medium)
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = child taxon (a); object = parent taxon (b). Asymmetric. Largest ISA family (~418K edges).

spoke_edges.meaning: Provisional Cell Ontology (PCL) to Cell Ontology bridge: a provisional/transcriptomically-defined cell type is-a an established CL cell type (e.g. 'Astro_53 astrocyte (Hsap)' is-a 'astrocyte' / 'brain macroglial cell').
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: is_a (high confidence)
spoke_edges.direction_notes: The ONLY cross-label ISA here: subject = ProvCellType (a), object = canonical CellType (b). Asymmetric; grounds provisional types into the CL hierarchy.

spoke_edges.meaning: Subclass within the Provisional Cell Ontology: a specific provisional (transcriptomic) cell type is-a a broader provisional cell type (e.g. 'MGE_249 sst GABAergic cortical interneuron (Hsap)' is-a 'MGE interneuron ... (Hsap)').

example.b_name: MGE interneuron medial ganglionic eminence derived interneuron (Hsap)

spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: is_a (high confidence)
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = specific ProvCellType (a); object = broader ProvCellType (b). Asymmetric hierarchical.

spoke_edges.meaning: Reactome pathway hierarchy: a child pathway is-a subcategory of a broader parent pathway (e.g. 'Signaling by Nuclear Receptors' is-a 'Signaling Pathways'). Encodes the Reactome pathway containment/classification tree.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: is_a (high); semantically overlaps with part_of a parent pathway (Reactome hierarchy), so part_of is a plausible alternative (medium)
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = child/sub-pathway (a); object = parent pathway (b). Asymmetric. Edge carries a Reactome 'version' property.

spoke_edges.meaning: Links a social-determinant-of-health measure (County Health Rankings, CHR_* identifiers) to the SNOMED CT concept that types/defines it (e.g. 'Adult Obesity' is-a SNOMED 'Obese (finding)'; 'Adult Smoking' is-a SNOMED 'Smoker (finding)'). Functions as a cross-vocabulary typing/mapping rather than a strict intra-ontology subclass tree.
edge_sources: County Health Rankings (CHR_* subject ids) / SNOMED CT (object concepts); no source property on the edge
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: is_a (medium); because it is a CHR-measure-to-SNOMED-concept mapping it also fits member_of / measures / associated_with (low-medium)
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = SDoH measure (a, CHR_*); object = SNOMED concept (b). Asymmetric. Edge carries NO properties.

spoke_edges.meaning: Uberon partonomy (meronymy): an anatomical structure is a physical part of a larger anatomical structure (e.g. 'transverse process of lumbar vertebra' part-of 'lumbar vertebra'). Distinct from ISA_AiA subclass.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: part_of (high confidence)
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = part / smaller structure (a); object = whole / larger structure (b). Asymmetric (part -part_of-> whole).

spoke_edges.meaning: A cell type is part of / located in an anatomical structure per Cell Ontology (e.g. 'melanocyte of foreskin' part-of 'skin of prepuce of penis'; 'peripheral blood stem cell' part-of 'blood').
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: part_of (high); overlaps with located_in for the cell-in-tissue reading (medium)
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = CellType (a); object = Anatomy (b). Asymmetric (cell type -part_of/located_in-> anatomy).

spoke_edges.meaning: ChEBI 'has part' partonomy between chemical entities: one compound/moiety is a structural part of another (e.g. a molecular entity contains a 'hassium atom'; a glycopeptide contains a 'heptopyranosyl group').
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: part_of (high); the whole->part reading also fits derives_from / member_of weakly (low)
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Direction per real edges: subject = whole/parent entity (a) points to the constituent atom/group (b) — i.e. a -PARTOF-> b where b is the component. This is the reverse of the usual 'part_of' subject=part convention, so mapping to part_of should flip subject/object (component -part_of-> whole). Asymmetric.

spoke_edges.meaning: A small-molecule Compound is a component of a Reactome physical-entity complex/set (PwGroup) (e.g. 'Zinc Cation' part-of the 'ADAM:Zn2+' complex; 'GTP' part-of 'p21 RAS:GTP').
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: member_of (high, molecule is a member/component of a complex); part_of (high alternative)
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = Compound (a); object = Reactome complex/set PwGroup (b). Asymmetric. Edge carries Reactome 'version'.

spoke_edges.meaning: A Gene is a component of a Reactome physical-entity set/complex (PwGroup) — typically gene entities appearing in transcriptional complexes (e.g. 'ARC' gene part-of 'AP-1 dimers:ARC gene', 'p-S133-CREB1:MEF2D:SRF:ARC gene').
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: member_of (high, gene entity is a member of the complex/set); part_of (high alternative)
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = Gene (a); object = Reactome PwGroup complex/set (b). Asymmetric. Edge carries Reactome 'version'.

spoke_edges.meaning: Geographic containment (GeoNames): a location is part of a larger location (e.g. 'St Saviour' part-of 'Jersey'; 'Laborie' part-of 'Saint Lucia'). Encodes administrative geographic nesting.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: part_of (high, geographic containment); located_in is a plausible alternative (medium)
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = smaller/contained Location (a); object = larger/containing Location (b). Asymmetric. Note some source Location nodes have empty identifier/name.

spoke_edges.meaning: A protein domain (InterPro/Pfam) is part of a protein — it is annotated onto a sequence span of that protein (e.g. 'Glycoside hydrolase 123, N-terminal domain' part-of protein A0A3R6BKY4). The 'start'/'end' edge properties give the residue coordinates of the domain within the protein.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: part_of (high); located_in also fits given start/end residue coordinates (medium)
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = ProteinDomain (a); object = Protein (b). Asymmetric (domain -part_of-> protein). By far the largest reltype in this set (~48M edges); positional 'start'/'end' props are load-bearing metadata.

spoke_edges.meaning: A Reactome physical-entity complex/set is a component of a larger complex/set (e.g. 'EGFR:EGF-like ligands' part-of 'EGF-like ligands:EGFR dimer'). Encodes nested assembly of molecular complexes.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: part_of (high); member_of (high alternative) since a sub-complex is a member/component of the larger complex
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = sub-complex/component PwGroup (a); object = larger containing PwGroup (b). Asymmetric. Edge carries Reactome 'version'.

spoke_edges.meaning: A Protein is a subunit/member of a protein Complex (CellChatDB ligand-receptor complexes, e.g. proteins 'NRP2' and 'PLXNA1' are part of complex 'NRP2_PLXNA1'; 'FZD7' part of 'FZD7_LRP5').
edge_sources: CellChatDB (from Complex node 'source' property; edge itself has no source property)
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: member_of (high, protein is a subunit/member of the complex); part_of (high alternative)
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = Protein subunit (a); object = Complex (b). Asymmetric. Edge carries NO properties; provenance (CellChatDB) lives on the Complex node's 'source'.

spoke_edges.meaning: A Protein is a component of a Reactome physical-entity complex/set (PwGroup) (e.g. 'EGFR' and 'AAMP' proteins part-of the 'EGFR:AAMP' complex). Component-of-complex, analogous to PpCP but for Reactome-defined sets.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: member_of (high, protein is a member/subunit of the complex); part_of (high alternative)
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = Protein (a); object = Reactome PwGroup complex/set (b). Asymmetric. Edge carries Reactome 'version'.

spoke_edges.meaning: A biochemical Reaction is part of a Pathway (Reactome): the reaction is one of the steps that make up the pathway (e.g. 'Phosphorylation of EGFR by SRC kinase', 'EGFR binds EGF ligand' are part-of 'Signaling by EGFR').

example.a_name: Phosphorylation of EGFR by SRC kinase

spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: part_of (high); a reaction being a step of a pathway also reads as participates_in (medium)
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = Reaction (a); object = Pathway (b). Asymmetric (reaction -part_of-> pathway). Edge carries Reactome 'version'.

spoke_edges.meaning: A proprietary supplement Blend contains a specific chemical Compound as a listed ingredient. Sourced from NHANES dietary-supplement label data; edges carry an ingredient category (Vitamin, Mineral, Amino Acid, Other).
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: part_of (high) with the Compound as part_of the Blend; equivalently the Blend 'has_part' the Compound. In BioOKF's subject->object convention this is best expressed as Compound part_of Blend (high confidence). No strong alternative predicate.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: SPOKE stores Blend->Compound (Blend CONTAINS Compound). BioOKF subject is the Compound (part_of the Blend), so the BioOKF edge direction is reversed relative to the stored SPOKE direction. Not symmetric (whole/part).

spoke_edges.meaning: A proprietary supplement Blend contains a whole Food/botanical ingredient (e.g., ginger root, garlic bulb). Membership of a food item in a named supplement blend, from NHANES label data.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: part_of (high): the Food is part_of the Blend (Blend has_part Food). No competing predicate.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: SPOKE stores Blend->Food. BioOKF subject is the Food (Food part_of Blend), so BioOKF direction is reversed from stored direction. Whole/part; not symmetric.

spoke_edges.meaning: A Chromosome contains/is subdivided into a Cytoband (chromosomal band). Pure genomic structural hierarchy; the edge records the genome build (HG38).
edge_sources: (no source/sources property; provenance encoded as build=HG38, i.e. Ensembl/UCSC cytoband model)
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: part_of (high): Cytoband part_of Chromosome (Chromosome has_part Cytoband). Could secondarily be read as located_in, but part_of is the canonical structural fit.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: SPOKE stores Chromosome->Cytoband (whole->part). BioOKF subject is the Cytoband (Cytoband part_of Chromosome), so BioOKF direction is reversed. Not symmetric.

spoke_edges.meaning: Assigns a Gene to the Cytoband (chromosomal band) it physically resides in, i.e. its cytogenetic location. Despite the 'CONTAINS' verb the stored source node is the Gene and the target is the Cytoband, so semantically the Cytoband contains/locates the Gene. From Ensembl HG38 gene coordinates.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: located_in (high): Gene located_in Cytoband; equivalently part_of (Gene part_of Cytoband region). located_in is the closest fit for cytogenetic localization.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: SPOKE stores Gene->Cytoband. The verb label ('CcG' = Cytoband contains Gene) is inverted relative to storage; semantically the containing entity is the Cytoband. BioOKF subject is the Gene (Gene located_in Cytoband), which matches the stored source->target direction. Not symmetric.

spoke_edges.meaning: A marketed DietarySupplement product contains a named proprietary Blend as a component. Edge records quantity, unit, and an operation qualifier; from NHANES supplement-label data.

example.a_name: SILVER SAGE THERMOGENICS PLUS QUICK START

spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: part_of (high): Blend part_of DietarySupplement (product has_part Blend). Quantity/unit make it a compositional part-of.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: SPOKE stores DietarySupplement->Blend (product->component). BioOKF subject is the Blend (Blend part_of DietarySupplement), so BioOKF direction is reversed from stored direction. Not symmetric.

spoke_edges.meaning: A marketed DietarySupplement product contains a specific chemical Compound (active/ingredient) at a stated amount. Edge records quantity, unit, an operator (e.g. comparison), and an ingredient category; from NHANES.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: part_of (high): Compound part_of DietarySupplement (product has_part Compound at a dose). No competing predicate.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: SPOKE stores DietarySupplement->Compound. BioOKF subject is the Compound (Compound part_of DietarySupplement), so BioOKF direction is reversed from stored direction. Not symmetric.

spoke_edges.meaning: A Food contains a chemical Compound/nutrient at a measured content level. Edge records content amount, original unit, and the food name string; provenance is nutrient databases (FooDB, ANZ, etc.).
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: part_of (high) as compositional containment (Compound part_of Food); with the quantitative content it also carries a 'measures/has content' flavor, but the structural predicate is part_of. Confidence high for part_of.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: SPOKE stores Food->Compound. BioOKF subject is the Compound (Compound part_of Food), so BioOKF direction is reversed from stored direction. Not symmetric.

spoke_edges.meaning: A PharmacologicClass (FDA/DrugCentral class such as a Mechanism of Action or Physiologic Effect) includes a drug Compound as a member of that class. class_type distinguishes MoA vs PE (physiologic effect) etc.; edge notes an 'unbiased' flag and license.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: member_of (high): Compound member_of PharmacologicClass (class includes Compound). is_a is a weaker alternative if the class is treated as a type. Confidence high for member_of.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: SPOKE stores PharmacologicClass->Compound (class INCLUDES compound). BioOKF subject is the Compound (Compound member_of PharmacologicClass), so BioOKF direction is reversed from stored direction. Not symmetric.

spoke_edges.meaning: A pharmacogenomic star-allele Haplotype (e.g. CYP2A6*19) belongs to / is defined on a Gene. Assigns each allele definition to its parent gene. Edge is bare (no properties).
edge_sources: (no edge source property; haplotype allele nomenclature, PharmVar/PharmGKB style via node identifiers)
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: part_of (medium-high): Haplotype part_of Gene (an allele/haplotype is a variant form belonging to the gene). member_of is an acceptable alternative reading. Confidence medium-high; part_of preferred.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: SPOKE stores Haplotype->Gene (haplotype BELONGS_TO gene). BioOKF subject is the Haplotype (Haplotype part_of Gene), matching the stored source->target direction. Not symmetric.

spoke_edges.meaning: A sequence Variant belongs to a Gene by genomic overlap/proximity. The r.category qualifier records the positional relationship ('within single gene', 'within multiple genes by overlap', 'near gene, upstream/downstream', 'asserted, but not computed'), i.e. a location-based gene assignment. Distinct from MAPS_VmG (which is an OpenTargets scored functional mapping).
edge_sources: (no edge source/sources property populated; dbSNP-style positional gene assignment)
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: located_in (medium) for 'within gene' cases (Variant located_in Gene) and associated_with (medium) as a generic fallback given the mixed 'near gene' categories. BioOKF has no dedicated variant-in-gene predicate; located_in preferred when category is 'within', otherwise associated_with. Confidence medium.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: SPOKE stores Variant->Gene (variant BELONGS_TO gene). BioOKF subject is the Variant (Variant located_in / associated_with Gene), matching the stored source->target direction. Not symmetric.

spoke_edges.meaning: A sequence Variant (rsID) belongs to / is a defining component of a star-allele Haplotype. Edge records the reference and alternative alleles and the variant type (substitution, deletion, insertion) that this variant contributes to the haplotype definition. From PharmVar.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: part_of (high): Variant part_of Haplotype (the variant is a constituent of the haplotype definition). member_of is an alternative. Confidence high for part_of.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: SPOKE stores Variant->Haplotype (variant BELONGS_TO haplotype). BioOKF subject is the Variant (Variant part_of Haplotype), matching the stored source->target direction. Not symmetric.

spoke_edges.meaning: A cancer CellLine harbors a somatic/germline sequence Variant. Rich mutation-annotation edge from the Cancer Cell Line Encyclopedia: genome change, variant classification, allele counts across assays (WES/WGS/RNAseq), ExAC AF, TCGA/COSMIC hotspot flags, protein/cDNA change, and deleteriousness.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: has_phenotype is a weak fit; the best fit is associated_with (medium) for 'cell line carries variant', or a genotype 'has variant' relation. Since BioOKF lacks a dedicated 'harbors_variant' predicate, map to associated_with (medium confidence). Not treats/causes.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: SPOKE stores CellLine->Variant (cell line HAS variant). BioOKF subject is the CellLine (CellLine associated_with Variant), matching the stored source->target direction. Not symmetric.

spoke_edges.meaning: A Protein has an Enzyme Commission (EC) number, i.e. is annotated with a catalytic enzyme classification / activity. Very high count (all UniProt enzyme annotations). Edge sourced from UniProt.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: catalyzes (medium-high): the protein catalyzes the reaction denoted by the EC class; alternatively is_a / member_of if EC is treated as an enzyme-family classification. Best BioOKF fit is catalyzes (protein->enzymatic activity). Confidence medium-high; member_of/participates_in are secondary.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: SPOKE stores Protein->EC (protein HAS EC activity). BioOKF subject is the Protein (Protein catalyzes/member_of EC activity), matching the stored source->target direction. Not symmetric.

spoke_edges.meaning: A Compound has a chemical/biological role, where the role is itself represented as a ChEBI Compound node (a role class such as 'plant metabolite', 'fragrance', 'NMR solvent', 'opioid analgesic'). Classifies a chemical by its functional/application role. From ChEBI.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: is_a (medium) / member_of (medium): the compound has/is-a member of a role class. Since the object is a ChEBI role term, member_of a role category is the closest fit; is_a acceptable. Not participates_in. Confidence medium.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: SPOKE stores Compound(chemical)->Compound(role) (chemical HAS_ROLE role). BioOKF subject is the chemical Compound (Compound member_of/is_a Role), matching the stored source->target direction. Self-loop label type (Compound->Compound) but asymmetric (chemical->role); not symmetric.

spoke_edges.meaning: A sequence Variant maps to a Gene as its most-likely functional/effector gene, with an OpenTargets Locus-to-Gene (L2G) Score. This is the large-scale scored variant-to-gene mapping (V2G/L2G), distinct from the smaller positional BELONGS_VbG. From OpenTargets.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: associated_with (high): Variant associated_with Gene via a scored functional mapping. located_in is a weaker alternative but the Score/L2G semantics are functional, not purely positional, so associated_with is preferred. Confidence high.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: SPOKE stores Variant->Gene (variant MAPS_TO gene). BioOKF subject is the Variant (Variant associated_with Gene), matching the stored source->target direction. Not symmetric.

spoke_edges.meaning: A CellLine derives from / was established from a tissue affected by a Disease, i.e. the disease of origin of the cell line (e.g. a leukemia cell line derived from childhood T-cell ALL). From Cellosaurus.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: derives_from (high): CellLine derives_from Disease(-affected tissue). associated_with is a weaker fallback. Confidence high for derives_from (predicate name matches directly).
spoke_edges.direction_notes: SPOKE stores CellLine->Disease (cell line DERIVES_FROM disease). BioOKF subject is the CellLine (CellLine derives_from Disease), matching the stored source->target direction. Not symmetric.

spoke_edges.meaning: A LOINC clinical laboratory test measures/quantifies something whose target component is an anatomical structure. Links a LOINC lab code to the Anatomy (UBERON) term that the assay is about (e.g. a liver fibrosis score or liver-antigen antibody test -> 'liver'). Encodes that the lab result characterizes that anatomical entity.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: measures (high confidence). The SPOKE verb MEASURES maps directly to the BioOKF 'measures' predicate.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = ClinicalLab, object = Anatomy (BioOKF: ClinicalLab measures Anatomy). Directed, not symmetric; the lab test is always the measuring agent.

spoke_edges.meaning: A LOINC clinical lab test measures/quantifies a biological process (GO BP). Links a lab assay to the physiological process it interrogates (e.g. coagulation-timing or clot-formation assays -> GO:0050817 'coagulation').
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: measures (high confidence).
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = ClinicalLab, object = BiologicalProcess. Directed; the lab test is the measuring agent, not symmetric.

spoke_edges.meaning: A LOINC clinical lab test measures/quantifies a chemical Compound analyte. This is the largest MEASURES variant: links a lab code to the small molecule / chemical it assays (e.g. an Estriol serum concentration test -> the compound Estriol). Represents the 'analyte = compound' component of a LOINC code.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: measures (high confidence).
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = ClinicalLab, object = Compound. Directed; lab test measures the compound. Not symmetric.

spoke_edges.meaning: A LOINC clinical lab test measures/quantifies a subcellular cellular component (GO CC). Links a lab assay to the cellular structure it targets (e.g. a basement-membrane antibody test -> GO:0005604 'basement membrane').
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: measures (high confidence).
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = ClinicalLab, object = CellularComponent. Directed; not symmetric.

spoke_edges.meaning: A LOINC clinical lab test measures/quantifies a cell type (Cell Ontology). Links a lab code to the cell population it counts or characterizes (e.g. a CD1a marker cell-fraction assay -> a CL cell type). Note some mappings are imprecise (broad marker panels mapped to specific CL terms), reflecting automated LOINC->ontology alignment.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: measures (high confidence).
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = ClinicalLab, object = CellType. Directed; not symmetric.

spoke_edges.meaning: A LOINC clinical lab test measures/quantifies a molecular function (GO MF). Smallest MEASURES variant. Links a lab assay to the molecular activity it interrogates. Mappings can be coarse (e.g. a mitochondrial-antibody test mapped to GO:0000010 enzyme activity), an artifact of automated term matching.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: measures (high confidence).
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = ClinicalLab, object = MolecularFunction. Directed; not symmetric.

spoke_edges.meaning: A LOINC clinical lab test measures/detects an organism (pathogen/microbe, NCBI Taxonomy). Links a microbiology/serology lab code to the organism it assays for (e.g. a Neisseria meningitidis DNA/antigen/antibody test -> the organism Neisseria meningitidis). Represents detection of infectious agents.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: measures (high confidence); could secondarily be read as 'detects', but BioOKF 'measures' covers the assay-quantifies/detects semantics.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = ClinicalLab, object = Organism. Directed; not symmetric.

spoke_edges.meaning: A LOINC clinical lab test measures/quantifies a Protein analyte (UniProt). Links a lab code to the protein it assays (e.g. protein electrophoresis / specific protein deficiency panels -> a UniProt protein such as PROS_HUMAN P07225). Represents the 'analyte = protein' component of a LOINC code.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: measures (high confidence).
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = ClinicalLab, object = Protein. Directed; not symmetric.

spoke_edges.meaning: A LOINC clinical lab test is performed/measured IN an anatomical location, i.e. the body site or specimen source (the LOINC 'System'/specimen axis) rather than the analyte itself. Links a lab code to the Anatomy (UBERON) tissue/site the sample comes from or the test targets (e.g. 'Biopsy:Imp:Pt:Muscle' -> 'muscle tissue'). Much larger than MEASURES_CLmA because most labs have a specimen site.
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: measures (medium-high confidence) with a locational nuance; the 'IN' semantics (measured within/at a site) could also inform located_in, but the edge is fundamentally a measurement-context relation so BioOKF 'measures' is the primary mapping.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = ClinicalLab, object = Anatomy (the site measured in). Directed; not symmetric. Distinct from MEASURES_CLmA: MEASURESIN captures specimen/system location, MEASURES captures the analyte/component being an anatomical entity.

spoke_edges.meaning: A LOINC clinical lab test is performed/measured IN a specific cell type (Cell Ontology), i.e. the cellular specimen/system the assay is run on (e.g. an egg-specimen microbiology count -> 'egg cell'; a muscle biopsy -> 'smooth muscle cell'). The cell-type analogue of MEASURESIN_CLmA (measurement context, not analyte).
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: measures (medium-high confidence), locational nuance as with MEASURESIN_CLmA; primary mapping 'measures'.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = ClinicalLab, object = CellType (measured in). Directed; not symmetric. Contrast with MEASURES_CLmCT (analyte cell type).

spoke_edges.meaning: Epidemiological disease-burden edge: a Disease has a measured prevalence in a geographic Location. Carries the quantitative prevalence estimate (value as a percent, with lower/upper uncertainty bounds and a year) for that disease in that country/region, sourced from IHME Global Burden of Disease. Very high cardinality (disease x country x year).
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: associated_with (medium confidence) as an epidemiological disease-location association; BioOKF has no dedicated 'prevalence' predicate, and 'measures' fits poorly since the subject is a Disease not an assay. Best mapped to associated_with (Disease associated_with Location) carrying the prevalence value; could alternatively be reported_in.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = Disease, object = Location (BioOKF: Disease associated_with Location). Directed; not symmetric. Numeric prevalence lives on the edge.

spoke_edges.meaning: A social determinant of health (SDoH, a SNOMED finding/situation such as 'Housing insecurity') has a measured prevalence IN a geographic Location (US census tract, GEOID). Carries the indicator value (e.g. '21.2%'), the underlying survey variable, estimation method (e.g. 'Crude prevalence'), time period and release year, from CDC PLACES local-health data. Highest cardinality of the set (indicator x census-tract).
edge_sources: PLACES: Local Data for Better Health, Census Tract Data 2024 release (CDC PLACES)
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: associated_with (medium confidence): an SDoH-indicator-to-location prevalence association. No BioOKF 'prevalence' predicate; 'measures' is a poor fit (subject is an SDoH finding, not a lab). Map to associated_with with the value on the edge; reported_in is a secondary possibility.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = SDoH, object = Location (BioOKF: SDoH associated_with Location). Directed; not symmetric. Location nodes here are census-tract GEOIDs (b_name often null; use identifier).

spoke_edges.meaning: Epidemiological mortality edge: a Disease has a measured mortality burden in a geographic Location. Carries absolute deaths (value), mortality_per_100k, the population denominator, and the WHO GHE cause code, sourced from the World Health Organization Global Health Estimates. Country-level (much lower cardinality than PREVALENCE_DpL).
spoke_edges.biookf_predicate_mapping: associated_with (medium confidence) as a disease-location mortality-burden association; no dedicated BioOKF mortality/prevalence predicate. Map to associated_with carrying mortality metrics on the edge; reported_in secondary.
spoke_edges.direction_notes: Subject = Disease, object = Location (BioOKF: Disease associated_with Location). Directed; not symmetric. Sibling of PREVALENCE_DpL but with mortality rather than prevalence metrics.

biookf.name: Gene
biookf.definition: A heritable genomic locus / gene / ncRNA-miRNA gene: the unit of heredity, typed by identity (the locus itself), distinct from its transcript or protein product (which are Molecule). The gene->product relation is the forward 'encodes' edge; there is no 'encoded_by' inverse. SCHEMA typing test (SPEC 5.D): heritable locus = Gene; a specific transcript/RNA = Molecule(subtype: rna).
biookf.identifier_pattern: Human-readable gene symbol as the bundle-unique identifier (e.g. 'ABCC8', 'ABL1', 'MAPK1', 'NR3C1'); occasionally a descriptive label ('5-HT6 receptor'). NO xref CURIE on any Gene node (0/619). in_taxon is absent (0/619) despite SCHEMA recommending it. Synonyms present on 499/619. Critically, many identifiers are gene-PRODUCT names, not loci: subtype='protein' set includes HBsAg, MAPK1/3, GSR, HP, keratins - the BioRED corpus conflates the gene and its protein under one Gene node.
xref_namespaces: benchmark-actual: NONE (0/619 nodes carry any xref)
biookf.mapping_strategy: Waterfall step 1 (auto-map): type==Gene + identifier is an exact HGNC-approved symbol -> SPOKE Gene by exact symbol/name match; this covers the majority ('general' subtype, standard symbols). Because there are zero xrefs, name/symbol is the ONLY join key, so normalize case and resolve symbol->HGNC via a lexicon before matching. Step 2 (synonym match): fall back to SPOKE Gene synonyms for aliases. Step 3 (LLM/semantic adjudication REQUIRED): whenever the Gene node is actually naming a protein product (subtype='protein'/'receptor'/'enzyme'/'viral protein', or identifier like HBsAg) decide Gene vs Protein target; also for non-human/ambiguous symbols (Drosophila, viral) and free-text descriptive labels.
biookf.pitfalls: PRIMARY collision: BioRED collapses gene and gene-product into one Gene node, so a single node may legitimately map to SPOKE Gene, SPOKE Protein, or both - subtype and identifier form decide, and this is the most frequent ambiguity here. No xrefs and no in_taxon means matching is purely lexical and species-blind: same symbol can collide across organisms (human vs Drosophila vs viral). Gene 'encodes' Molecule is nearly unused (3 edges) so the product is usually not modeled as a separate node. Provenance ('reported_in' to Publication) is the dominant outgoing edge and has no SPOKE analogue - do not emit it as a biomedical edge.

biookf.name: Molecule
biookf.definition: A single chemical or macromolecular entity: protein, drug, compound, metabolite, antibody, ion, complex, or RNA species (mRNA/miRNA/lncRNA). Typed by identity as ONE entity (a grouping is MolecularClass; a 3D coordinate model is Structure that derives_from the Molecule; a heritable locus is Gene). This is a chemically/structurally heterogeneous umbrella whose SPOKE target is subtype-dependent.
subtypes_seen: and ~15 other single-instance agent-coined drug-descriptor tokens
biookf.identifier_pattern: Human-readable chemical/drug name as bundle-unique identifier (e.g. 'ATP', '2,3,7,8-tetrachlorodibenzo-p-dioxin', 'L-arginine', 'MK-801', 'ACE inhibitor'). Ranges from tidy drug names to research-code compounds (17-DMAG, EPZ015666) to biomolecule names (DNA, EGF, prolactin). NO xref on any node (0/337); synonyms on 197/337.
xref_namespaces: SCHEMA-canonical: UniProtKB (protein), CHEBI/PUBCHEM.COMPOUND (compound), DRUGBANK/RXNORM (drug), CHEMBL, RNACENTRAL/ENSEMBL (RNA)
biookf.mapping_strategy: Waterfall is strongly subtype-gated. Step 1 (auto-map, high confidence): subtype in {drug, small_molecule, metabolite, and specific drug-class descriptors} + exact name match -> SPOKE Compound. subtype in {protein, peptide, antibody, biologic, hormone naming a protein like prolactin} -> SPOKE Protein by name/synonym. Step 2 (synonym): use SPOKE Compound/Protein synonym lists for brand/alias/research-code names. Step 3 (LLM/semantic REQUIRED): (a) subtype in {drug class, statin, NSAID, 'inhibitor', 'anticoagulant'...} is actually a CLASS not an instance -> re-route to SPOKE PharmacologicClass or MolecularClass semantics, NOT Compound; (b) generic biomolecules (DNA, ATP, EGF) and research codes with no clean CHEBI/DrugBank name; (c) protein-vs-compound disambiguation when subtype='general'.
biookf.pitfalls: Molecule->Compound vs Molecule->Protein is the core subtype-dependent split; guessing Compound for a protein (or vice versa) is a hard error. Many agent-coined 'drug class' style subtypes (statin, NSAID, atypical antipsychotic, 'drug class') are really PharmacologicClass/MolecularClass groupings mis-housed under Molecule - these must NOT map to a single SPOKE Compound. RNA-species Molecules could collide with Gene nodes of the same symbol. Zero xrefs forces lexical matching, so isomer/salt/stereochemistry distinctions collapse. Negation present: not_affects_response_to (13), not_regulates, not_causes - only assert the contradicting not_* against SPOKE when a positive SPOKE edge actually exists.

biookf.name: MolecularClass
biookf.definition: A GROUPING of molecular entities rather than a single one: drug class, protein family, protein domain, gene set/signature, or chemical class. Members attach to it via the 'member_of' edge. The discriminating test (SPEC 5.D): one entity = Molecule; a grouping/family/domain/gene-set = MolecularClass.
biookf.identifier_pattern: Human-readable class/family name as identifier: 'BMP', 'C-type lectin', 'ESCRT-III', 'G protein-coupled receptor', 'membrane protein', 'selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors'. All subtype='general' (the agent did not differentiate pharmacologic vs protein_family vs chemical_class). NO xref (0/6); synonyms on 5/6. Note these are semantically mixed: protein families (C-type lectin, GPCR, ESCRT-III), a signaling family (BMP), a broad chemical/pharmacologic class (SSRIs).
xref_namespaces: SCHEMA-canonical: ATC, NCIT, INTERPRO, PFAM, MSIGDB
biookf.mapping_strategy: Because subtype is uniformly 'general' and there are no xrefs, the SPOKE target label must be inferred from the identifier semantics by LLM/semantic adjudication - little can auto-map on a type match alone. Heuristic within the waterfall: protein-family names (C-type lectin, ESCRT-III, G protein-coupled receptor) -> SPOKE ProteinFamily (or ProteinDomain for domain-named ones); pharmacologic/drug-class names (selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors) -> SPOKE PharmacologicClass; ligand/signaling families (BMP) -> ProteinFamily. Step 1 auto-map only when the identifier exactly matches a SPOKE ProteinFamily/PharmacologicClass name; otherwise defer to LLM to choose the family vs domain vs pharmacologic-class SPOKE label.
biookf.pitfalls: Target label is not fixed by BioOKF type - one MolecularClass type spreads across three distinct SPOKE labels (ProteinFamily, ProteinDomain, PharmacologicClass) so choosing among them is mandatory adjudication. Collision with Molecule: pharmacologic-class tokens (SSRIs) also appear as Molecule subtypes ('statin','NSAID','drug class'), so class-vs-instance must be decided consistently. 'membrane protein' is a very broad functional grouping that may have no clean SPOKE family node. Tiny n (6) means low coverage; do not over-fit. member_of edges into these classes are almost absent (4 total), so membership must often be inferred rather than read.

biookf.name: Variant
biookf.definition: A DEVIATION from the reference sequence: SNV, indel, CNV/SV, allele, genotype, haplotype, fusion, STR. Discriminating test (SPEC 5.D): a deviation from reference = Variant; a region of the reference (enhancer, promoter, UTR) = SequenceFeature. Variant CONSEQUENCE (missense, splice-donor, 5'UTR) is an ATTRIBUTE on the variant (here carried in stats.qualifier / subtype), never a node; structural partonomy (variant part_of a Gene) is an edge.
subtypes_seen: and ~15 other consequence/mechanism tokens (consequence is really an attribute, coined into subtype here)
biookf.identifier_pattern: Human-readable variant description as identifier, in mixed notations: HGVS-ish protein/cDNA ('+2740 A>G', '1858C/T', '-134delA'), rsID form (57/321 match ^rs\d+), allele names ('1A1 allele'), and prose descriptors ('105-bp deletion','-1607 promoter polymorphism'). NO xref (0/321) - so no dbSNP/ClinVar CURIE even for the 57 rs-style ones; synonyms on 214/321. Consequence lives in subtype and stats.qualifier, not as its own field.
xref_namespaces: benchmark-actual: NONE (rsID appears only inside the human-readable identifier string, never as a resolved xref)
biookf.mapping_strategy: Step 1 (auto-map): identifier is a clean rsID (^rs\d+, ~57 nodes) -> SPOKE Variant by exact rsID match; this is the only reliable auto-join since SPOKE Variants are keyed by dbSNP. Step 2 (contextual match): non-rs variants must be resolved via their located_in/part_of Gene + the change notation ('1858C/T' in PTPN22) to a SPOKE Variant - requires the gene context edge, not the identifier alone. Step 3 (LLM/semantic REQUIRED, the majority): prose/positional descriptors, allele names, haplotypes, fusions, and legacy notations that need normalization to HGVS/rsID before any match; many will have no SPOKE Variant node at all and remain unmapped.
biookf.pitfalls: Only ~18% of identifiers are rsIDs; the rest are non-standard notations with no xref, so most Variants cannot auto-map and need gene-anchored normalization or stay unmapped. rsID is embedded in a free-text identifier, easy to miss - parse it out. subtype conflates the variant TYPE (snv/indel/cnv) with its CONSEQUENCE (missense/nonsense/frameshift), which per SCHEMA is an attribute not a subtype - don't treat consequence tokens as structural class. located_in points to Gene (147) and part_of to Gene (114) - use these as the disambiguating context but never invent exon/intron nodes. Heavy negation: not_associated_with (32) and not_predisposes_to (6) from Variants - only contradict a SPOKE edge that positively exists. SPOKE Variant is human/dbSNP-centric, so non-human or novel variants have no target.

biookf.name: SequenceFeature
biookf.definition: A REGION/element of the REFERENCE genome with functional or structural role: enhancer, promoter, silencer, TFBS, CpG island, open chromatin, transposon, locus, motif, repeat element, protein/functional domain-as-region. Discriminating test (SPEC 5.D): region of reference = SequenceFeature; deviation from reference = Variant. Exon/intron/CDS/codon are expressed as part_of EDGES, not SequenceFeature nodes.
biookf.identifier_pattern: Human-readable feature name as identifier: 'Alu element', 'D9S180' (a marker), 'DFNA36 locus', 'DFNB7/B11 locus', 'carbohydrate recognition domain', 'ligand binding domain', 'nuclear localization signal'. NO xref (0/7); synonyms on 6/7. Mix of genomic regions (Alu, microsatellite marker, disease loci) and protein sequence/functional domains/motifs.
xref_namespaces: SCHEMA-canonical: SO, ENSEMBL, Ensembl Regulatory Build / ENCODE cCRE
spoke_targets: SequenceFeature (SPOKE has no clean regulatory-region label; several have no direct target)
biookf.mapping_strategy: No auto-map on type alone - SPOKE lacks a general regulatory-region node, so this is almost entirely LLM/semantic adjudication. Within the waterfall: protein sequence/functional domains ('carbohydrate recognition domain','ligand binding domain','nuclear localization signal') -> SPOKE ProteinDomain if an exact/synonym match exists; genomic loci/markers ('DFNA36 locus','D9S180') -> best resolved to the associated Gene/region context rather than a dedicated SPOKE node; repeat elements (Alu, microsatellite) typically have NO SPOKE target and stay unmapped. Decide target label per node from the identifier semantics.
biookf.pitfalls: Heterogeneous: genomic regions vs protein domains map to entirely different SPOKE labels (or none). Collision with Variant: subtype 'microsatellite' appears in BOTH SequenceFeature (the reference locus) and Variant (a repeat expansion) - must key on reference-vs-deviation, not the token. Collision with ProteinDomain-flavored MolecularClass. Disease-loci names (DFNA36) are region labels not diseases - do not map to SPOKE Disease. Tiny n (7); very low coverage. part_of edges express partonomy into Gene - do not fabricate exon/intron nodes.

biookf.name: Structure
biookf.definition: A resolved or predicted 3D atomic-coordinate model of a macromolecule (x-ray, cryo-EM, NMR, predicted), which 'derives_from' the Molecule it models. Discriminating test (SPEC 5.D / 5.D Structure vs Molecule): the chemical entity is a Molecule; its 3D coordinate model is a Structure. NOTE: in this benchmark the agent used 'Structure' loosely for macromolecular ASSEMBLIES / cellular structures rather than PDB coordinate models.
biookf.identifier_pattern: Human-readable structure/assembly name as identifier: 'BBSome','caveolae','desmosome','extracellular matrix','major histocompatibility complex','microtubule','midbody','mitochondrial complex I','primary cilium','Birbeck granule'. NO xref (0/10) - no PDB/AlphaFoldDB IDs; synonyms on 7/10. These are macromolecular complexes / subcellular assemblies, NOT 3D coordinate files - a divergence from the SCHEMA 'atomic-coordinate model' definition.
biookf.mapping_strategy: No PDB/AlphaFold xref means the SCHEMA-intended PDB->coordinate mapping is impossible; this is entirely LLM/semantic adjudication over the identifier meaning. Because the benchmark's Structure nodes are actually cellular/subcellular assemblies, route by semantics: subcellular components ('caveolae','desmosome','microtubule','primary cilium','midbody','extracellular matrix') -> SPOKE Anatomy (subcellular/cellular-component) or GO cellular-component semantics; multiprotein complexes ('BBSome','MHC','mitochondrial complex I') -> SPOKE ProteinComplex/MolecularClass if such a node exists, else the constituent Proteins. No auto-map; decide per node.
biookf.pitfalls: Definition mismatch: SCHEMA says 3D coordinate model but the benchmark uses Structure for subcellular assemblies/complexes - do NOT expect PDB IDs and do not map to a coordinate-file node. Strong collision with Anatomy(subcellular) - SPOKE has no Structure label, so most map to Anatomy or a complex node, overlapping with what CellType/Anatomy already cover (part_of edges here point to CellType and Anatomy). 'genomic region' and 'cell junction' subtypes further blur into SequenceFeature/Anatomy territory. Tiny n (10); derives_from (the SCHEMA-canonical Structure->Molecule link) is entirely ABSENT in the benchmark, so the model->molecule lineage cannot be traced.

biookf.name: Anatomy
biookf.definition: A body region, organ, organ system, tissue, gross anatomical structure, subcellular component/organelle, or body fluid (SCHEMA/SPEC type #7). Type-by-identity: a physical location/structure of the body, distinct from a cell type (CellType) and from a process. Per SPEC §5.D, a cellular component/organelle aligns to Anatomy (subtype: subcellular / cell component), NOT to a BiologicalPathway or CellType. A raw number/coordinate is never a node.
biookf.identifier_pattern: Human-readable anatomical label, lowercase common name, no CURIE. E.g. 'brain', 'liver', 'lung', 'adipose tissue', 'CA1 region of hippocampus', 'endoplasmic reticulum', 'nucleus', 'sarcolemma'. Organelles (endoplasmic reticulum, nucleus) appear here as subcellular Anatomy. Xrefs are absent; only synonyms (36/52 nodes) disambiguate.
xref_namespaces: CL/CLO (canonical for subcellular-cell-context per SCHEMA cheatsheet grouping)
GO-CC (cellular component, implied for organelle subtype)
BENCHMARK: none present — 0 of 52 Anatomy nodes carry any xref
spoke_targets: CellularComponent (SPOKE, for subtype subcellular/organelle e.g. nucleus, ER)
biookf.mapping_strategy: Waterfall: (1) AUTO-MAP when node_type=Anatomy AND identifier or a synonym exactly/strongly matches a SPOKE Anatomy label (organ/tissue names like brain, liver, kidney, spleen map cleanly; UBERON-backed). (2) Route subcellular subtype (endoplasmic reticulum, nucleus, sarcolemma) to SPOKE CellularComponent, not Anatomy — split target by subtype. (3) DEFER to LLM/semantic adjudication for fine-grained brain subregions and organ subparts ('CA1 region of hippocampus','globus pallidus interna','urorectal septum','kidney cortex' vs 'kidney') where the correct UBERON grain and part_of parent are ambiguous, and for lexical variants ('CA3','myocardium' vs 'heart'). Because xrefs are absent, all mapping is name/synonym-driven → semantic matcher required as fallback.
biookf.pitfalls: (a) Subcellular collision: 'nucleus','endoplasmic reticulum','sarcolemma' are Anatomy(subcellular) here and must route to SPOKE CellularComponent, not organ-Anatomy — subtype-dependent target. (b) Anatomy vs CellType boundary: a compartment is Anatomy, a cell type/line is CellType (§5.D); do not conflate 'germinal center'(Anatomy) with immune cell types. (c) Anatomy is almost always an edge OBJECT (incoming located_in 43x, expressed_in 30x, mostly from Gene/Disease/Molecule); its only outgoing edges are reported_in provenance — so it is a target/anchor node, treat direction of located_in/expressed_in as X→Anatomy. (d) Missing xrefs mean no CURIE-facet pin; grain mismatches (region vs whole organ) are the main auto-map failure mode.

biookf.name: CellType
biookf.definition: A cell type, cell state, cell line, or organoid (SCHEMA/SPEC type #8). Type-by-identity: an individual kind or state of cell (or an immortalized line / organoid), distinct from the tissue/compartment that contains it (Anatomy) and from an organism. Per SPEC §5.D, a cell type/state/line/organoid = CellType; an organelle/compartment = Anatomy(subcellular).
biookf.identifier_pattern: Human-readable cell label, lowercase, no CURIE. Native cell types: 'B cell','T cell','macrophage','neuron','dopaminergic neuron','hematopoietic stem cell','podocyte','microglia'. Cell lines (subtype: cell line): 'HEK293 cells','MCF7/AdrR','LbetaT2','HEK cell'. Synonyms carry plural/lymphocyte variants (42/48 nodes have synonyms, e.g. 'B cell' → 'B cells','B lymphocytes'). No xrefs.
xref_namespaces: CLO (Cell Line Ontology, canonical for cell_line)
BENCHMARK: none present — 0 of 48 CellType nodes carry any xref
spoke_targets: CellLine (SPOKE, for subtype 'cell line' e.g. HEK293, MCF7/AdrR)
biookf.mapping_strategy: Waterfall: (1) AUTO-MAP when node_type=CellType, subtype!='cell line', and identifier/synonym exactly matches a SPOKE CellType label backed by CL (e.g. 'macrophage','B cell','dendritic cell','fibroblast','endothelial cell' map cleanly via CL). (2) Route subtype='cell line' (HEK293, MCF7/AdrR, LbetaT2, HEK cell) to SPOKE CellLine, not CellType — subtype-dependent target. (3) DEFER to LLM/semantic adjudication for compound/qualified cell descriptors that may not have a single CL term ('B3 serotonin neurons','glomerular capillary endothelial cell','keloid fibroblast','epithelial hair cell','airway basal cell'), and for near-synonym line vs type (e.g. 'HEK cell' vs 'HEK293 cells'). All matching is name/synonym-driven since xrefs are absent.
biookf.pitfalls: (a) Cell line vs cell type: subtype='cell line' must map to SPOKE CellLine; misrouting HEK293/MCF7 to CellType is wrong. (b) CellType vs Anatomy(subcellular): do not confuse cells with compartments (§5.D); 'peripheral blood mononuclear cells' is a cell population (CellType), not Anatomy. (c) 'tumor cell'/'cancer stem cell' are CellType, not Disease — type-by-identity. (d) CellType is both subject and object of expressed_in/located_in (gene expressed_in a cell type, cell type located_in an anatomy); watch direction — expressed_in incoming 32x (Gene→CellType), outgoing 9x (CellType→Anatomy). (e) No xrefs → CL grounding must be inferred by name; plural/synonym normalization needed before matching.

biookf.name: Organism
biookf.definition: A species, strain, taxon, or pathogen (bacterium/virus/fungus/parasite), microbe, model organism, or host (SCHEMA/SPEC type #9). Type-by-identity: a taxonomic entity. Per SPEC §5.D, a taxon/species/strain = Organism (distinct from a group of people = Population, and from the investigation = Study). A defined chemical exposure routes to Molecule; an infectious agent routes here to Organism.
biookf.identifier_pattern: Human-readable taxon name, mixed case; scientific binomials or common/pathogen names, no CURIE. Species: 'Mus musculus','Rattus norvegicus','Drosophila melanogaster','zebrafish','Crocus sativus'. Pathogens/viruses (subtype: virus): 'HIV-1','Hepatitis C virus','Dengue virus type 2','Human papillomavirus'. Bacteria: 'Neisseria meningitidis','Streptococcus pyogenes'. in_taxon field is present but NULL on all 19 (no NCBITaxon populated). 16/19 have synonyms.
xref_namespaces: NCBITaxon (canonical per SCHEMA cheatsheet and SPEC §9 xref table)
BENCHMARK: none present — 0 of 19 Organism nodes carry any xref and in_taxon is null on all of them
biookf.mapping_strategy: Waterfall: (1) AUTO-MAP when node_type=Organism and identifier/synonym resolves to a SPOKE Organism (NCBITaxon) — canonical binomials ('Mus musculus','Rattus norvegicus','Drosophila melanogaster') and well-known common names ('zebrafish'→Danio rerio,'HIV-1') map with high confidence via name→NCBITaxon lookup. (2) Normalize duplicate/variant identifiers pointing to the same taxon BEFORE mapping: 'Human immunodeficiency virus 1' == 'human immunodeficiency virus type 1' == 'HIV-1', and 'hepatitis B virus' — these are lexical duplicates of one taxon. (3) DEFER to LLM/semantic for genus-only or ambiguous grain ('Aedes','Plasmodium' — genus, not species) and rat/mouse STRAIN identifiers coined as subtypes ('spontaneously hypertensive rat','CD-1 mouse') where the target is the species-level Organism plus a strain qualifier. Because in_taxon and xref are empty, taxonomy resolution is entirely name-based.
biookf.pitfalls: (a) in_taxon is NULL and xref empty on every Organism node — the recommended NCBITaxon anchor is entirely missing, so all resolution is name-lexical and duplicate-prone. (b) Duplicate identifiers for one taxon (three HIV-1 spellings) will over-count and must be deduped before/at mapping. (c) Population vs Organism: a 'group of people' is Population, not Organism (§5.D) — do not route cohorts here. (d) Model-organism strains coined as subtypes ('CD-1 mouse') should map to the species Organism, not a novel taxon. (e) Organism participates in host-pathogen interacts_with (symmetric) and causes edges (pathogen→Disease); direction of causes is Organism→Disease. (f) Plant organisms ('Crocus sativus','Rhodiola rosea','Mangifera indica') are Organism, not Food — the food item would be a separate Food node linked by derives_from.

biookf.name: BiologicalPathway
biookf.definition: A PROCESS: a pathway, reaction, signaling cascade, GO biological process (GO-BP), physiologic or pathologic process, or behavior (SCHEMA/SPEC type #10). Per SPEC §5.D the discriminating test is process (BiologicalPathway) vs elemental molecular activity/GO-MF (BiologicalFunction); reactions live under BiologicalPathway and catalyzes points here. Absorbs the deprecated BiologicalProcess/Process types.
biookf.identifier_pattern: Human-readable process/pathway name, no CURIE. Signaling cascades: 'Akt signaling pathway','MAPK signaling pathway','Wnt signaling pathway','JAK-STAT signaling pathway','PI3K/Akt/mTOR signaling pathway'. Metabolic pathways: 'glycolysis','oxidative phosphorylation','tricarboxylic acid cycle','purine metabolism','cholesterol biosynthesis'. Named lexical/spelling variants coexist as separate nodes ('BMP signaling pathway' vs 'BMP signalling pathway'; 'NF-kB pathway' vs 'NF-kappaB signaling pathway'). 25/31 have synonyms. No xrefs.
xref_namespaces: GO (BP), REACT, KEGG, WIKIPATHWAYS, RHEA (canonical per SCHEMA/SPEC §9)
BENCHMARK: none present — 0 of 31 BiologicalPathway nodes carry any xref
spoke_targets: BiologicalProcess (SPOKE — GO-BP-flavored processes route here rather than to curated Pathway)
biookf.mapping_strategy: Waterfall: (1) AUTO-MAP curated canonical pathways whose identifier/synonym matches a SPOKE Pathway (Reactome/KEGG/WikiPathways-backed) name: 'glycolysis','oxidative phosphorylation','tricarboxylic acid cycle','Wnt signaling pathway' are strong matches. (2) Split target by flavor: GO-biological-process-style processes ('DNA mismatch repair','cholesterol biosynthesis','lipolysis') may map better to SPOKE BiologicalProcess than to the curated Pathway label. (3) DEFER to LLM/semantic adjudication to (i) collapse spelling/format variants ('signaling'/'signalling','NF-kB'/'NF-kappaB','MAPK'/'MAPK/ERK') to one target, and (ii) resolve informal cascade names (e.g. 'Smad signaling','EPOR signaling pathway') to the right GO/Reactome node. No xref means the pathway database anchor must be recovered semantically.
biookf.pitfalls: (a) BiologicalPathway vs BiologicalFunction is the central collision: a PROCESS/cascade is BiologicalPathway (→SPOKE Pathway/BiologicalProcess); an elemental GO-MF activity is BiologicalFunction (→SPOKE MolecularFunction). Misclassifying a signaling process as a function (or vice versa) routes to the wrong SPOKE label. (b) Dual SPOKE targets (Pathway vs BiologicalProcess) require a per-node decision — curated canonical pathway → Pathway; generic GO-BP process → BiologicalProcess. (c) Spelling/format duplicate nodes over-count and split evidence; dedupe before mapping. (d) BiologicalPathway is mostly an edge OBJECT: incoming participates_in (15x, Gene/Molecule→Pathway) and regulates (23x) and not_regulates (2x) — for negation, a not_regulates(X→pathway) must only be emitted to contradict an existing positive SPOKE regulates edge. (e) 'behavior'/'physiologic'/'pathologic' subtypes are allowed under this type but none appear (all 'general'); watch for behaviors mis-typed elsewhere.

biookf.name: BiologicalFunction
biookf.definition: An ELEMENTAL MOLECULAR ACTIVITY — a GO molecular function (GO-MF): catalytic, binding, or transporter activity of a gene product (SCHEMA/SPEC type #11). Per SPEC §5.D, distinguished from BiologicalPathway by process (pathway/cascade/GO-BP) vs elemental molecular activity (GO-MF). Maps to Biolink MolecularActivity / SPOKE MolecularFunction.
biookf.identifier_pattern: Human-readable activity/process label, lowercase, no CURIE. In this benchmark the nodes are broad cellular processes and functions: 'apoptosis','cell proliferation','cell migration','angiogenesis','DNA repair','autophagy','inflammation','oxidative stress','epithelial-mesenchymal transition','ferroptosis','hematopoiesis','metastasis','transcriptional regulation'. Note MANY are GO-BP-flavored process terms, not strict GO-MF catalytic/binding/transporter activities. 48/74 have synonyms. No xrefs.
xref_namespaces: BENCHMARK: none present — 0 of 74 BiologicalFunction nodes carry any xref
spoke_targets: BiologicalProcess (SPOKE — MANY benchmark nodes are actually GO-BP-style processes e.g. apoptosis, angiogenesis, and belong to BiologicalProcess, not MolecularFunction)
biookf.mapping_strategy: Waterfall: (1) AUTO-MAP only true GO-MF activities (catalytic/binding/transporter) by exact name/synonym to SPOKE MolecularFunction. (2) CRITICAL re-route: most benchmark 'BiologicalFunction' nodes are broad processes ('apoptosis','cell proliferation','angiogenesis','inflammation','autophagy','hematopoiesis','metastasis') that are GO-BP, so their correct SPOKE target is BiologicalProcess (or even a Pathway), NOT MolecularFunction — a per-node LLM/semantic classification (GO-MF vs GO-BP) MUST precede target selection. (3) DEFER to LLM for disease-adjacent processes that blur into Phenotype/Pathway ('cellular senescence','oxidative stress','endoplasmic reticulum stress','tumor growth') and for near-duplicate pairs ('DNA repair'/'DNA damage repair','epithelial-mesenchymal transition'/'epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition'). No xref → GO axis (MF vs BP) is inferred purely from the term semantically.
biookf.pitfalls: (a) The dominant pitfall: this type is spec-defined as GO-MF but the benchmark populated it overwhelmingly with GO-BP process terms — blindly mapping BiologicalFunction→SPOKE MolecularFunction would be wrong for the majority; classify GO axis per node and split targets (MolecularFunction vs BiologicalProcess). (b) BiologicalFunction vs BiologicalPathway boundary (§5.D) is fuzzy here and both may target SPOKE BiologicalProcess/Pathway. (c) Process-vs-Phenotype collision: 'inflammation','oxidative stress','cellular senescence' can also read as Phenotype/Disease facets — keep to the process facet unless the source frames a manifestation. (d) Heavy edge-object role: incoming regulates 108x + not_regulates 8x + causes 29x, mostly Gene→function; negation polarity — a not_regulates/not_associated_with edge must only contradict where a positive SPOKE regulates/associated_with edge exists, else it is unassertable. (e) Near-duplicate identifiers split evidence and should be deduped. (f) catalyzes range is BiologicalPathway(reaction), so enzyme→reaction should land on a Pathway node, not here — watch mis-linked catalyzes(3x incoming) targets.

biookf.name: Disease
biookf.definition: A diagnosed condition an organism *has* — a disposition/diagnosis: disease, syndrome, disorder, neoplasm, infection, injury, congenital/acquired abnormality (SCHEMA type #12; SPEC §5.A/§5.C). The test (§5.C): 'Does a clinician diagnose it and a patient have it?' Anchored to MONDO/DOID/ICD/SNOMED '(disorder)'. Distinct from the observable manifestation (Phenotype) and the measurable variable (BiomedicalMeasure); a Disease has_phenotype its signs/symptoms.
biookf.identifier_pattern: Plain human-readable diagnosis label, no CURIE, no ':' — e.g. "Alzheimer's disease", "Crohn's disease", "B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma", "22q11.2 deletion syndrome", "AIDS". 262/334 carry free-text synonyms; xref is empty for every Disease node (only Publications carry PMIDs in this benchmark).
xref_namespaces: SCHEMA/SPEC canonical: MONDO, DOID, OMIM, ICD10, MESH (+UMLS DISO CUI as glue)
Benchmark actual: NONE — 0/334 Disease nodes have any xref
biookf.mapping_strategy: Waterfall: (1) direct auto-map when BioOKF type==Disease AND identifier or a synonym exactly/normalized-matches a SPOKE Disease name (SPOKE Disease is MONDO-backed, so exact lexical hit on preferred label or synonym is high-confidence). (2) Because xrefs are ABSENT, there is no CURIE fast-path — matching is name/synonym-only; leverage the 262 synonym-bearing nodes. (3) Defer to LLM/semantic adjudication when the label is ambiguous, an abbreviation (e.g. 'AIDS'), a lay/eponymous term, or when a lexical match lands on a SPOKE Symptom/SideEffect instead of Disease (facet collision). Never fabricate a MONDO CURIE.
biookf.pitfalls: Trio collision: many source words are dual/triple-listed (hyperlipidemia = Disease + Phenotype 'elevated lipids' + BiomedicalMeasure 'LDL'); BioOKF facets by identity but without xref you cannot lean on the CURIE to pin the facet, so a name that is a Disease here may resolve to SPOKE Symptom. Benchmark subtype is almost always 'general', so subtype cannot disambiguate. Incoming edges are dense (Gene associated_with, Molecule/Variant/Gene causes/predisposes_to/treats) — a mis-typed target corrupts many edges. Negation: not_associated_with/not_causes/not_has_phenotype appear (34 Gene not_associated_with etc.); a not_* edge must only be emitted to CONTRADICT an existing positive SPOKE edge, never as a standalone assertion. Provenance targets (Publication via reported_in, 446 edges) have NO SPOKE equivalent and must not be mapped as Disease.

biookf.name: Phenotype
biookf.definition: An observable manifestation an organism *exhibits*: symptom, sign, side effect, qualitative trait, morphologic/behavioral feature (SCHEMA type #13; SPEC §5.A/§5.C). Test (§5.C): 'Is it observed/exhibited as a characteristic?' Anchored to HPO/MP/MedDRA/SYMP. subtype convention: symptom=subjective/patient-reported, sign=objective/observer-detected, side_effect=drug reaction. Distinct from the diagnosed Disease and the quantified BiomedicalMeasure.
biookf.identifier_pattern: Plain human-readable trait/sign/side-effect phrase — e.g. "QT interval prolongation", "T cell exhaustion", "aggression", "adverse skin reaction", "CA3 cell loss", "advanced maternal age". 133/240 carry synonyms; xref empty for all. Note the benchmark mixes true signs/symptoms with process-y and measure-adjacent phrasings.
xref_namespaces: SCHEMA/SPEC canonical: HP, MP, MEDDRA (side effects), SYMP
Benchmark actual: NONE — 0/240 Phenotype nodes have any xref
spoke_targets: PhenotypicFeature (Biolink; if no SPOKE Symptom/SideEffect match)
biookf.mapping_strategy: Waterfall: (1) subtype-aware target selection — a side_effect-flavored phenotype maps to SPOKE SideEffect (MedDRA-backed), a symptom/sign to SPOKE Symptom; but benchmark subtype is uniformly 'general', so this signal is UNAVAILABLE here and must be inferred from the label/edge context (e.g. object of a Molecule 'causes' edge from a drug ≈ side effect). (2) Auto-map only on exact/normalized name or strong synonym match to a SPOKE Symptom/SideEffect. (3) Defer to LLM for the large fraction of phrases that are not canonical HPO terms (composite descriptions, cellular phenotypes like 'T cell exhaustion').
biookf.pitfalls: Heaviest trio-collision type: same word spans Phenotype/Disease/BiomedicalMeasure. SPOKE splits manifestations into Symptom vs SideEffect — choosing the wrong one is a subtype-dependent target error, and the uniform 'general' subtype gives no help. Many benchmark 'Phenotype' labels are borderline BiomedicalMeasure ('2-hour plasma glucose level') or Disease — do not blindly force to Symptom. Incoming edges dominated by Molecule causes (128) and Disease has_phenotype (91): a target mis-map propagates. No xref means no HP CURIE fast-path. Negation: not_has_phenotype exists and must only contradict an existing positive SPOKE manifestation edge.

biookf.name: BiomedicalMeasure
biookf.definition: A named measurable variable — a quantity/analyte/score that carries a unit or value or comes from a test/score: lab test/result, vital, index (BMI, PRS, TNM), scale, biomarker readout, omics readout, imaging finding (SCHEMA type #14; SPEC §5.A/§5.C). Test: 'Does it take a value, or come from a test/score?' Anchored LOINC/OBA/EFO/PATO. The VALUE itself ('183 cm') is an edge attribute, never a node; the measure measures a Phenotype/Disease/Molecule.
biookf.identifier_pattern: Human-readable analyte/measurement name — e.g. "blood pressure", "serum creatinine", "bone mineral density", "waist-to-hip ratio", "PAI-1 serum level", "arylsulfatase A activity". 7/8 carry synonyms; xref empty for all 8.
xref_namespaces: SCHEMA/SPEC canonical: LOINC, NCIT, OBA, EFO
Benchmark actual: NONE — 0/8 nodes have any xref
spoke_targets: BiologicalProcess/MolecularFunction (for activity readouts e.g. 'arylsulfatase A activity')
Compound/Protein (when the measured analyte's underlying entity is what SPOKE models)
biookf.mapping_strategy: Waterfall: SPOKE has no clean ClinicalAttribute/Measurement node, so this type rarely auto-maps as itself. (1) Decompose: a measure often points (via 'measures') at a Disease/Phenotype/Molecule that DOES have a SPOKE target — map the edge target, not the measure node. (2) An activity readout ('arylsulfatase A activity') may semantically align to a SPOKE MolecularFunction/EC or to the Protein whose activity it is. (3) Otherwise defer to LLM/semantic adjudication or leave unmapped (provenance-style: keep as attribute). Never force a measure into SPOKE Disease/Symptom.
biookf.pitfalls: Core trio collision: measures are constantly confusable with the Phenotype/Disease they quantify ('blood pressure' the measure vs 'hypertension' the disease). A biomarker that is a protein is a Molecule (→Compound/Protein) while its measured level is the BiomedicalMeasure — subtype-dependent target. Only n=8 in benchmark, so lexical priors are thin. No SPOKE home node means over-eager mappers wrongly coerce it to Disease/Symptom. Negation present (not_associated_with -> Disease). The numeric value belongs on the edge (effect_size+unit+direction), never as a node — do not create a SPOKE node for a value.

biookf.name: MethodOrProcedure
biookf.definition: A technique or protocol: a clinical procedure (surgical/imaging/preventive/diagnostic/intervention/vaccination/screening) AND a lab assay/technique, computational pipeline/tool/software, statistical method (e.g. PCA), model, algorithm, or protocol (SCHEMA type #15; SPEC §5.A/§5.D). Type by identity: the technique is the node; its inputs/outputs (MaterialSample, Dataset) are their own types; a specific execution is an edge, not a node. Anchored SNOMEDCT/CPT/NCIT/OBI/EDAM.
biookf.identifier_pattern: Human-readable technique/procedure name — e.g. "kidney transplantation", "magnetic resonance imaging", "functional magnetic resonance imaging", "high-performance liquid chromatography", "comet assay", "DNA pooling", "SEREX". 17/18 carry synonyms; xref empty for all.
xref_namespaces: SCHEMA/SPEC canonical: SNOMEDCT, CPT, NCIT, OBI, EDAM
Benchmark actual: NONE — 0/18 nodes have any xref
spoke_targets: Compound/PharmacologicClass (only when the 'procedure' is really a drug therapy — rare here)
biookf.mapping_strategy: Waterfall: SPOKE lacks a Procedure/Method node, so direct auto-map as itself is usually impossible. (1) Map via the edge target instead: a procedure 'treats'/'used_to_study'/'measures' a Disease/Phenotype that IS in SPOKE — carry the biomedical target across, treat the method as context. (2) Only when a 'procedure' is actually a pharmacologic therapy might it semantically route to a SPOKE Compound. (3) Otherwise defer to LLM or leave unmapped as a method/provenance-adjacent node. Never coerce an assay ('comet assay') into a SPOKE biomedical entity.
biookf.pitfalls: No SPOKE equivalent — the main pitfall is forcing it into Disease/Compound. Collision with MaterialSample/Dataset (inputs/outputs) and with the entity it studies via 'used_to_study' (5 edges to Disease) — keep the tangible model/organoid separate from the act of using it (TB-3). 'treats' edges (7, all → Disease) mean a procedure can look like a therapy; map the Disease, not the method, into SPOKE reltypes. Diagnostic methods overlap BiomedicalMeasure (both measure Phenotype/Disease). Small n=18; only two subtype tokens ('general', 'stereotactic surgery').

biookf.name: Exposure
biookf.definition: A behavioral / environmental / occupational / dietary-pattern exposure (SCHEMA type #16; SPEC §5.A/§5.D). Type by identity, express 'risk factor' as the predisposes_to/prevents ROLE, never a type. A *defined chemical* exposure routes to Molecule; an *infectious* one to Organism; a *food item* to Food; a *social/structural determinant* to SocialFactor. Anchored ECTO/ExO; Biolink ExposureEvent.
biookf.identifier_pattern: Human-readable exposure/behavior phrase — e.g. "cigarette smoking", "alcohol consumption", "early-life arsenic exposure", "prenatal alcohol exposure", "hypoxia", "high altitude", "injection drug use", "low folate intake". 13/14 carry synonyms; xref empty for all.
xref_namespaces: Benchmark actual: NONE — 0/14 nodes have any xref
spoke_targets: Compound (when the exposure is a defined chemical/agent, e.g. arsenic, alcohol as ethanol, caffeine)
Organism (if an infectious exposure — none in benchmark)
biookf.mapping_strategy: Waterfall: SPOKE has no ExposureEvent node.
