(1) Route by identity per §5.D: a defined-chemical exposure ('early-life arsenic exposure', 'alcohol consumption') can auto-map its chemical to a SPOKE Compound when the agent name matches; a dietary-item exposure to Food. (2) Behavioral/pattern exposures ('cigarette smoking', 'injection drug use') have no SPOKE node — carry the predisposes_to/causes edge to the SPOKE Disease/Phenotype target instead. (3) Defer to LLM for ambiguous behavioral vs chemical framing. Do NOT invent a SPOKE Exposure node.
biookf.pitfalls: Three-way collision Exposure vs SocialFactor vs Food (and vs Molecule/Organism): 'high fat diet' is Food, 'low socioeconomic status' is SocialFactor, arsenic exposure decomposes to a Compound — mis-routing sends it to the wrong SPOKE label. 'Risk factor' is a ROLE (predisposes_to), never a type — do not create a node for it. Heavy outgoing 'regulates -> Gene' (15) and 'causes -> Phenotype/Disease' (16) edges: map the target entity, not the exposure. Negation present (not_associated_with -> Disease) — only contradict an existing positive SPOKE edge. Uniform 'general' subtype gives no routing signal; must infer chemical-vs-behavioral from the label.

biookf.name: SocialFactor
biookf.definition: A social determinant of health — a social/economic/structural factor affecting health: income, education, housing, employment, food security, access to care, social support (SCHEMA type #17, deprecated aliases SDOH/SDoH normalize here; SPEC §5.A/§5.D). Distinct from behavioral/environmental Exposure and from Food. Biolink SocialDeterminantOfHealth; no dedicated ontology (Biolink SDoH / local).
biookf.identifier_pattern: Human-readable determinant phrase — the single benchmark node is "low socioeconomic status". 1/1 carries synonyms; xref empty.
xref_namespaces: SCHEMA/SPEC canonical: Biolink SDoH, local (no strong external ontology)
Benchmark actual: NONE — 0/1 has any xref
spoke_targets: (no SPOKE label — SPOKE has no SocialDeterminantOfHealth node)
biookf.mapping_strategy: Waterfall: essentially never auto-maps as itself — SPOKE has no SDoH node. (1) The only sensible move is to carry its single edge (associated_with -> Disease) to the SPOKE Disease target and drop the factor, or leave it unmapped as out-of-SPOKE context. (2) Always defer to LLM before attempting any coercion. Do not force it into Exposure/Compound/Disease.
biookf.pitfalls: Only n=1, so no lexical prior. Collision with Exposure (behavioral) — a determinant like 'low socioeconomic status' can be mis-typed as a behavioral exposure; §5.D keeps social/economic/structural determinants in SocialFactor. No SPOKE equivalent means the biggest risk is inventing a spurious mapping. Its association is via the associated_with ROLE, not identity. Deprecated aliases SDOH/SDoH must be normalized to SocialFactor on read.

biookf.name: Food
biookf.definition: A food item, food group, or dietary product (SCHEMA type #18; SPEC §5.A/§5.D). Distinct from a dietary-pattern Exposure (behavior) and from a defined chemical Molecule/Nutrient. A food derives_from an Organism. Anchored FOODON/FooDB; maps to SPOKE Food.
biookf.identifier_pattern: Human-readable food/diet name — the two benchmark nodes are "green tea" and "high fat diet". 1/2 carries synonyms; xref empty for both.
xref_namespaces: Benchmark actual: NONE — 0/2 have any xref
spoke_targets: Nutrient (for a constituent nutrient/compound rather than the whole food)
Compound (if the item is really a defined chemical)
biookf.mapping_strategy: Waterfall: (1) direct auto-map when type==Food AND identifier/synonym exactly matches a SPOKE Food name (SPOKE Food is FOODON-adjacent) — e.g. 'green tea'. (2) If the label is really a nutrient/compound, route to SPOKE Nutrient/Compound. (3) Defer to LLM for pattern-diet phrasings ('high fat diet') that straddle Food vs Exposure(dietary) — these may be better modeled as the exposure/edge than a SPOKE Food node. No xref fast-path.
biookf.pitfalls: Collision with Exposure: 'high fat diet' is a dietary PATTERN that reads as an Exposure but is typed Food here — the boundary (§5.D: food item/group/product = Food; dietary-pattern behavior = Exposure) is genuinely fuzzy and n=2 gives no prior, so a wrong pick sends it to the wrong SPOKE label (Food vs no-node exposure). Food vs Nutrient/Compound is subtype-dependent (whole food → Food; constituent → Nutrient/Compound). Outgoing 'prevents'/'causes'/'regulates' edges: prefer carrying the Disease/BiologicalFunction target into SPOKE.

biookf.name: Device
biookf.definition: An engineered artifact: medical device, implant/prosthesis/graft/mesh, drug-delivery device, research instrument, reagent/kit (SCHEMA type #19; SPEC §5.A/§5.D). Distinct from a biospecimen (MaterialSample): Device = engineered artifact, MaterialSample = biological sample. Can be subject of treats/contraindicated_in and used_to_study edges. Biolink Device; namespace typically local.
biookf.identifier_pattern: ABSENT from benchmark-biored (0 nodes). Per SCHEMA/SPEC would be a human-readable artifact name (e.g. a stent, an assay kit); no ':' , xref namespace is 'local' so a CURIE is unlikely even when present.
xref_namespaces: SCHEMA/SPEC canonical: local (no strong external ontology; Biolink Device)
Benchmark actual: N/A — 0 Device nodes exist in benchmark-biored
spoke_targets: (no SPOKE label — SPOKE has no Device node)
biookf.mapping_strategy: Waterfall: no benchmark instances and no SPOKE Device node, so there is nothing to auto-map and no lexical prior. Any future Device would (1) carry its treats/contraindicated_in/used_to_study edge to the SPOKE Disease/Phenotype/entity target and (2) otherwise be left unmapped as out-of-SPOKE context, always via LLM adjudication. Never coerce a device into Compound/Disease.
biookf.pitfalls: Zero coverage in this benchmark, so no evidence to calibrate against — flag as unmapped rather than guessing. No SPOKE equivalent: risk is inventing a mapping. Primary type collision is Device vs MaterialSample (engineered artifact vs biospecimen) and Device vs Molecule (a reagent that is a defined chemical is a Molecule→Compound, not a Device). A drug-delivery device is a Device, but the drug it delivers is a Molecule.

biookf.name: MaterialSample
biookf.definition: A biospecimen / physical biological sample: serum, biopsy, aliquot, tissue block, cell-line stock (SCHEMA type #20; SPEC §5.A/§5.D). derives_from an Organism/Anatomy/donor; can be a used_to_study investigative model. Distinct from the engineered-artifact Device and from the abstract CellType. Anchored BioSample (else local); Biolink MaterialSample.
biookf.identifier_pattern: ABSENT from benchmark-biored (0 nodes). Per SCHEMA/SPEC would be a human-readable specimen name (e.g. 'patient serum aliquot'); xref namespace BioSample/local, so CURIEs are rare even when present.
xref_namespaces: Benchmark actual: N/A — 0 MaterialSample nodes exist in benchmark-biored
spoke_targets: (no SPOKE label — SPOKE has no MaterialSample/BioSample node)
biookf.mapping_strategy: Waterfall: no benchmark instances and no SPOKE MaterialSample node, so nothing to auto-map. A future specimen would (1) route its derives_from edge to the SPOKE Anatomy/Organism/CellType it comes from (those DO have SPOKE labels) and carry any used_to_study target across, while (2) the sample node itself is left unmapped as context, via LLM adjudication. Never coerce a specimen into CellType/Anatomy as if identical.
biookf.pitfalls: Zero coverage here — no calibration data. No SPOKE equivalent: the specimen node cannot map, but its derives_from source (Anatomy/Organism/CellType) can — do not conflate the sample with its source (a serum sample is NOT the Anatomy 'blood', a cell-line stock is NOT the CellType). Collision with Device (biospecimen vs engineered artifact) and with CellType (a cell-line stock is a MaterialSample, the cell line as a type is CellType). Method inputs/outputs (§5.D) are their own types, distinct from the MethodOrProcedure that uses them.

biookf.name: Publication
biookf.definition: A document/artifact node (SCHEMA type 21, SPEC 5.B): a journal article, preprint, book, patent, drug label, guideline, abstract, poster, slide deck, blog, tweet/thread, lab-notebook or meeting note. It is the *document* facet, distinct from the designed investigation (Study) and the data artifact (Dataset) per SPEC 5.D. In v0.5 provenance is node-based: a Publication is the canonical source node an edge's mandatory primary_source names, and it anchors to immutable bytes via raw_source (raw/<id>) and/or to a citation via xref. It is a first-class provenance node with NO biomedical-entity semantics.
biookf.identifier_pattern: identifier is the full human-readable paper TITLE (e.g. 'A Critical Role for the Type I Interferon Receptor in Virus-Induced Autoimmune Diabetes in Rats.'), not a code. This is the ONLY node type that reliably carries xrefs in the benchmark: every Publication has xref ['PMID:<n>','https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/<n>/'] and a raw_source path 'raw/<pmid>-t-...'. Subtypes are free-text lowercase-ish tokens ('case report','clinical trial') coined, not from a controlled list.
xref_namespaces: benchmark actual: PMID: (400/400) plus a pubmed https URL; DOI/PMC absent
spoke_targets: (none — no SPOKE node label; SPOKE has no Publication entity)
biookf.mapping_strategy: DO NOT map to any SPOKE biomedical node. Publications are pure provenance and have no SPOKE equivalent (SPOKE is entity/relationship, not source-tracking). In the mapper: strip Publication nodes from entity mapping; instead use them to populate edge-level provenance/evidence (a SPOKE relationship's 'sources'/'pmids' property). The PMID xref is the join key — attach it to the SPOKE edges that the BioOKF edges (whose primary_source is this Publication) become. Never auto-create a SPOKE node for a Publication.
biookf.pitfalls: 1) All 5360 benchmark edges use a Publication as primary_source and all 2585 reported_in edges point at Publications — so Publications dominate the graph but must be routed to edge provenance, not nodes. 2) Do not confuse with Study (an investigation like a GWAS/RCT) or Dataset (a data file/DB); the benchmark collapses everything to Publication, so a 'clinical trial' subtype here is still a Publication document, not a Study node. 3) Title-as-identifier means near-duplicate titles could collide; the PMID xref is the reliable dedup key. 4) reported_in edges to Publications are provenance links, not biomedical assertions — never emit them as SPOKE relationships.

biookf.name: Study
biookf.definition: A designed-investigation node (SCHEMA type 22, SPEC 5.B): a clinical trial, cohort/case-control/RCT, GWAS, observational study, registry, or screen. Distinct from Publication (the document reporting it) and Population (the people enrolled) per SPEC 5.D 'Population vs Study vs Organism' and 'Publication vs Study vs Dataset'. Can serve as a provenance source node (primary_source) and as the domain of used_to_study (a GWAS used_to_study a disease's genetic architecture).
biookf.identifier_pattern: ABSENT in benchmark-biored (0 nodes). Per SCHEMA it would be a human-readable investigation name; xref pattern would be clinicaltrials:NCT######## for trials. The BioRED text-mining pipeline folded all sources into Publication, so no Study nodes were minted.
spoke_targets: (none — no SPOKE node label; SPOKE has no Study entity)
biookf.mapping_strategy: No SPOKE equivalent — provenance/context type. Were Study nodes present, they would map to edge provenance (like Publication) and to the used_to_study investigative axis, NOT to a SPOKE node. In this benchmark there is nothing to map. Defer to LLM only if a future bundle mints Study nodes that must be disambiguated from Population/Publication.
biookf.pitfalls: Zero occurrences here so no live pitfall, but the design pitfall is the Study/Population/Publication trio: an investigation (Study) is not its participants (Population) nor its write-up (Publication). If a downstream bundle adds Study nodes, do not fold them into SPOKE entities; treat as provenance. used_to_study direction is resource→subject-of-study (forward only).

biookf.name: Dataset
biookf.definition: A data-artifact node (SCHEMA type 23, SPEC 5.B): a dataset, data file, table/CSV/XLSX, omics matrix, image collection, or knowledge base. An external cited knowledge base (GO, DrugBank, SemMedDB) that was NOT ingested is typed Dataset (subtype knowledge_base) with its CURIE in xref and no raw_source (SPEC 8.1 external-reference source node). Can be a primary_source and the domain of used_to_study (a database used_to_study a gene).
biookf.identifier_pattern: Single node: 'FH mutation database' (human-readable name). xref ['local:fh-mutation-database'], no PMID, no raw_source. Its edges are: used_to_study -> FH (Gene) and reported_in -> the paper describing it. subtype 'general' is a pipeline default, not one of SCHEMA's table/omics_matrix/knowledge_base examples.
xref_namespaces: SCHEMA cheatsheet: none (Dataset has no canonical registry); external KBs use their own CURIE/infores in xref
spoke_targets: (none — no SPOKE node label; SPOKE has no Dataset entity)
biookf.mapping_strategy: No SPOKE node equivalent. A Dataset is provenance/context. The one benchmark Dataset ('FH mutation database') should NOT become a SPOKE node; its used_to_study->FH edge is an investigative-context link, not a SPOKE biomedical relationship. If it were an external KB used as evidence, route it to edge provenance. Do not auto-map; if a bundle uses Dataset as a citable source, treat like Publication (provenance), else drop.
biookf.pitfalls: 1) Only 1 node so statistically negligible. 2) Do not confuse a Dataset (the data artifact / knowledge base) with a Study (the investigation that produced data) or the entity the data is about (FH the Gene). 3) used_to_study from a Dataset is directional (resource -> studied entity) and is NOT an associated_with — do not emit it as a SPOKE ASSOCIATION. 4) local: xref is not resolvable to any SPOKE namespace.

biookf.name: Agent
biookf.definition: A person/organization node (SCHEMA type 24, SPEC 5.B): author, curator, patient-case, lab, consortium, organization, company, regulator, funder, software agent, or online handle. In v0.5 a naming authority or database organization cited as provenance (HGNC, a regulator) is typed Agent (subtype organization) with its infores:/ROR/ORCID CURIE in xref and no raw_source (SPEC 8.1). An Agent can be named as a primary_source.
biookf.identifier_pattern: ABSENT in benchmark-biored (0 nodes). Per SCHEMA it would be a human-readable name (person/org); xref pattern ORCID:####-####-####-#### , ROR:, or infores:<source>. The text-mining pipeline did not emit author/organization Agent nodes.
spoke_targets: (none — no SPOKE node label; SPOKE has no Agent/Author entity)
biookf.mapping_strategy: No SPOKE equivalent — provenance/context. Nothing to map in this benchmark. In general, Agents are source/authorship context: fold into edge provenance (e.g. an infores: source) rather than minting a SPOKE node. Never auto-map to a biomedical label.
biookf.pitfalls: Zero occurrences here. Design pitfall: an Agent (organization like HGNC/DrugBank-as-org) can look like a Dataset (DrugBank-as-knowledge-base) — SPEC 8.1 disambiguates by identity (naming authority/org -> Agent; citable data/KB artifact -> Dataset). Neither maps to a SPOKE node; both are provenance. Do not confuse a company Agent with a Compound it makes.

biookf.name: Population
biookf.definition: A group-of-people node (SCHEMA type 25, SPEC 5.B / 5.D): a cohort, study population, ancestry group, or demographic group. Explicitly distinct from Study (the investigation) and Organism (the taxon/species) per SPEC 5.D 'Population vs Study vs Organism'. It is context, not a biomedical entity; it can be a subject of predisposes_to/associated_with/affects_response_to and can derives_from a source.
biookf.identifier_pattern: Human-readable population/ancestry labels: 'African Black ancestry','Amerindian ancestry','Ashkenazi Jewish population','Basques','Europeans'. No xref (0/5). subtype uniformly 'general' (pipeline default; SCHEMA examples would be cohort/ancestry/demographic). Synonyms present (e.g. 'European populations'). Participates in real assertions: e.g. 'African Black ancestry' associated_with 'cleft lip...' (Disease); 'Basques' located_in 'Basque Country' and not_associated_with 'Europeans'.
xref_namespaces: benchmark actual: none (0/5 carry any xref)
spoke_targets: (closest, weak) Organism — only if a Population is actually an ancestry proxy for a taxon; SPOKE has no Population/Ancestry/Cohort node, so generally (none)
biookf.mapping_strategy: No clean SPOKE label — SPOKE lacks a Population/ancestry node. Default: do NOT auto-map to a SPOKE node; treat as context. If a Population participates in an edge like Population associated_with Disease, that edge has no SPOKE analogue (SPOKE has no Population subject) and should be dropped or logged, NOT coerced onto Organism. Defer to LLM only to decide whether an 'ancestry' Population is being used as a stand-in for a HANCESTRO term worth preserving as an edge qualifier. Never exact-name-map Populations to Disease/Organism.
biookf.pitfalls: 1) Collision with Organism: 'African Black ancestry'/'Europeans' are human demographic groups, NOT species — do not map to SPOKE Organism (Homo sapiens). 2) Population appears as the SUBJECT of associated_with/not_associated_with/affects_response_to — SPOKE association edges are between biomedical entities, so a Population-subject edge has no SPOKE home; dropping it (not forcing it) avoids fabricating a SPOKE relationship. 3) 'Basques' not_associated_with 'Europeans' is a Population-to-Population negation with no SPOKE meaning. 4) Distinguish from Study (the enrolling investigation).

biookf.name: GeographicLocation
biookf.definition: A place-context node (SCHEMA type 26, SPEC 5.B): a country, region, or place. Also the range of the geographic sense of located_in (SCHEMA: located_in range += GeographicLocation). Pure context; no biomedical-entity semantics and no SPOKE analogue.
biookf.identifier_pattern: Three nodes: 'Basque Country' (subtype general, a real place; synonyms 'Navarre and Guipuzcoa provinces','Spain') and 'chromosome 1','chromosome 11' (subtype 'chromosome'). No xref (0/3). The two chromosome nodes are a MISTYPING artifact: a chromosome is a genomic location, and NDUFS2/NDUFS3 (Genes) point at them via located_in — but chromosomes are not geographic places (they should be a genomic located_in target/SequenceFeature context, not GeographicLocation).
biookf.mapping_strategy: No SPOKE equivalent — drop from entity mapping. For the genuine place ('Basque Country') there is no SPOKE label. For the mistyped 'chromosome N' nodes, do NOT map to any SPOKE node; the Gene located_in chromosome relationship is genomic context that SPOKE encodes as a Gene property (chromosome), not as an edge to a location node — so consume it as a Gene attribute if at all, else drop. Never auto-map GeographicLocation to a biomedical SPOKE label.
biookf.pitfalls: 1) Subtype-dependent semantic split inside one type: subtype 'chromosome' is genomic, subtype 'general' is truly geographic — do not treat them uniformly. 2) The 'chromosome N' nodes are an upstream typing error (should be genomic, not geographic); a Gene located_in 'chromosome 1' must not become a SPOKE Gene->GeographicLocation edge — it is a chromosome attribute. 3) 'Basque Country' listing 'Spain' as a synonym conflates place granularity. 4) No xrefs means no reliable join key; matching is name-only and low-value.

biookf.name: Concept
biookf.definition: An abstract-concept node (SCHEMA type 27, SPEC 5.B): an abstract attribute, classification system, unit, ontology-term-as-label, or score definition not better typed above. Per SPEC 5.D 'class vs instance', a bare abstract category (a SO term used as a label, 'a principal component' as a derived variable) is a Concept, whereas a coordinate-bearing instance is its concrete type. A catch-before-Other bucket for abstractions.
biookf.identifier_pattern: ABSENT in benchmark-biored (0 nodes). Per SCHEMA it would be a human-readable term (unit/classification/ontology_term); xref namespace: none (UMLS CONC / Biolink Attribute conceptually). The BioRED entity set (Gene/Disease/Chemical/Variant/Species/CellLine) yielded no abstract Concept nodes.
biookf.mapping_strategy: No SPOKE equivalent. Nothing to map in this benchmark. In general, Concept nodes are abstractions (units, ontology-term-as-label) that should not become SPOKE biomedical nodes; defer to LLM only to decide whether a Concept is a mistyped concrete entity (e.g. a real SequenceFeature typed as Concept) that should be re-typed before mapping, otherwise drop.
biookf.pitfalls: Zero occurrences here. Design pitfall: Concept vs Other (Concept = abstract attribute/unit/classification; Other = a biomedical thing fitting none of the 27) and class-vs-instance (an abstract '3' UTR' label is a Concept, a specific '3' UTR of EPAS1' is a SequenceFeature). Mis-typed concrete entities hiding under Concept would be silently dropped if not caught.

biookf.name: Other
biookf.definition: The explicit escape hatch (SCHEMA type 28, SPEC 5.B): a biomedical concept that genuinely fits none of the other 27 types, always authored with a note: explaining why. Preserves OKF's minimally-opinionated closure (Biolink NamedThing root). Never invent a new type — use Other with a note instead.
biookf.identifier_pattern: ABSENT in benchmark-biored (0 nodes). Per SCHEMA it has no subtype (none) and requires a note; xref namespace none. The benchmark's constrained entity ontology never needed the escape hatch, so no Other nodes exist.
biookf.mapping_strategy: No SPOKE equivalent by definition. Any Other node is an unresolved/unclassifiable concept: it must ALWAYS go to LLM/semantic adjudication (read its note:) to decide whether it is a mistyped concrete entity re-mappable to a real SPOKE label, or genuinely unmappable and dropped. Never auto-map an Other node.
biookf.pitfalls: Zero occurrences here. General pitfall: Other is the last resort — a populated Other node often signals an upstream typing gap; do not force it onto the nearest SPOKE label without reading its note. Distinguish from Concept (abstract attribute) — Other is a substantive biomedical thing that simply lacks a type, not an abstraction.

biookf.name: is_a
biookf.definition: Ontology backbone: subject is a more-specific kind/instance of the object (UMLS isa / Biolink subclass_of / SPOKE ISA). Direction subject(host doc)->object, forward-only (no inverse). Domain/range: any->same type. Non-negatable (structural/definitional; negation rejected under open-world semantics as lint edge.not_negatable).
biookf.identifier_pattern: Edge endpoints are human-readable identifiers (node names), never CURIEs. In benchmark is_a runs mostly Disease->Disease (8; e.g. 'juvenile idiopathic arthritis' is_a 'arthritis'), Gene->MolecularClass (5; a gene classified into a family/class), Variant->Gene (5), Gene->Gene (3), one Disease->BiologicalFunction (noisy).
xref_namespaces: endpoints' canonical namespaces per type: Disease=MONDO/DOID/MESH, Gene=HGNC/NCBIGene, MolecularClass=NCIT/PFAM/INTERPRO
benchmark: NONE present on any biomedical endpoint (only Publications carry PMID)
spoke_targets: SPOKE has no universal is_a reltype; maps only where the pair matches a SPOKE hierarchy edge (Disease ISA Disease, CellType/Anatomy part-hierarchies, Compound->PharmacologicClass via MEMBEROF)
biookf.mapping_strategy: Waterfall: (1) auto-map ONLY the endpoints (name+type -> SPOKE node) with exact-name/strong-synonym match; the predicate itself rarely auto-maps because SPOKE lacks a generic ISA between arbitrary types. (2) If both endpoints resolve to same-typed SPOKE nodes AND SPOKE models that hierarchy (Disease ISA), emit the SPOKE hierarchy edge. (3) Gene->MolecularClass / Variant->Gene under is_a are mistyped-in-benchmark and should be re-routed (member_of / part_of|located_in) by LLM adjudication rather than forced onto ISA. Defer all cross-type is_a to semantic review.
biookf.pitfalls: Benchmark misuses is_a for non-taxonomic links (Variant->Gene should be part_of/located_in; Gene->MolecularClass should be member_of; a Disease->BiologicalFunction is pure noise). SPOKE has no single ISA reltype spanning all node types, so a naive predicate->reltype map fails. Not negatable: any not_is_a is invalid. Endpoints have no xrefs, so resolution is name-only and collision-prone (e.g. same label as Gene vs Molecule vs Disease).

biookf.name: part_of
biookf.definition: Structural/compositional mereology; per v0.5 STRUCTURAL GENOMIC PARTONOMY lives here (exon/intron/CDS/codon and, in practice, a variant's location on its gene). Domain extended to SequenceFeature, Variant; range extended to Gene, SequenceFeature (plus base Anatomy/Molecule/BiologicalPathway -> larger whole). Forward-only, non-negatable.
biookf.identifier_pattern: Human-readable endpoint names. Benchmark is dominated by Variant->Gene (114; a variant is 'part of' its gene, e.g. '-1123 G>C' part_of 'PTPN22'), then Gene->Structure (6), Variant->Variant (4), Gene->BiologicalPathway (3); a long tail of noisy pairs (CellType->Disease, Molecule->Exposure).
xref_namespaces: endpoint namespaces: Gene=HGNC/NCBIGene, Variant=DBSNP/CLINVAR/HGVS, SequenceFeature=SO, Structure=PDB
spoke_targets: no direct SPOKE reltype for Variant->Gene (in SPOKE a Variant links to Gene via location/association, not PARTOF)
Gene->Pathway would be PARTICIPATES/CONTAINS in SPOKE, not part_of
biookf.mapping_strategy: Waterfall: (1) Anatomy->Anatomy and Molecule-complex->Molecule part_of map cleanly to SPOKE PARTOF when both endpoints resolve by exact name/synonym. (2) The dominant Variant->Gene part_of is a BioOKF partonomy convention with NO SPOKE PARTOF equivalent -> re-route: attach the Variant to its Gene via SPOKE's Variant-Gene structural edge (located_in / gene-of-variant), decided by LLM/type rule, not by literal predicate map. (3) Gene->BiologicalPathway part_of -> SPOKE Gene-PARTICIPATES-Pathway. Defer mixed-type tails to semantic review.
biookf.pitfalls: Biggest trap: 114/141 part_of edges are Variant->Gene, which must NOT become an anatomical PARTOF in SPOKE; direction and target-type drive a different SPOKE reltype. Overlaps with located_in (same Variant->Gene pair also appears there 147x) — dedupe. Not negatable. Endpoints lack xrefs; Variant names are free-text HGVS-ish strings ('-1123 G>C') that rarely resolve to a SPOKE Variant, so many will stay BioOKF-only.

biookf.name: member_of
biookf.definition: Subject belongs to a class/family/group (drug->drug class, gene->gene set, protein->family). Domain Molecule/Gene; range extended to MolecularClass (plus BiologicalPathway/gene-set). Forward-only, non-negatable. Distinct from part_of (grouping/classification vs physical composition).
biookf.identifier_pattern: Endpoint names. Benchmark: Gene->MolecularClass (3; e.g. a gene member_of a protein family/class like 'BMP' or 'G protein-coupled receptor') and one Gene->Gene. Very rare in this corpus.
biookf.mapping_strategy: Waterfall: (1) auto-map when Molecule(drug)->PharmacologicClass or Molecule(protein)/Gene->ProteinFamily and both endpoints resolve by exact name/strong synonym -> SPOKE MEMBEROF. (2) The MolecularClass target's own subtype (pharmacologic vs protein_family vs protein_domain vs gene_set) selects the SPOKE class label (PharmacologicClass vs ProteinFamily vs ProteinDomain), so the target must be sub-classified first. (3) Gene->Gene member_of is anomalous -> defer to LLM. Low volume, so hand adjudication is cheap.
biookf.pitfalls: Subtype-of-the-target drives which SPOKE class label to use — mis-picking ProteinFamily vs PharmacologicClass corrupts the edge. Easily confused with is_a and part_of (benchmark scatters classification edges across all three). MolecularClass has only 6 nodes, all subtype 'general', so the family-vs-class distinction must be inferred from the name. No xrefs; class names ('C-type lectin','ESCRT-III') need fuzzy match to SPOKE. Not negatable.

biookf.name: derives_from
biookf.definition: Material/data lineage: sample<-donor, cell<-tissue, metabolite<-parent compound, dataset<-study, structure<-molecule, food<-organism, population<-source. Domain extended to MaterialSample, Structure, Food, Population (plus CellType/Device/Molecule/Dataset); range Organism/Anatomy/Study/Molecule. Forward-only (this doc is the DERIVED entity), non-negatable.
biookf.identifier_pattern: Endpoint names. Benchmark: Molecule->Molecule (3; metabolite<-parent, e.g. a derivative compound), Molecule->Organism (3; a substance derived from a species/plant, e.g. 'Crocus sativus'), CellType->CellType (1), Variant->Gene (1, noisy). Rare.
xref_namespaces: endpoint namespaces: Molecule=CHEBI/PUBCHEM/UniProtKB, Organism=NCBITaxon, MaterialSample=BioSample, Structure=PDB
spoke_targets: Compound<-Organism lineage (no first-class SPOKE derives reltype; nearest is Compound-Organism source or metabolite relations)
no clean SPOKE reltype for most derives_from — SPOKE lacks a general provenance/lineage edge
biookf.mapping_strategy: Waterfall: (1) auto-map only the endpoints by name/type. (2) The PREDICATE itself usually has NO SPOKE equivalent (SPOKE models few lineage edges), so most derives_from edges either drop to a supported nearby SPOKE relation (Compound sourced-from Organism) or remain BioOKF-only. (3) Structure->Molecule derives_from could feed a SPOKE Structure-Compound link. Given only 8 edges, fully LLM/semantic-adjudicate each.
biookf.pitfalls: Direction is subtle: the DERIVED thing hosts the edge (metabolite derives_from parent, NOT parent produces metabolite). Molecule->Molecule can be either metabolic derivation or should have been converts_to — check semantics. Metabolite<-parent vs converts_to overlap. No general SPOKE lineage reltype, so expect many non-mappable. Not negatable. Endpoints lack xrefs.

biookf.name: located_in
biookf.definition: Positioned/found in — ANATOMICAL, GENOMIC, or GEOGRAPHIC. Domain extended to Variant, SequenceFeature (plus Disease/BiologicalPathway/Molecule/CellType); range extended to Gene, SequenceFeature, GeographicLocation (plus Anatomy/Organism). Forward-only, non-negatable. Genomic sense (Variant/SequenceFeature located_in Gene) overlaps part_of by design.
biookf.identifier_pattern: Endpoint names. Benchmark is dominated by the GENOMIC sense Variant->Gene (147; a variant located in its gene), then anatomical Disease->Anatomy (19), Gene->Anatomy (7), Gene->Structure (6), Molecule->Anatomy (6), CellType->Anatomy (4), Phenotype->Anatomy (4); two geographic Gene->GeographicLocation (noisy).
xref_namespaces: endpoint namespaces: Anatomy=UBERON, Gene=HGNC/ENSEMBL, Variant=DBSNP/HGVS, GeographicLocation=GeoNames/GADM/ISO-3166
spoke_targets: SPOKE has anatomical localization edges (DLA) but the Variant->Gene genomic sense maps to Variant-Gene structural edge, not an anatomical LOCATEDIN
biookf.mapping_strategy: Waterfall: MUST branch by the located_in SENSE. (1) Anatomical: Disease/Gene/Molecule/CellType ->Anatomy auto-maps to SPOKE localization (e.g. Disease LOCALIZES Anatomy) when Anatomy resolves to a UBERON-backed SPOKE Anatomy node by exact name/synonym. (2) Genomic Variant->Gene (the 147 majority) re-routes to SPOKE's Variant-Gene edge, NOT an anatomical LOCATEDIN. (3) Geographic ->GeographicLocation has no SPOKE target -> drop/BioOKF-only. Sense detection = endpoint TYPES, so type both ends first, then map.
biookf.pitfalls: Three distinct senses fused in one predicate — mapping the genomic Variant->Gene majority onto an anatomical SPOKE reltype is the top failure mode. Heavy overlap/dedup with part_of (same Variant->Gene pairs). GeographicLocation has no SPOKE analog. Anatomy names must hit UBERON via SPOKE; free-text like 'CA1 region of hippocampus' needs synonym match. Not negatable. No xrefs on endpoints.

biookf.name: expressed_in
biookf.definition: A gene/molecule is expressed / abundant / present in an anatomy or cell context. Domain Gene/Molecule; range Anatomy/CellType. Carries direction, effect_size, p_value. Forward-only. THE ONE negatable predicate in this set: not_expressed_in exists for a stated absence of expression.
biookf.identifier_pattern: Endpoint names. Benchmark: Gene->CellType (32) and Gene->Anatomy (29) are the intended sense; also 9 CellType->Gene (reversed/noisy), 7 Gene->Disease (should be a different predicate), 1 Gene->Organism, 1 Molecule->Anatomy. not_expressed_in (3): CellType->Gene, Gene->CellType, Gene->Disease.
spoke_targets: Gene expression in CellType (SPOKE cell-level expression)
biookf.mapping_strategy: Waterfall: (1) STRONG auto-map — Gene->Anatomy and Gene->CellType expressed_in map directly to SPOKE EXPRESSEDIN when both endpoints resolve by exact name/synonym (Gene symbol match is high-precision; Anatomy->UBERON, CellType->CL). Carry direction/effect_size/p_value onto the SPOKE edge. (2) Reversed CellType->Gene and off-target Gene->Disease should be re-oriented or re-routed (associated_with) by LLM. (3) not_expressed_in: only emit a contradiction/suppression if a POSITIVE EXPRESSEDIN exists in SPOKE for that Gene-Anatomy pair; otherwise record as a negative finding with no positive SPOKE edge to contradict.
biookf.pitfalls: Polarity is live here: not_expressed_in must ONLY negate/flag when a positive SPOKE EXPRESSEDIN exists for the same subject->object; absent that, it is just an open-world negative and must not fabricate an edge. Direction matters — Gene->Anatomy is correct; the 9 CellType->Gene are reversed. Gene->Disease under expressed_in is a mis-predicate (likely associated_with). Molecule->Anatomy expressed_in maps to abundance, not gene-expression. No xrefs; Gene symbols are the reliable join key.

biookf.name: encodes
biookf.definition: Gene encodes / is transcribed-translated to its product; authored on the GENE page (there is NO inverse encoded_by — the deprecated encoded_by normalizes to a forward encodes on the gene). Domain Gene; range Molecule. Forward-only, non-negatable.
biookf.identifier_pattern: Endpoint names, always Gene->Molecule (3/3), e.g. a gene symbol -> its protein/product name. Strikingly rare in this benchmark (BioRED is variant/disease-centric, and gene-vs-protein are often collapsed to a single Gene node so the encodes edge is seldom authored).
biookf.mapping_strategy: Waterfall: (1) clean, high-precision auto-map — Gene->Molecule(subtype protein) maps to SPOKE Gene-ENCODES-Protein when the Gene resolves by symbol and the Molecule resolves to the cognate UniProt protein. Gene symbol + product name is usually unambiguous. (2) If the Molecule target is not a protein (drug/metabolite), the edge is malformed -> defer/reject. Given only 3 edges, verify each by hand.
biookf.pitfalls: Gene-vs-Protein collision: BioOKF (and this benchmark) frequently model a gene and its protein as ONE Gene node, so encodes is under-populated and a Molecule product may be missing entirely — SPOKE's Gene->Protein split then has no BioOKF counterpart to hang the edge on. No inverse: never emit encoded_by. Range must be a protein Molecule; a Gene->drug 'encodes' is invalid. Not negatable. No xrefs — rely on Gene symbol and UniProt-name match.

biookf.name: reported_in
biookf.definition: The universal PROVENANCE edge: the subject node (or reified claim) is reported/curated/studied/evidenced in the object Publication/Study/Dataset/Agent. Domain any; range Publication/Study/Dataset/Agent. Replaces the removed node-level provided_by. Forward-only, non-negatable.
biookf.identifier_pattern: Subject = any biomedical entity name; OBJECT is a Publication identifier that is the full article TITLE string (e.g. 'Association of adipocyte genes with ASP expression...'), and the Publication node carries the PMID in xref. This is by far the largest predicate (48% of all edges). Domain spread mirrors node counts: Gene->Pub 723, Disease->Pub 446, Molecule->Pub 444, Variant->Pub 323, Phenotype->Pub 286, etc. Range is 100% Publication in the benchmark.
xref_namespaces: object (Publication) canonical: PMID, DOI, PMC — and in the benchmark Publications DO carry PMID (+ a source https URL); this is the ONLY node type with populated xrefs
spoke_targets: NO SPOKE node/edge equivalent — SPOKE has no first-class Publication node or generic provenance edge
provenance is metadata, not a graph edge, in SPOKE
biookf.mapping_strategy: Waterfall: DO NOT map to any SPOKE reltype. reported_in edges are provenance scaffolding: the Publication object (Publication/Study/Dataset/Agent) has NO SPOKE label, so these edges are dropped from the SPOKE graph and instead folded into the SUPPORTING evidence/PMID metadata of whatever biomedical SPOKE edge the same source underpins. Use the PMID (from the Publication node's xref) to populate publications/sources on real biomedical edges. No entity mapping needed.
biookf.pitfalls: Trap: treating provenance as a graph edge and trying to create a SPOKE Publication node — SPOKE has none (Publication/Study/Dataset/Agent are provenance types with NO SPOKE equivalent). Because it is 48% of all edges, naive mapping floods the target with junk. The Publication object is a title string, not a CURIE; the PMID lives in the node's xref and must be pulled from there to attribute evidence. Not negatable.

biookf.name: used_to_study
biookf.definition: New in v0.5. An investigative resource (method/study/dataset/device/research-model) is used to study, model, probe, or make tractable the object entity under investigation. Direction resource->entity-studied. Domain MethodOrProcedure/Study/Dataset/Device/Organism/CellType/MaterialSample; range Disease/Phenotype/BiologicalPathway/BiologicalFunction/Gene/Variant/Molecule. Forward-only, non-negatable. Carves the 'method/model -> what it studies' axis off of associated_with.
biookf.identifier_pattern: Endpoint names. Benchmark: MethodOrProcedure->Disease (5; e.g. an assay/procedure used to study a disease), Organism->Disease (3; a model organism/animal model used to study a disease), Dataset->Gene (1), Molecule->Disease (1), Organism->BiologicalFunction (1). Rare.
xref_namespaces: endpoint namespaces: MethodOrProcedure=SNOMEDCT/OBI/EDAM/NCIT, Organism=NCBITaxon, Disease=MONDO/MESH, Dataset=none
spoke_targets: NO direct SPOKE reltype — SPOKE lacks a 'resource used_to_study entity' edge
nearest SPOKE modeling: an Organism/model-line associated with a Disease, or a Compound used as a research tool, but these are weak/lossy analogs
biookf.mapping_strategy: Waterfall: (1) The predicate has NO clean SPOKE equivalent, so most used_to_study edges are BioOKF-only or drop. (2) Where the SUBJECT is itself a SPOKE-representable entity (Molecule->Disease, Organism->Disease), an LLM may re-route to a supported SPOKE association ONLY if the source genuinely means an entity-level relation rather than a methodological one — usually it does not. (3) Domain nodes that are provenance/method resources (Study, Dataset, MethodOrProcedure) have no SPOKE label -> drop. Given 11 edges, adjudicate each individually.
biookf.pitfalls: Meaning is methodological (resource->subject-of-study), NOT a biological association — must not be collapsed into associated_with/treats in SPOKE. Domain is heavily provenance/method types (MethodOrProcedure, Study, Dataset) that have NO SPOKE node, so the edge frequently has no anchorable subject. Per TB-3 keep the tangible model (Organism/MaterialSample) separate from the ACT of using it (MethodOrProcedure). Direction is resource->entity. Not negatable. No xrefs.

biookf.name: measures
biookf.definition: Subject ascertains the value of, or is diagnostic for, the object (includes diagnoses). Domain MethodOrProcedure/BiomedicalMeasure/Molecule; range Disease/Phenotype/Molecule. Maps to UMLS measures/diagnoses; carries sensitivity/specificity/auc/unit. Forward-only, non-negatable.
biookf.identifier_pattern: Endpoint names. Benchmark usage is noisy: Gene->Disease (6) and Gene->BiologicalFunction (4) dominate (Gene is off-domain — measures expects a MethodOrProcedure/BiomedicalMeasure subject), then the correct BiomedicalMeasure->Disease (3), MethodOrProcedure->Phenotype (3), BiomedicalMeasure->Gene/Phenotype (2), MethodOrProcedure->Disease (1), Molecule->BiologicalFunction (1).
xref_namespaces: endpoint namespaces: BiomedicalMeasure=LOINC/OBA/EFO/NCIT, MethodOrProcedure=SNOMEDCT/CPT/OBI, Disease=MONDO/MESH, Phenotype=HP/MEDDRA
spoke_targets: NO first-class SPOKE 'measures' reltype; BiomedicalMeasure/lab-test as a SPOKE node type is limited
a diagnostic Compound/assay -> Disease could approximate SPOKE MEASURES/biomarker edges, but SPOKE mostly lacks BiomedicalMeasure as a node label
biookf.mapping_strategy: Waterfall: (1) The canonical BiomedicalMeasure->Disease/Phenotype form maps only if SPOKE models the measure/biomarker (often it does not -> BioOKF-only). (2) The benchmark's Gene->Disease/BiologicalFunction 'measures' edges are MISTYPED (a gene does not measure) and must be re-routed by LLM to associated_with / biomarker-for, not forced onto measures. (3) MethodOrProcedure->Phenotype (diagnostic assay) has no SPOKE target unless the method resolves. Low volume -> hand-adjudicate.
biookf.pitfalls: Domain violation is rampant here: >45% of benchmark measures edges have a Gene subject, which is off-domain (measures wants MethodOrProcedure/BiomedicalMeasure/Molecule) — do not trust the predicate, re-classify. BiomedicalMeasure vs Disease vs Phenotype trio collision: the SUBJECT measure and the OBJECT condition must not be swapped, and a raw value is edge data not a node. SPOKE largely lacks a BiomedicalMeasure node, so many edges are unmappable. Not negatable. No xrefs.

biookf.name: interacts_with
biookf.definition: Physical or functional interaction between two entities of the same kind (PPI, gene-gene, drug-drug, host-pathogen). Symmetric, undirected. SCHEMA/SPEC 6.C #8; domain/range Molecule.Gene.Organism <-> same. Maps to UMLS interacts_with, Hetionet GiG, PubTator3 interact.
biookf.identifier_pattern: Both endpoints are human-readable labels (e.g. Gene symbol -> Gene symbol). All 24 edges carry symmetric:true. Observed domain/range: 17 Gene->Gene, 4 Molecule->Gene, 2 Molecule->Molecule, 1 Gene->CellType. No xrefs on either endpoint (only Publications carry PMIDs).
xref_namespaces: (predicate has no xref; endpoint types use HGNC/NCBIGene/ENSEMBL for Gene, UniProtKB/CHEBI/DRUGBANK for Molecule, NCBITaxon for Organism per SCHEMA)
biookf.mapping_strategy: Two-step waterfall: first resolve each endpoint node to a SPOKE node (type match + exact label/synonym match; else LLM/semantic), THEN choose the SPOKE reltype by the resolved endpoint labels (Gene->Gene => GiG; Protein->Protein => PiP; Compound->Compound). Symmetric, so emit once and let SPOKE's symmetry handle the inverse. Only auto-map when BOTH endpoints resolve exactly; defer to LLM when either endpoint is ambiguous.
biookf.pitfalls: Symmetric: do not double-emit. Gene-vs-Protein routing collision: a BioOKF Gene endpoint may need to become a SPOKE Protein (or Gene) depending on whether the interaction is transcript/protein-level; benchmark Molecule(subtype protein) and Gene both surface here. Distinct from binds (directed, affinity-bearing) - do not conflate. not_interacts_with must only be emitted as a contradiction when a positive interacts edge exists in SPOKE.

biookf.name: binds
biookf.definition: Direct binding with measurable affinity (drug-target, TF-DNA, antibody-antigen). Directed, NOT symmetric. SCHEMA/SPEC 6.C #9; domain Molecule -> range Molecule.Gene.Variant.SequenceFeature (TF->TFBS/enhancer). Carries Kd/Ki/IC50 via effect_metric. Maps to Biolink binds, Hetionet CbG.
biookf.identifier_pattern: Directed (symmetric:false on all 73). Human-readable labels. Observed: 31 Molecule->Gene, 30 Gene->Gene, 11 Gene->Molecule, 1 Molecule->Molecule. The Gene->Gene / Gene->Molecule cases are text-mining artifacts where the physical binder is really a protein product of that Gene. No affinity xrefs; no endpoint xrefs.
biookf.mapping_strategy: Resolve subject (usually a drug/compound or protein) and object; auto-map when subject label resolves to a SPOKE Compound/Protein and object to Gene/Protein. Direction is preserved (drug/TF -> target). When benchmark records Gene->Gene binding, LLM must decide whether to route through the Protein layer (Gene encodes Protein, Protein binds Protein). Defer affinity: benchmark has no Kd/IC50 to carry.
biookf.pitfalls: Directional (not symmetric) unlike interacts_with. Gene-as-binder collision: benchmark frequently names the Gene when the real binder is its Protein - LLM/semantic step must lift to Protein for a faithful SPOKE CbG/PiP edge. Distinct from regulates (functional up/down) and interacts_with (undirected). not_binds (1 edge, Variant->Gene) may only contradict an existing positive SPOKE bind.

biookf.name: regulates
biookf.definition: Subject increases/decreases activity, abundance, or expression of object (signed). Directed. SCHEMA/SPEC 6.C #10; domain Molecule.Gene.Variant.SequenceFeature -> range Molecule.Gene.BiologicalPathway.BiologicalFunction. direction (increased/decreased/unspecified) is REQUIRED; aspect (activity/abundance/expression/localization) optional. Maps to Biolink affects+direction, SemMedDB INHIBITS/STIMULATES, SPOKE up/down-regulates.
biookf.identifier_pattern: Directed. Second most common predicate. Human-readable labels. Observed: 181 Gene->Gene, 157 Molecule->Gene, 82 Gene->BiologicalFunction, 36 Molecule->Molecule, 24 Variant->Gene, 16 Molecule->BiologicalFunction. CRITICAL benchmark quirk: direction attribute is <none> on all 605 edges despite SPEC requiring it - polarity/sign is lost in this text-mining export.
xref_namespaces: (endpoints: Gene HGNC/NCBIGene; Molecule CHEBI/DRUGBANK; BiologicalFunction GO-MF)
biookf.mapping_strategy: Resolve endpoints, then pick SPOKE up- vs down-regulation reltype BY DIRECTION. Because benchmark direction is absent, cannot auto-assign polarity - must default to an unsigned/regulates edge or defer to LLM to re-read the source phrase (SPEC folds up-vs-down into the same predicate + direction attribute). Auto-map the endpoints; ALWAYS defer polarity resolution.
biookf.pitfalls: Missing direction attribute in this benchmark = cannot faithfully split into SPOKE up/down reltypes; a mapper that assumes a default sign will corrupt polarity. Molecule->Molecule vs Molecule->Gene routing decides Compound-Gene vs Compound-Compound target. Gene endpoints may need Protein lifting. not_regulates (22 edges) only contradicts an existing positive regulates in SPOKE - and with direction absent, contradiction detection is coarse.

biookf.name: catalyzes
biookf.definition: An enzyme/complex catalyzes a reaction (substrate -> product). Directed. SCHEMA/SPEC 6.C #11; domain Molecule -> range BiologicalPathway(reaction). Maps to UMLS produces, GO/Rhea.
biookf.identifier_pattern: Directed. Human-readable labels. Observed: 15 Gene->Molecule, 3 Gene->BiologicalFunction, 1 Gene->BiologicalPathway. Note: SPEC domain is Molecule (enzyme protein) but the benchmark authors the enzyme as a Gene 19/19 times (Gene stands in for its protein product); target is often a product Molecule rather than a Reaction node.
biookf.mapping_strategy: Resolve the enzyme (lift Gene->Protein for SPOKE), then target. SPOKE typically ties catalysis to Reaction/EC nodes; when the benchmark object is a product Molecule (Gene->Molecule), LLM must reconstruct the Reaction/EC linkage. Rarely auto-mappable end-to-end; defer to semantic step for the reaction/EC target.
biookf.pitfalls: Enzyme-as-Gene collision (must lift to Protein). Object mismatch: benchmark Gene->Molecule (product) does not match SPEC's Molecule->Reaction shape, so a direct reltype match fails; needs LLM to map to Reaction/EC. Not negatable (no not_catalyzes - structural). Distinct from converts_to (the substrate->product transformation itself, no enzyme subject).

biookf.name: converts_to
biookf.definition: Subject is chemically transformed / metabolized into object. Directed. SCHEMA/SPEC 6.C #12; domain Molecule -> range Molecule. Maps to SemMedDB CONVERTS_TO, PubTator3 convert.
biookf.identifier_pattern: Directed. Clean shape: 11/11 Molecule->Molecule (the only predicate that is perfectly on-schema here). Human-readable compound/metabolite labels (e.g. parent drug -> metabolite). No CHEBI/PUBCHEM xrefs.
biookf.mapping_strategy: Resolve both Molecule endpoints to SPOKE Compound by label/synonym; auto-map when both resolve exactly. Direction (parent -> metabolite) is preserved. SPOKE may lack a first-class converts reltype - defer to LLM to choose the closest metabolic/derivation reltype or a Reaction node.
biookf.pitfalls: SPOKE has no clean converts_to reltype in the core Compound-Compound model, so the target reltype is uncertain even when endpoints resolve. Endpoints are both Molecule so no Gene/Protein routing ambiguity. Not negatable. Do not confuse with derives_from (material/data lineage) or catalyzes (enzyme-mediated).

biookf.name: participates_in
biookf.definition: Subject takes part in / enables / is input-output of a pathway, process, or function. Directed. SCHEMA/SPEC 6.C #13; domain Gene.Molecule.Organism -> range BiologicalPathway.BiologicalFunction. Maps to Biolink participates_in/enables, Hetionet GpBP/GpPW, SemMedDB PROCESS_OF.
biookf.identifier_pattern: Directed. Human-readable labels. Observed: 17 Gene->BiologicalFunction, 14 Gene->BiologicalPathway, 2 MolecularClass->BiologicalFunction, 1 Molecule->BiologicalPathway. Subject dominated by Gene (protein product participating).
biookf.mapping_strategy: Resolve subject (Gene/Protein) and object; route to SPOKE by object type: BiologicalPathway->Pathway/BiologicalProcess, BiologicalFunction->MolecularFunction. Auto-map when the pathway/function label matches a SPOKE Pathway/BP/MF node exactly; defer to LLM otherwise (GO/Reactome names rarely match free-text labels verbatim without xrefs).
biookf.pitfalls: BiologicalPathway vs BiologicalFunction split maps to SPOKE Pathway/BiologicalProcess vs MolecularFunction - misrouting collapses the process/activity distinction. Absent GO/Reactome xrefs make pathway node resolution the hard part - almost always needs semantic matching. Not negatable. Distinct from regulates (signed control) and catalyzes (enzymatic).

biookf.name: causes
biookf.definition: Subject brings about / induces / drives object (etiology; incl. pathogen->disease, somatic driver, drug->adverse-event with object=Phenotype). Directed. SCHEMA/SPEC 6.D #14; domain any agent -> range Disease.Phenotype.BiologicalPathway. Maps to UMLS causes, SemMedDB CAUSES, Hetionet CcSE.
biookf.identifier_pattern: Directed. Third most common. Human-readable labels. Observed: 128 Molecule->Phenotype (drug adverse events), 105 Molecule->Disease, 96 Variant->Disease, 64 Gene->Disease, 17 Gene->Phenotype, 9 Gene->BiologicalFunction. Very broad subject domain as SPEC specifies.
xref_namespaces: (Molecule CHEBI/DRUGBANK; Variant DBSNP/CLINVAR/HGVS; Gene HGNC; Disease MONDO/DOID/MESH; Phenotype HP/MEDDRA)
biookf.mapping_strategy: Resolve subject+object then route by types: Molecule->Phenotype(side_effect) => SPOKE Compound-SideEffect (CcSE); Variant/Gene->Disease => causal disease edges. Auto-map when both resolve exactly; the strong signal is drug->adverse-event. Defer to LLM to distinguish a SideEffect target from a Symptom/Phenotype target since benchmark Phenotype subtype is uniformly general.
biookf.pitfalls: Object-type routing collision: benchmark Phenotype subtype is 100% general, so distinguishing a drug SideEffect (SPOKE SideEffect) from a disease Symptom (SPOKE Symptom) requires LLM adjudication. causes (mechanistic/etiologic) MUST be kept distinct from associated_with (statistical) and predisposes_to (risk) - the benchmark separates them and a mapper must not merge. not_causes (12 edges) only contradicts a positive causal SPOKE edge.

biookf.name: predisposes_to
biookf.definition: Subject increases the risk/likelihood of object without being sufficient cause (the epidemiology risk-factor edge; broad domain, risk factor = role). Directed. SCHEMA/SPEC 6.D #15; domain Variant.Gene.Molecule.Exposure.SocialFactor.Food.Disease.BiomedicalMeasure.Phenotype -> range Disease.Phenotype.BiomedicalMeasure. Carries odds_ratio/hazard_ratio/relative_risk. Maps to UMLS/SemMedDB PREDISPOSES.
biookf.identifier_pattern: Directed. Human-readable labels. Observed: 56 Variant->Disease, 45 Gene->Disease, 6 Disease->Disease, 6 Molecule->Disease, 4 Exposure->Disease, 4 Gene->Phenotype. Genetic-risk dominated (Variant/Gene -> Disease). Effect-size attributes largely absent in this export.
xref_namespaces: (Variant DBSNP/CLINVAR; Gene HGNC; Disease MONDO/MESH; Exposure ECTO/ExO)
biookf.mapping_strategy: Resolve subject+object; route Variant->Disease and Gene->Disease to SPOKE genetic-risk/association reltypes. Auto-map endpoints by label/synonym. Preserve risk semantics distinct from causes. LLM decides whether SPOKE's target is a dedicated predisposition/risk reltype or its general Gene/Variant-Disease association edge (SPOKE often lacks a separate predispose reltype).
biookf.pitfalls: Semantic collision with both causes (stronger, etiologic) and associated_with (weaker, non-causal) - benchmark keeps three separate predicates that SPOKE may collapse into one Gene/Variant-Disease association; a mapper must decide the collapse consciously, not accidentally. Risk factor is a ROLE (any subject type) not a node type. not_predisposes_to (10 edges: Variant/Gene->Disease) only contradicts a positive predisposes edge.

biookf.name: treats
biookf.definition: Subject (drug/procedure/device/intervention) cures, manages, ameliorates, or palliates object condition. Directed. SCHEMA/SPEC 6.D #16; domain Molecule.MethodOrProcedure.Device -> range Disease.Phenotype. Carries clinical_phase, effect_metric. Maps to UMLS/SemMedDB TREATS, Hetionet CtD.
biookf.identifier_pattern: Directed. Human-readable labels. Observed: 103 Molecule->Disease (drug->disease, the canonical CtD), 23 Molecule->Phenotype, 7 MethodOrProcedure->Disease, 6 Gene->Disease (text-mining slip - a Gene should not be a treatment subject), 2 Disease->Phenotype, 2 Exposure->Disease. Drug->disease dominant.
xref_namespaces: (Molecule DRUGBANK/CHEBI/RXNORM/CHEMBL; MethodOrProcedure SNOMEDCT/CPT; Disease MONDO/MESH; Phenotype HP)
spoke_targets: MethodOrProcedure (no direct SPOKE label; nearest PharmacologicClass/procedure context)
biookf.mapping_strategy: Strongest auto-map candidate: Molecule->Disease with an exact drug-label/synonym match to a SPOKE Compound and disease-label match to a SPOKE Disease => CtD. Auto-map when both endpoints resolve exactly; defer domain-violating rows (Gene->Disease as treats) to LLM which should likely re-route or drop them.
biookf.pitfalls: Domain violations in benchmark (Gene->Disease treats, 6 rows) are text-mining errors - a faithful mapper must not emit a Compound-treats edge from a Gene; flag/repair. MethodOrProcedure and Device subjects have imperfect SPOKE homes. Phenotype target may be a Symptom in SPOKE. not_treats (5 edges, all Molecule->Disease/Phenotype) is a clinically important negative that must ONLY contradict an existing positive CtD-type edge in SPOKE.

biookf.name: prevents
biookf.definition: Subject stops / hinders / reduces onset risk of object condition. Directed. SCHEMA/SPEC 6.D #17; domain Molecule.MethodOrProcedure.Exposure.Food.SocialFactor -> range Disease.Phenotype. Maps to UMLS/SemMedDB PREVENTS.
biookf.identifier_pattern: Directed. Human-readable labels. Observed: 13 Molecule->Phenotype, 11 Molecule->Disease, 5 Gene->Disease, 3 Gene->Phenotype, 2 Variant->Disease, 1 Food->Disease. Chemopreventive/protective framing.
xref_namespaces: (Molecule CHEBI/DRUGBANK; Food FooDB/FOODON; Disease MONDO; Phenotype HP)
spoke_targets: SPOKE prevention or negative-risk reltype (often none - closest is a protective association)
biookf.mapping_strategy: Resolve endpoints; Molecule->Disease/Phenotype protective edges are the auto-map core. SPOKE frequently lacks a dedicated prevents reltype, so LLM must map to the closest protective/negative-risk edge or annotate direction. Auto-map endpoint nodes; defer reltype selection.
biookf.pitfalls: prevents is the polar opposite of causes/predisposes for the same subject-object - loading it as a generic association would erase the protective polarity. Gene/Variant subjects (protective alleles) may need lifting. SPOKE has weak native support for prevention. not_prevents (5 edges) only contradicts a positive prevents edge; do not confuse the negative of prevents with the positive of causes.

biookf.name: contraindicated_in
biookf.definition: Subject (drug/procedure) must not be used in object condition/context. Directed. SCHEMA/SPEC 6.D #18; domain Molecule.MethodOrProcedure -> range Disease.Phenotype.Organism. Maps to Biolink contraindicated_in, SPOKE CcD.
biookf.identifier_pattern: Directed. Rare (only 2 edges). Both Molecule->Disease. Human-readable drug/disease labels. No xrefs.
biookf.mapping_strategy: Direct type+label waterfall: Molecule->Disease resolving to Compound and Disease maps cleanly to SPOKE's CcD contraindication reltype. Auto-map when both endpoints resolve exactly (small volume, high precision). This is one of the cleaner clinical predicates to map.
biookf.pitfalls: This is NOT a negation of treats - contraindicated_in is a distinct positive clinical assertion with its own SPOKE reltype (CcD), and must never be collapsed into not_treats. Not itself negatable (no not_contraindicated_in in the 11). Very low volume so any mapping error is proportionally visible. Organism-context objects (per SPEC) do not appear in benchmark.

biookf.name: affects_response_to
biookf.definition: Subject (gene/variant/biomarker) modulates response, sensitivity, resistance, or metabolism of object drug (pharmacogenomics). Directed. SCHEMA/SPEC 6.D #19; domain Gene.Variant.BiomedicalMeasure -> range Molecule. response_direction attribute expected. Maps to Biolink affects_response_to, SPOKE pharmacogenomic edges.
biookf.identifier_pattern: Directed. Human-readable labels. Observed: 34 Molecule->Molecule (drug-drug response modulation, off the SPEC Gene/Variant domain), 7 Gene->Molecule (canonical PGx), 5 Variant->Molecule, 4 Molecule->Phenotype, 2 Disease->Molecule, 2 Molecule->Anatomy. Benchmark domain is looser than SPEC (dominated by Molecule subject).
spoke_targets: Compound-Compound drug-response interaction (for the Molecule->Molecule cases)
biookf.mapping_strategy: Canonical Gene/Variant->Molecule rows map to SPOKE pharmacogenomic reltypes after endpoint resolution. The dominant Molecule->Molecule rows are really drug-drug response modulation and should be adjudicated by LLM (possibly interacts/associated). Auto-map only the on-schema Gene/Variant->Molecule subset; defer the rest.
biookf.pitfalls: Benchmark domain drift: 34/59 are Molecule->Molecule, outside SPEC's Gene/Variant/BiomedicalMeasure domain - a naive PGx mapper would mislabel drug-drug modulation as pharmacogenomic. response_direction (sensitize vs resist) is absent in export, losing polarity. not_affects_response_to (14 edges, mostly Molecule->Molecule) only contradicts a positive response edge.

biookf.name: has_phenotype
biookf.definition: Subject (disease/organism/genotype) presents / manifests object phenotype, sign, or symptom (disease-vs-symptom is this edge, not a type). Directed. SCHEMA/SPEC 6.D #20; domain Disease.Organism.Variant -> range Phenotype. Carries frequency, onset, severity. Maps to Biolink has_phenotype, SemMedDB MANIFESTATION_OF, Hetionet DpS.
biookf.identifier_pattern: Directed. Human-readable labels. Observed: 91 Disease->Phenotype (the canonical DpS), 4 Variant->Phenotype, 1 CellType->Phenotype, 1 Gene->Phenotype. Overwhelmingly Disease->Phenotype.
biookf.mapping_strategy: Strong auto-map: Disease->Phenotype resolving to SPOKE Disease and SPOKE Symptom maps to DpS. Auto-map when both endpoints resolve by label/synonym; SPOKE's phenotype endpoint is typically Symptom. Defer only when the Phenotype could instead be a Disease (comorbidity) or a BiomedicalMeasure.
biookf.pitfalls: The tricky-trio collision: benchmark Phenotype subtype is 100% general, so the object could semantically be a SPOKE Symptom, a Disease, or a BiomedicalMeasure - LLM must place it. SPEC insists disease-vs-symptom is THIS EDGE not a type, so do not spawn duplicate nodes. not_has_phenotype (1 edge, Disease->Phenotype) only contradicts a positive DpS edge in SPOKE.

biookf.name: associated_with
biookf.definition: A statistical/observed/co-occurrence association, non-causal, non-mechanistic (GWAS, eQTL, correlation, comorbidity, literature co-occurrence). The quantitative umbrella edge. SYMMETRIC. SCHEMA/SPEC 6.E #22; domain any <-> any. Carries the full statistical bundle. Maps to UMLS associated_with/co-occurs_with, SemMedDB ASSOCIATED_WITH, Hetionet DaG/GcG.
biookf.identifier_pattern: Symmetric (symmetric:true on all 383). Fourth most common. Human-readable labels. Observed: 147 Gene->Disease (DaG), 56 Variant->Disease, 32 Variant->Phenotype, 21 Disease->Disease (comorbidity), 21 Gene->Phenotype, 16 Molecule->Disease. Very broad any<->any as SPEC specifies.
xref_namespaces: (all endpoint namespaces apply: HGNC, DBSNP, MONDO, HP, CHEBI, etc.)
spoke_targets: many SPOKE association reltypes chosen by endpoint pair
biookf.mapping_strategy: The umbrella edge: after resolving endpoints, the SPOKE reltype is chosen ENTIRELY by the endpoint-type pair (Gene+Disease=>DaG, Gene+Gene=>GcG, Disease+Disease=>comorbidity, etc.). Auto-map endpoints by label/synonym; then rule-route by type pair. Symmetric so emit once. Defer to LLM when endpoints resolve to an unusual pair with no obvious SPOKE association reltype.
biookf.pitfalls: It is the catch-all - do NOT upgrade an associated_with to causes/predisposes/regulates just because SPOKE has a stronger edge; the benchmark deliberately reserves associated_with for non-causal findings. Symmetric: avoid double-emission. Endpoint-pair explosion means one BioOKF predicate fans out to many SPOKE reltypes. not_associated_with (85 edges - the largest negative class) must only contradict an existing positive association.

biookf.name: not_interacts_with
biookf.definition: Canonical negation of interacts_with: a source-stated tested-and-refuted physical/functional interaction. Inherits interacts_with domain/range and SYMMETRY. SCHEMA 6.F / SPEC 6.F. One of the 11 negatable effect predicates.
biookf.identifier_pattern: Symmetric (inherits). 2 edges: 1 Molecule->Molecule, 1 Variant->Gene. Human-readable labels. Represents an explicit no-interaction finding in text.
spoke_targets: (no positive SPOKE edge; used to suppress/contradict a GiG/PiP/interaction edge)
biookf.mapping_strategy: Do NOT create a positive SPOKE edge. Resolve endpoints, then check whether SPOKE (or the accumulating BioOKF graph) asserts a positive interacts edge for the same pair; only then record a contradiction/negative annotation. If no positive edge exists, open-world semantics mean it is a no-op. Never auto-emit as an interaction.
biookf.pitfalls: Polarity trap: must never be loaded as a positive interaction. Symmetric like its base, so check both orderings. Only meaningful against an existing positive edge - absence already covers negation. Extremely low volume.

biookf.name: not_binds
biookf.definition: Canonical negation of binds: a source-stated refuted direct binding. Inherits binds domain/range and directionality (NOT symmetric). SCHEMA 6.F / SPEC 6.F. One of the 11 negatable predicates.
biookf.identifier_pattern: Directed (inherits binds, not symmetric). 1 edge: Variant->Gene. Human-readable labels. An explicit no-binding finding.
spoke_targets: (no positive SPOKE edge; contradicts a CbG/binds edge)
biookf.mapping_strategy: Resolve endpoints; suppress or flag a contradiction ONLY if a positive binds/CbG edge exists for the same directed pair. Otherwise no-op under open-world semantics. Never emit as a positive bind.
biookf.pitfalls: Directional (respect subject->object). Polarity trap - do not create a binding. The single benchmark row (Variant->Gene) also reflects the Gene-as-target text-mining pattern. Meaningful only against an existing positive.

biookf.name: not_regulates
biookf.definition: Canonical negation of regulates: a source-stated refuted regulatory effect. Inherits regulates domain/range and directionality. SCHEMA 6.F / SPEC 6.F. One of the 11 negatable predicates.
biookf.identifier_pattern: Directed. 22 edges. Observed: 8 Gene->BiologicalFunction, 6 Molecule->Gene, 4 Gene->Gene, 2 Gene->BiologicalPathway, 1 CellType->Gene, 1 Gene->Disease. Human-readable labels; like base regulates the direction attribute is absent.
xref_namespaces: (inherits regulates endpoint namespaces: Gene HGNC, Molecule CHEBI, BiologicalFunction GO-MF)
spoke_targets: (no positive edge; contradicts a regulates / up-down-regulation SPOKE edge)
biookf.mapping_strategy: Resolve endpoints; record a contradiction only against an existing positive regulates edge for the same pair. Because base direction is absent, contradiction matching is polarity-blind (any positive regulates on the pair). Never emit a positive regulation.
biookf.pitfalls: Polarity trap plus lost direction (cannot say not-up vs not-down). Directional. Gene endpoints may need Protein lifting to match SPOKE. Meaningful only against an existing positive regulates.

biookf.name: not_causes
biookf.definition: Canonical negation of causes: a source-stated refuted etiologic/causal claim. Inherits causes broad domain and direction. SCHEMA 6.F / SPEC 6.F. One of the 11 negatable predicates.
biookf.identifier_pattern: Directed. 12 edges. Observed: 5 Molecule->Phenotype, 3 Gene->Disease, 1 Disease->Phenotype, 1 Gene->Phenotype, 1 Molecule->Disease, 1 Variant->Disease. Human-readable labels. Explicit no-causation findings (e.g. drug does not cause adverse event).
spoke_targets: (no positive edge; contradicts a causes / CcSE / causal-disease SPOKE edge)
biookf.mapping_strategy: Resolve endpoints; contradict an existing positive causal edge only. Especially relevant for refuted drug->side-effect (Molecule->Phenotype). Never emit a positive causal edge.
biookf.pitfalls: Polarity trap. Must not be confused with prevents (a positive protective claim) - not_causes only says causation was tested and not found, it does not assert prevention. Directional. Meaningful only against an existing positive causes.

biookf.name: not_predisposes_to
biookf.definition: Canonical negation of predisposes_to: a source-stated refuted risk/predisposition (no association / not a risk factor). Inherits predisposes_to broad domain and direction. SCHEMA 6.F / SPEC 6.F.
biookf.identifier_pattern: Directed. 10 edges: 6 Variant->Disease, 4 Gene->Disease. Human-readable labels. Negative genetic-risk findings (e.g. variant not associated with increased risk).
xref_namespaces: (inherits predisposes_to endpoint namespaces: Variant DBSNP/CLINVAR, Gene HGNC, Disease MONDO)
spoke_targets: (no positive edge; contradicts a predisposes / genetic-risk SPOKE association)
biookf.mapping_strategy: Resolve Variant/Gene and Disease endpoints; contradict an existing positive risk edge only. Common in GWAS null results. Never emit a positive risk edge.
biookf.pitfalls: Polarity trap. Overlaps semantically with not_associated_with (many GWAS nulls are authored either way) - do not double-count. Directional. Meaningful only against an existing positive predisposes edge.

biookf.name: not_treats
biookf.definition: Canonical negation of treats: a source-stated refuted therapeutic effect (drug did not treat / no efficacy). Inherits treats domain/range and direction. SCHEMA 6.F / SPEC 6.F.
biookf.identifier_pattern: Directed. 5 edges: 4 Molecule->Disease, 1 Molecule->Phenotype. Human-readable drug/disease labels. Negative trial/efficacy findings.
xref_namespaces: (inherits treats endpoint namespaces: Molecule DRUGBANK/RXNORM, Disease MONDO)
spoke_targets: (no positive edge; contradicts a CtD / Compound-treats-Disease edge)
biookf.mapping_strategy: Resolve drug and disease endpoints; contradict/suppress an existing positive CtD edge only. Clinically important negative (failed therapy). Never emit a positive treatment edge.
biookf.pitfalls: Polarity trap - loading as a positive CtD would invert a failed-therapy finding into a claimed treatment. Distinct from contraindicated_in (a positive do-not-use claim) - do not merge. Directional. Meaningful only against an existing positive treats.

biookf.name: not_prevents
biookf.definition: Canonical negation of prevents: a source-stated refuted preventive effect (no protection observed). Inherits prevents domain/range and direction. SCHEMA 6.F / SPEC 6.F.
biookf.identifier_pattern: Directed. 5 edges: 3 Molecule->Disease, 2 Molecule->Phenotype. Human-readable labels. Negative prevention findings (e.g. supplement did not reduce onset).
xref_namespaces: (inherits prevents endpoint namespaces: Molecule CHEBI/DRUGBANK, Disease MONDO)
spoke_targets: (no positive edge; contradicts a prevents / protective SPOKE edge)
biookf.mapping_strategy: Resolve endpoints; contradict an existing positive prevents/protective edge only. Never emit a positive prevention edge; and never re-express as causes.
biookf.pitfalls: Polarity trap. not_prevents (no protection) is NOT the same as causes/predisposes (harm) - keep them separate. Directional. SPOKE rarely has a positive prevents edge to contradict, so most rows are open-world no-ops. Meaningful only against an existing positive prevents.

biookf.name: not_affects_response_to
biookf.definition: Canonical negation of affects_response_to: a source-stated refuted pharmacogenomic/response modulation (no effect on drug response). Inherits affects_response_to domain/range and direction. SCHEMA 6.F / SPEC 6.F.
biookf.identifier_pattern: Directed. 14 edges: 13 Molecule->Molecule, 1 Variant->Molecule. Human-readable labels. Mostly refuted drug-drug response modulation (mirrors base predicate's Molecule->Molecule drift).
xref_namespaces: (inherits affects_response_to endpoint namespaces: Gene HGNC, Variant DBSNP, Molecule DRUGBANK)
spoke_targets: (no positive edge; contradicts a PGx / response SPOKE edge)
biookf.mapping_strategy: Resolve endpoints; contradict an existing positive response edge only. The dominant Molecule->Molecule rows are refuted drug-drug response claims and, like the positive base, sit outside SPEC's Gene/Variant PGx domain - defer to LLM. Never emit a positive response edge.
biookf.pitfalls: Polarity trap plus the same domain drift as the base (13/14 Molecule->Molecule, off the canonical PGx Gene/Variant domain). response_direction absent. Directional. Meaningful only against an existing positive affects_response_to.

biookf.name: not_has_phenotype
biookf.definition: Canonical negation of has_phenotype: a source-stated refuted manifestation (condition does not present the phenotype). Inherits has_phenotype domain/range and direction. SCHEMA 6.F / SPEC 6.F.
biookf.identifier_pattern: Directed. 1 edge: Disease->Phenotype. Human-readable labels. An explicit absent-manifestation finding.
xref_namespaces: (inherits has_phenotype endpoint namespaces: Disease MONDO/MESH, Phenotype HP/MEDDRA)
spoke_targets: (no positive edge; contradicts a DpS / Disease-presents-Symptom edge)
biookf.mapping_strategy: Resolve Disease and Phenotype endpoints; contradict an existing positive DpS edge only. Never emit a positive manifestation. Extremely low volume.
biookf.pitfalls: Polarity trap. Same tricky-trio ambiguity as base has_phenotype for the object (Symptom vs Disease vs Measure). Directional. Meaningful only against an existing positive has_phenotype.

biookf.name: not_associated_with
biookf.definition: Canonical negation of associated_with: a source-stated refuted statistical association (explicit no association / null result). Inherits associated_with any<->any domain/range and SYMMETRY. SCHEMA 6.F / SPEC 6.F. The largest negative class in the benchmark.
biookf.identifier_pattern: Symmetric (inherits). 85 edges - by far the most common not_* predicate. Observed: 34 Gene->Disease, 22 Variant->Disease, 4 Variant->Phenotype, 3 Gene->Phenotype, 3 Molecule->Phenotype, 2 Disease->Gene. Human-readable labels. Reflects the many null-result / no-association statements in the source corpus.
spoke_targets: (no positive edge; contradicts a DaG / GcG / any association SPOKE edge chosen by endpoint pair)
biookf.mapping_strategy: Resolve endpoints; the pair-type determines which positive SPOKE association it would contradict (Gene+Disease=>DaG). Record a contradiction/suppression ONLY where that positive association exists; otherwise open-world no-op. Symmetric so check both orderings. Never emit as a positive association.
biookf.pitfalls: Highest-volume polarity trap: 85 rows that must NEVER become positive DaG/association edges - a naive loader that drops the not_ prefix would inject 85 false associations. Symmetric (both directions). Overlaps not_predisposes_to for genetic nulls - avoid double-counting. Meaningful only against an existing positive associated_with.

biookf.name: not_expressed_in
biookf.definition: Canonical negation of expressed_in: a source-stated refuted expression/abundance in an anatomy or cell context. Inherits expressed_in domain/range and direction. SCHEMA 6.F / SPEC 6.F. (expressed_in itself is #6, not in the primary requested list but its negation is one of the 11.)
biookf.identifier_pattern: Directed. 3 edges: 1 CellType->Gene, 1 Gene->CellType, 1 Gene->Disease. Human-readable labels. Explicit not-expressed findings; note the mixed orderings and one off-range Gene->Disease (text-mining slip).
xref_namespaces: (inherits expressed_in endpoint namespaces: Gene HGNC, Anatomy UBERON, CellType CL/CLO)
spoke_targets: (no positive edge; contradicts an EXPRESSEDIN / Anatomy-expresses-Gene edge)
biookf.mapping_strategy: Resolve Gene and Anatomy/CellType endpoints (normalizing subject/object ordering to Gene->context); contradict an existing positive expressed_in edge only. Never emit a positive expression edge.
biookf.pitfalls: Polarity trap. Endpoint ordering is inconsistent in benchmark (both Gene->CellType and CellType->Gene) - normalize to the SPEC Gene/Molecule->Anatomy/CellType direction. One row is off-range (Gene->Disease). Directional. Meaningful only against an existing positive expressed_in.
